He led a naval force of 100,000 men out from Piāoyú Jīn.
The Shuǐjīng states: "To the northeast of Qīnghé, it passes Piāoyú Yì and enters the sea."

read as *shuài*.

3rd month.

守,

—to flee to Mìyún Shān.

The Duàn clan had their capital at Língzhī,
and their residence was called the palace.
He relocated over 20,000 households of Duàn's people to the four provinces of Sī, Yōng, Yǎn, and Yù.
All scholar-officials with talent and virtue
were promoted and given positions.
Yáng Yù went to the army gate to surrender.
Hǔ reproached him, saying:
"In the past, you fled as a captive;
now you come as a scholar.
Do you recognize the Mandate of Heaven,
or is it that you have nowhere left to hide?"
Yù replied:
"I formerly served King Gōng
but could not save him.
'King Gōng' refers to Wáng Jùn.
Yù's flight to Língzhī is recorded in volume 89, Mǐndì Jiànxīng 2nd year.
Then again I failed to preserve (my lord).
Now Your Majesty's heavenly net is cast wide,
enveloping the four seas,
and the heroes of Yōu and Jì all follow like the wind.
Compared to others like me,
I have no unique shame.
The matter of life and death
is solely for Your Majesty to decide!"
Hǔ was pleased
and immediately appointed him Grand Administrator of Běipíng.
2 Summer,
4th month,
guǐchǒu.
Mùróng Huàng was appointed General-in-chief of the Expedition to the North and Governor of Yōuzhōu,
also overseeing the Inspector of Píngzhōu.
3 Chéng Lord Qī's tyranny and cruelty grew daily,
and he executed many,
confiscating their wealth, property, and women.
Because of this, many high officials felt insecure.
Hàn King Shòu had always been highly esteemed
and possessed great prestige,
and Qī, along with Jiànníng King Yuè and others, were all jealous of him.
Shòu, fearing he would not escape,
often feigned border reports whenever he was due to attend court,
excusing himself due to urgent alerts.
Shòu was garrisoned at Fúchéng at that time.
朝,
read as *cháo*.
Initially,
Gōng Zhuàng (龔壯), a reclusive scholar from Bāxī (巴西),
had his father and paternal uncle both killed by Lǐ Tè (李特).
His father and paternal uncle.
處 (chǔ),
read chāng lǚ.
He did not remove his mourning attire for many years.
Lǐ Shòu (李壽) repeatedly tried to recruit him with ritual propriety,
but Gōng Zhuàng did not respond.
However, he went to see Lǐ Shòu.
Lǐ Shòu secretly asked Gōng Zhuàng for advice on how to secure his position.
Gōng Zhuàng said:
“The people of Bā (巴) and Shǔ (蜀) were originally subjects of Jìn (晉).
If Your Excellency could raise troops to march west and take Chéngdū (成都),
and declare fealty to Jìn,
who would not eagerly step forward to fight for Your Excellency?
Since the Wèi (魏) and Jìn dynasties,
those who held the credentials of 'Jie' (節) or 'Jia Jie' (假節) and were stationed in a region
were all referred to as 'Your Excellency' (Jiéxià 節下).
為 (wéi),
read yú wěi.
Your name would be immortalized;
why merely escape today’s calamity?”
Lǐ Shòu agreed.
He secretly plotted with his Chief Clerk, Luō Héng (羅恆) of Luèyáng (略陽), and Jiě Sīmíng (解思明) of Bāxī (巴西), to attack Chéngdū.
Lǐ Qī (李期) somewhat heard of this
and frequently sent Xǔ Fú (許涪) to Lǐ Shòu’s residence
to observe his movements.
He also poisoned and killed Lǐ Shòu's adopted younger brother, Yōu (攸), the General Who Pacifies the North.
Lǐ Shòu then forged a letter from his sister's husband, Rèn Diào (任調),
claiming that Lǐ Qī intended to seize Lǐ Shòu.
He falsely stated that Lǐ Qī wanted to seize Lǐ Shòu
to incite his troops.
任 (Rèn),
pronounced rén;
same below.
He then led more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry from Fú (涪) to attack Chéngdū,
promising them the city's wealth;
he made his general Lǐ Yì (李奕) the vanguard.
Lǐ Qī did not expect his arrival
and had made no preparations.
Lǐ Shòu’s heir apparent, Lǐ Shì (李勢), who was the Colonel of the Winged Army,
opened the gates to admit them.
They thus captured Chéngdū
and encamped their troops at the palace gate.
Lǐ Qī sent a Chamberlain to console Lǐ Shòu.

Lǐ Shòu impeached Yuè (越) the King of Jiànníng (建寧), Jǐng Qiān (景騫), Tián Bāo (田褒), Yáo Huá (姚華), Xǔ Fú (許涪), and General Who Conquers the West Lǐ Xiá (李遐), General Lǐ Xī (李西) and others for harboring treachery and disrupting governance,
and had them all arrested and executed.
He allowed his troops to plunder extensively,
and order was restored only after several days.
Lǐ Shòu falsely issued an edict from Empress Dowager Rèn (任) to depose Lǐ Qī as the Duke of Qióngdū County,
and confined him in a separate palace.
Qióngdū County (邛都縣)
belonged to Yuèsuí Commandery (越嶲郡).
邛 (Qióng),
read qú róng.
In the ninth year of Xiánhé (咸和),
Lǐ Qī and Yuè (越) had assassinated their lord, Lǐ Bān (李班),
who was posthumously titled Crown Prince Lì (戾太子).
Luō Héng (羅恆), Jiě Sīmíng (解思明), Lǐ Yì (李奕) and others urged Lǐ Shòu to claim the title of General Who Guards the West, Governor of Yìzhōu (益州), and King of Chéngdū,
to declare fealty to Jìn,
and to send the Duke of Qióngdū to Jiànkāng (建康).
Rèn Diào (任調) and Commander Cài Xīng (蔡興), Chamberlain Lǐ Yàn (李豔) and others advised Lǐ Shòu to declare himself emperor.
Lǐ Shòu ordered a divination.
Turtle shells were for 'bu' (卜),
yarrow stalks for 'shi' (筮).
The result was: "Can be emperor for several years."
Rèn Diào happily said:
“Even one day would be enough, let alone several years!”
Jiě Sīmíng said:
“To be emperor for several years, how does that compare to being a marquis for a hundred generations?”
Lǐ Shòu said:
“To hear the Way in the morning,
and die in the evening, is acceptable.”
Citing Confucius' words from the Analects.
Lǐ Shòu (壽),
courtesy name Wǔkǎo (武考),
was the son of Lǐ Xiáng (李驤).
He granted a general amnesty
and changed the era name to Hànxīng (漢興).
He summoned Gōng Zhuàng (龔壯) as Grand Mentor with an "an-che shu-bo" (安車束帛) (a carriage and silks, indicating great respect);
Gōng Zhuàng swore not to serve,
and accepted none of the gifts
Lǐ Shòu offered.
Lǐ Shòu changed and established ancestral temples,
posthumously honoring his father Lǐ Xiáng (李驤) as Emperor Xiàn (獻皇帝).
His mother, Lady Zǎn (昝氏), was titled Empress Dowager,
Lady Yán (閻氏) was established as empress,
and heir apparent Lǐ Shì (李勢) as crown prince.
He further renamed the old temple as the Dàchéng Temple (大成廟).
The old temple
was for worshipping Lǐ Tè (李特) and Lǐ Xióng (李雄);
Lǐ Xióng (雄) had established the state name Chéng (成).
Lǐ Shòu (壽) changed the state name to Hàn (漢),
thus calling the temples of Lǐ Tè (特) and Lǐ Xióng (雄) the Dàchéng Temple.
Many things were changed.
He appointed Dǒng Jiǎo (董皎) as Chancellor,
Luō Héng (羅恆) as Minister of the Secretariat,
Jiě Sīmíng (解思明) as Administrator of Guǎnghàn (廣漢),
Rèn Diào (任調) as General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Liángzhōu (梁州),
Lǐ Yì (李奕) as Colonel of the Western Yi,
and his cousin Lǐ Quán (李權) as Inspector of Níngzhōu (寧州).
Dukes, ministers, provincial, and commandery officials
were all replaced by his own subordinates;
the former officials and close relatives of the Chéng (成) regime, as well as the literati from the Six Commanderies,
were all alienated and dismissed.
The literati from the Six Commanderies
were those who had entered Shǔ (蜀) with Lǐ Tè (李特) and his brothers.
Lǐ Qī (李期), the Duke of Qióngdū, sighed:
“To be the ruler of all under Heaven, and now a mere duke of a small county,
it is better to die!”
In the fifth month,
he hanged himself.
According to the Annals,
Lǐ Qī died in the third year,
aged twenty-five.
縊 (yì),
read yú cì,
also yú jì.
He was buried with the rites of a king.
4 Zhào Wáng Hǔ (趙王虎) was angry that Yàn Wáng Huàng (燕王皝) did not join the Zhào (趙) forces in attacking Duàn Liáo (段遼) and monopolized the benefits for himself.
Because Mùróng Huàng (皝) had plundered Duàn (段) clan's people and livestock
and returned north without waiting for the Zhào (趙) army to arrive.
The Grand Astrologer Zhào Lǎn (趙攬) advised:
“The Jupiter star guards the Yàn (燕) division;
the army will surely gain no merit.”
According to the Astronomical Treatise,
when the Jupiter star (歲星) waxes or wanes,
its dwelling determines the fate of nations.
If it stays long in one place,
that nation has great virtue,
and its five grains will be abundant.
It should not be attacked.
分 (fēn),
read fú wèn.
Hǔ (虎) had him whipped.
Mùróng Huàng (皝) heard of this
and tightened military preparations;
he dismissed the officials of the Six Ministers (六卿), Nàyán (納言), Chángbó (常伯), and Chángshì (常侍) of the Mounted Guard (⿱宀儿騎).
Last year, Mùróng Huàng (皝) had established the Six Ministers and other officials.
⿱宀儿 (ér),
read ér lǒng.
The people of Yàn (燕) were terrified.
Mùróng Huàng (皝) asked his Inner Historian Gāo Xǔ (高詡):
“What should we do?”
Inner Historian
refers to the Inner Historian of Yàn (燕).
“Although the Zhào (趙) army is strong,”
he replied, “it is not a cause for worry.
Just hold firm to our defenses to resist them,
and they will be able to do nothing.”
Hǔ (虎) sent envoys in all directions
to entice the common people and the Yi (夷) tribes.

Cuī Tāo (崔燾), Inner Historian of Chéngzhōu (成周) of Yàn (燕), Yóu Hóng (游泓), Magistrate of Jūjiù (居就), Cháng Bà (常霸), Magistrate of Wǔyuán (武原), Fēng Chōu (封抽), Colonel of the Eastern Yi, Hùjūn (護軍) Sòng Huàng (宋晃) and others all responded,
and a total of thirty-six cities defected.
Yóu Hóng (泓)
was the elder nephew of Yóu Suì (邃).
The displaced scholars of Jìyáng (冀陽) jointly killed their Administrator Sòng Zhú (宋燭) and surrendered to Zhào (趙).
Sòng Zhú (燭)
was the cousin of Sòng Huàng (晃).
Xiānyú Qū (鮮于屈), Inner Historian of Yíngqiū (營丘), also sent envoys to surrender to Zhào (趙).
Sūn Xīng (孫興) of Guǎngpíng (廣平), Magistrate of Wǔníng (武寧), exhorted the officials and common people to jointly apprehend Xiānyú Qū (屈),
enumerated his crimes, killed him,
and closed the city gates to defend.
The commanderies of Chéngzhōu (成周), Jìyáng (冀陽), Yíngqiū (營丘)
were all established by Mùróng Kuì (慕容廆),
see volume 89, Mǐndì (愍帝) Jiànxīng (建興) second year.
Jūjiù County (居就縣)
belonged to Liáodōng (遼東) Commandery during the Hàn (漢) and Jìn (晉) dynasties.
Wǔyuán (武原)
was probably also a county established by the Mùróng clan.
Wǔníng County (武寧縣)
was also established by the Mùróng clan,
and was under Yíngqiū Commandery.
Yóu Suì (游邃) is mentioned in volume 88, Mǐndì (愍帝) Jiànxīng (建興) first year.
The prominent local gentry Wáng Qīng (王清) and others secretly plotted to side with Zhào (趙).
Yóu Yǒng (泳) apprehended and executed them;
several hundred co-conspirators were terrified and begged for mercy,
but Yóu Yǒng (泳) released them all
and defended the city with them.
Jū Péng (鞠彭), Administrator of Lèlàng (樂浪), seeing that his entire territory had rebelled,
selected over two hundred able-bodied men from his hometown
and returned with them to Jíchéng (棘城).
Lèlàng (樂浪)
was not the ancient commandery territory of Hàn (漢), but was established by Mùróng Kuì (慕容廆),
see volume 88, Mǐndì (愍帝) Jiànxīng (建興) first year.
Judging from the Records of the Five Dynasties,
the counties of Lèlàng (樂浪), Jìyáng (冀陽), Yíngqiū (營丘) commanderies, Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮), Wǔníng (武寧) and others
should all be within the boundaries of Liǔchéng County (柳城縣) of Liáoxī Commandery (遼西郡) during the Suí (隋) dynasty.
Jū Péng (鞠彭) leading his townsmen back to Yàn (燕)
is mentioned in volume 90, Yuándì (元帝) Tàixīng (太興) second year.
樂浪 (Lèlàng),
pronounced luò láng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Zhào soldiers advanced to besiege Jíchéng.
Yàn Wáng Mùróng Huǎng wanted to flee,
but his general Mùyú Gēn remonstrated, saying:
"Zhào is strong and we are weak.
If Your Majesty takes a single step, the momentum of Zhào will be fully formed,
allowing the Zhào people to gather and subdue our populace.
The populace
refers to the people of Yàn State.
We will then be unable to resist them again.
I secretly believe that the Zhào people precisely wish Your Majesty to do so;
why fall into their trap?
If we now steadfastly defend this strong city,
our strength will be a hundredfold.
Even if they attack urgently,
we can still hold out,
observe the situation and discern changes,
then emerge to seek advantage.
This means seizing an opportunity to attack Zhào and seek advantage.
The character 'jiàn' (間)
is pronounced 'gǔ xiàn fān'.
We should not fail by fleeing.
Why give up at the first sign of trouble,
embracing the certainty of ruin?"
Huǎng then stopped,
but his fear was still evident on his face.
Xuántú Tàishǒu Liú Pèi of Héjiān said:
"Now a powerful enemy is outside,
and the hearts of the multitude are terrified.
The safety or danger of our cause
rests on one person.
At this moment, Your Majesty has no one to rely upon,
but should strengthen yourself to encourage the generals and soldiers.
You should not show weakness.
The situation is urgent;
I request to go out and attack them.
Even without a great victory,
it will be enough to reassure the multitude."
So he led several hundred 'dare-to-die' cavalry to charge the Zhào soldiers.
Wherever they went, the enemy fell before them.
They killed and captured many before returning,
whereupon morale instantly doubled.
Huǎng asked Fēng Yì for a plan,
who replied:
"Shí Hǔ's tyranny has gone too far;
both people and gods resent him.
The arrival of disaster and defeat for him,
what day could it be but soon?
Dù Yù said: 'It means it is imminent.'
The dynamics of offense and defense are different.
Although their cavalry is strong,
they cannot cause us harm.
If they halt their troops for many days,
internal discord will naturally arise.
We should simply hold fast and wait for it."
Huǎng's mind then found peace.
Someone advised Huǎng to surrender,
but Huǎng said:
"I am about to take over the world;
what do you mean by surrender?"
The Zhào soldiers, like ants, swarmed and climbed the city walls from all four sides.
This means they pressed close to the city walls and ascended,
like ants.
For more than ten days,
the Zhào soldiers could not overcome the city.
On the day Rénchén,
they retreated.
Huǎng dispatched his son Mùróng Kè to lead two thousand cavalry to pursue and attack them.
The Zhào soldiers were greatly defeated,
suffering over thirty thousand casualties.
All the Zhào armies abandoned their armor and fled in disarray.
Only the army of Campaigning General Shí Mǐn remained intact.
Mǐn's father was Shí Zhān,
a native of Nèihuáng.
Nèihuáng County
belonged to Wèijùn.
Because Chénliú had Wàihuáng,
it was given
the prefix "Nèi" (內).
Zhào Lord Shí Lè defeated Chén Wǔ
and captured Zhān,
ordering Shí Hǔ to adopt him as a son.
Mǐn was valiant and skilled in battle,
and full of strategies.
Shí Hǔ loved him
and treated him like his own grandsons.
Rǎn Mǐn began here.
Shí Lè adopted Shí Hǔ, thereby destroying his own clan.
Shí Hǔ adopted Rǎn Mǐn,
who then annihilated his entire clan.
This is perhaps the way of Heaven.
The character 'xiāo' (驍)
is pronounced 'jiān yáo fān'.
Shí Hǔ returned to Yè.
He appointed Liú Huì as Zhōngshū Lìng
and Lú Chén as Zhōngshū Shìláng.
Pú Hóng, for his accomplishments, was appointed Emissary with Imperial Credentials, Area Commander-in-Chief of All Barbarian Armies, and Grand General of the Champions,
and enfeoffed as Gōng of Xīpíng Commandery.
Shí Mǐn said to Shí Hǔ:
"Pú Hóng is heroic and outstanding,
and has the unwavering loyalty of his generals and soldiers.
All his sons possess extraordinary talent,
and he commands a strong army of fifty thousand,
encamped near the capital.
Near the capital
refers to Pú Hóng being encamped at Fāngtóu,
which is close to Yè.
This secures the state."
Shí Hǔ said:
"I am relying on his father and sons to conquer Wú and Shǔ;
why would I kill them?"
He treated them even more generously.
Shí Hǔ's inability to kill Pú Hóng
was like Fú Jiān's inability to kill Mùróng Chuí and Yáo Cháng.
Yàn Wáng Mùróng Huǎng divided his forces to suppress the rebellious cities,
and all were pacified.
He expanded his territory to Fánchéng.
The Shuǐjīng Zhù states: "From Lúlóng eastward over Qīngxíng to Fánchéng is about two hundred lí.
From Fánchéng northeast towards the old city of Pínggāng is about one hundred eighty lí.
Towards Huánglóngchéng is five hundred lí."
Fēng Chōu, Sòng Huǎng, and Yóu Hóng fled to Gāogōulí.
Huǎng rewarded Jū Péng, Mùyú Gēn, and others, and dealt with the rebels,
executing many;
Gōngcáo Liú Xiáng interceded for them,
saving many lives.
When Zhào attacked Jíchéng,
Lǐ Pǔ, the younger brother of Yàn's Right Sīmǎ Lǐ Hóng, believed that Jíchéng would surely fall,
and urged Hóng to flee the danger.
Hóng said:
"The way of Heaven is profound and distant,
and human affairs are difficult to foresee.
Let us await orders for now
and not lightly move to incur regret!"
Pǔ earnestly insisted without ceasing.
Hóng said:
"If you believe your judgment is clear and sound,
then act on it yourself.
I have received great kindness from the Mùróng clan;
it is against my principles to leave or stay.
I shall simply devote my life here."
He shed tears and bid farewell to Pǔ.
Jué (訣)
means 'to part'.
Pǔ followed the Zhào army south,
and died in the chaos.
Hóng thereby became famous for his loyalty and steadfastness.
Zhào Wáng Shí Hǔ dispatched the General Who Crosses the Liáo, Cáo Fú, to lead the troops from Qīngzhōu to garrison a sea island.
According to the Zàijì,
Shí Hǔ sent Cáo Fú across the sea to garrison Tàdùnchéng,
but he returned due to lack of water,
and then garrisoned a sea island.
He also used three hundred ships to transport three hundred thousand hú of grain to Gāogōulí,
and ordered the Colonel of Agriculture, Wáng Diǎn, to lead over ten thousand men to set up military farms along the seashore.
He also ordered Qīngzhōu to build one thousand ships
in preparation for attacking Yàn.
Shí Hǔ, incensed by the defeat at Jíchéng,
again planned to attack Yàn but ultimately failed.
The character 'sōu' (艘)
is pronounced 'sū zāo fān'.
Zhào Crown Prince Shí Xuān led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack the Xiānbēi Húmótóu in Shuòfāng,
defeating them and
beheading over forty thousand.
The eight commanderies of Jìzhōu suffered a severe locust plague.
The Zhào Sīlì requested to punish the local officials.
Zhào's capital was Yè,
and Jìzhōu was designated as the Sī Department.
[Shí Hǔ said:] "This is caused by my poor governance,
yet you want to blame the local officials?
Is this not the intention to condemn myself?
The Sīlì did not offer upright advice
and assist me where I was lacking,
but instead wished to wrongfully implicate the innocent.
You may hold your office as a commoner!"
He demoted his rank,
making him equal to commoners,
but still allowed him to retain the position of Sīlì.
The character 'dǎng' (讜)
is pronounced 'dǎng'.
Shí Hǔ sent Gōng of Xiāngchéng Shè Guī and Gōng of Shàngyōng Rì Guī to lead troops to garrison Cháng'ān.
The two Guī
were also members of the Shí clan.
They secretly plotted rebellion.
Shí Hǔ pursued Guǎng to Yè and killed him.
7 Yǐwèi
day, Sītú Dǎo was appointed TàiFù,
Grand Administrator of All Military Affairs Inside and Outside the Capital.
Xī Jiàn was appointed Tàiwèi,
and Yǔ Liàng was appointed Sīkōng.
In the sixth month,
Dǎo was appointed Chéngxiàng,
and the office of Sītú was abolished and merged into the Chéngxiàng's office.
In the Eastern Hàn dynasty, Sītú
was effectively the same office as Chéngxiàng.
Shěn Yuē said: Chéng
means "to receive" or "to serve";
xiàng
means "to assist."
At that time, Wáng Dǎo was made Chéngxiàng,
and the Sītú's mansion was abolished and merged with the Chéngxiàng's mansion.
After Dǎo died,
the Chéngxiàng office was abolished and reverted to the Sītú's mansion.
In the early Sòng dynasty, Shìzǔ appointed Nánjùn Wáng Yìxuān as Chéngxiàng,
but the Sītú's mansion remained as before.
Dǎo was by nature generous and magnanimous,
entrusting various generals such as Zhào Yìn and Jiǎ Níng.
Many of them did not adhere to the law,
which greatly troubled the high officials.
Yǔ Liàng wrote a memorial to Xī Jiàn, saying:
"Since the Emperor was eight or nine years old until adulthood,
when he is inside, he is in the hands of palace women;
when he is outside, he is only with military officials and commoners.
He has no one from whom to learn the pronunciation and phrasing when reading,
and has never encountered a gentleman when seeking advice.
Qín Zhèng wished to make his common people ignorant.
Qín Shǐhuáng, whose given name was Zhèng,
called the common people 'qiánshǒu,'
and burned the Odes and Documents to make them ignorant.
How much more so does he wish to make his sovereign ignorant!
When the sovereign's age is mature,
he should resume his rule over the realm.
If he does not bow down and return the administration to the sovereign,
but instead holds the honored position of a tutor—
Fǔ
means 'just now' or
'at the beginning'—
you, Duke, and this humble official both bear the heavy trust
(meaning that they received the last wishes of the late Emperor,
who entrusted them with the young orphan),
Hè
can be pronounced 'xià'—
how can we face the late Emperor in the afterlife!"
He wanted to raise an army with Jiàn to depose Dǎo,
but Jiàn did not agree.
Táo Chēng, the Nánmán Xiàowèi,
(the office of Nánmán Xiàowèi
was first established in Xiāngyáng during the early reign of Emperor Wǔ,
later governing Jiānglíng),
informed Dǎo of Liàng's plan.
Some advised Dǎo to secretly prepare for it,
but Dǎo said:
"Yuánkuī and I share weal and woe.
Such idle talk
should be stopped by the mouths of the wise.
(Meaning that the mouths of the wise
should not spread such idle talk.)
If Yuánkuī comes,
I will simply put on my kerchief and return home.
What is there to fear!"
He also wrote a letter to Chēng,
stating
that "Duke Yǔ is the Emperor's maternal uncle.
You should treat him well! "
This shows Dǎo's profound insight and magnanimity.
"Wáng Gōng often harbors thoughts beyond this world.
(Meaning Dǎo's heart always desired to resign from affairs
and live a leisurely life outside the human world.)
This must be the doing of sycophantic and wicked individuals who wish to sow discord between us."
Liàng then ceased his plans.
If Yǔ Liàng's plot
had not been resisted by Xī Jiàn from without
and stopped by Sūn Shèng from within,
it would surely have plunged the world into chaos again.
Jiàn
is pronounced 'gǔ xiàn'.
(Sūn) Chǔ's descendant.
Sūn Chǔ was a famous scholar of the early Jìn dynasty.
Yǔ Liàng, however, remotely held power in the imperial court.
Since he occupied the upstream region
and commanded a strong army,
many opportunists flocked to him.
Dǎo was inwardly unsettled by this.
Whenever the west wind blew and dust rose,
Cháng
should be written as Cháng.
Xú said:
"Yuánkuī defiles people!"
Dǎo appointed Lǐ Chōng of Jiāngxià as Chéngxiàng Yuàn.
Chōng, seeing that the customs of the time overly admired superficiality and emptiness,
wrote the "Xué Zhēn" (Admonition on Learning).
He believed that Lǎozi said,
"Abandon benevolence and discard righteousness,
and the people will return to filial piety and compassion."
He wondered, "Is it that the way of benevolence and righteousness must be abolished
before filial piety and compassion can arise?"
Perhaps it was because those who truly embodied benevolence and righteousness were few, while those who exploited benevolence and righteousness were many,
and so they sought to impose responsibility on the sages and cast off the burdens of past actions.
Most people see only the outward forms,
but few grasp the true Way.
The more diligently one pursues the traces,
the further one deviates from the origin.
Therefore, he wrote "Xué Zhēn" to dispel this delusion,
saying:
"Where fame is manifest,
the Way is forsaken;
only by diminishing what is honored
can what is neglected be exalted.
Without benevolence, things cannot grow;
without righteousness, shame cannot be dispelled.
Benevolence and righteousness are indeed indispensable;
one should only remove what harms benevolence and righteousness."
8 Lǐ Yì's cousin, Liú Shòu of Hàn, Lǐ Gān, the Grand Administrator of Guǎnghàn, informed the high officials of a plot to depose and enthrone a new ruler.
In autumn,
in the seventh month,

(This means declaring vassalage to Jìn.)
Shà
is pronounced 'sè qià.'
Great achievements were made;

the expediency of assuming the imperial title.
(This refers to Liú Shòu ascending the imperial throne.)
Famine and plague have arrived simultaneously,

Your humble servant believes that it is advisable to follow the former oath

Some commentators say that if the two commanderies attached themselves to Jìn, they would prosper.
(The two commanderies
refer to Liáng and Yì.)
When Gōngsūn Shù was in Shǔ,

Many scholars from Chǔ were honored.
Páng Tǒng, Huáng Zhōng, Dǒng Hé, Liú Bā, the Mǎ Liáng brothers, Lǚ Yì, Liáo Lì, Lǐ Yán, Yáng Yí, Wèi Yán, Jiǎng Wǎn, Fèi Yī, Dǒng Yǔn, etc.,
were all scholars from Chǔ.
Wú and Dèng
refer to Wú Hàn and Dèng Ài.
How could one distinguish between host and guest!
Commentators do not understand the basis of stable security,
and merely value fame and position,
believing that the Liú clan's governors and magistrates are now serving in provinces and commanderies.
They do not realize that in those cases, the state perished and the ruler changed.
How could that be compared to today's righteous act,
where the ruler is honored and the officials are glorified!
(Presenting the entire state to Jìn is a righteous act;
if Jìn bestows favored ranks,
then the ruler will be honored and the officials glorified.)
Fǎ Zhèng advised Liú Bèi to take Chéngdū;
Zhuàng also advised Liú Shòu to seize Lǐ Qī,
which is why commentators compare them.
Allow your humble servant to do as he sees fit;
as for glory and emoluments,
regardless of Hàn or Jìn,
your servant will not accept them.
Why should I emulate Fǎ Zhèng then!"
Liú Shòu read the memorial, felt internal shame,
and kept it secret, not proclaiming it.

Rèn,

"Wáng Dǎo, the Emperor's master and tutor, holds an eminent and revered position;

*Jiànglǐ*,

Wéi,

same below.
Hán said:

Piān,

"Perhaps this is appropriate for you gentlemen;

Afterwards, he told others:

Féng Huái,
courtesy name Zǔsī.
Guō Pú once met Hán

"Age is determined by Heaven,

If one cultivates oneself but Heaven does not grant success, that is destiny;
if one upholds the Dao but men do not recognize it, that is one's nature;

11 Yīhuái, the younger brother of Dài King Shíyìjiān, was held as a hostage in Zhào.

Jiān,

Zhì,

—and that his return was not certain,

Nàn,

Thereupon, from Huì Mò in the east,
to Pòluònà in the west,

and extending north to the desert,

The *Shuǐjīngzhù* states: "East of Ān Prefecture is the Wǔliè River,

The western source is called Xīzàng River,
flowing southwest,

The water issues from the eastern stream,
flows southwest out of the valley,
and merges with the Zhōngzàng River;
the water from the central stream flows south out of the valley
and south into the Dōngzàng River.
The Dōngzàng River then flows south and enters the Xīzàng River from the right.
Hence the stream is called Sānzàng River."
The *Wèi Shōu Dìxíngzhì* states: "In the second year of Huángxīng, Ān Prefecture was established,

Bài,

Furthermore, Shí Yù (石遇)
was a detachment,
Huán Píngběi (桓平北)
was a border general.
Huán Xuān (桓宣) was General Píngběi (平北).
Jiàng (將),

the same below.
If advantageous, they advanced;
if not, they retreated.
It was not an urgent matter.

This is what I doubt.
The strength of Sū Jùn (蘇峻) was not equal to Shí Hǔ (石虎), and the strategic advantage of the Miǎn River is not equal to that of the Great Jiāng River.
The Great Jiāng River could not repel Sū Jùn (蘇峻), yet he wishes to use the Miǎn River to repel Shí Hǔ (石虎).
This is also what I doubt.
In the past, Zǔ Shìzhì (祖士稚) was at Qiáo,

This is also what I doubt.
However, this only discusses after the **Zhēngxī** (征西) had arrived.

West of the **Miǎn** (沔),

The *Zuǒ Zhuàn* (左傳) says: Lord **Xiāng** (襄) of **Sòng** (宋) fought the **Chǔ** (楚) people at **Hóng** (泓).

**Cài Mó**'s (蔡謨) deliberation,

Later, when **Xī Jiàn** (郗鑒) recommended him to take his own place,

Upon reflection, the sword blade is sharp,
so it cannot be toyed with.
It must refer to the sword ring.
It also says: “dāo què rèn shòu yǐng” (刀卻刃授穎).
Zhèng said: Yǐng (穎),
is the ring.
Huán (鐶),
is equivalent to huán (環).
Shè (射),
read as ér yì.
Zhòng (中),
read as zhú zhòng.
When Huáng heard of Hàn’s arrival,
he was greatly pleased,
and treated him with exceeding generosity.
4 On the day of Gēngchén,
a comet appeared in Tàiwēi.
The Jìn Shū, Astronomical Treatise says: Tàiwēi is the emperor’s court,
the seat of the Five Emperors,
and the residences of the twelve feudal lords.
Bèi (孛),
read as pú nèi.
5 In the third month,
on the day of Dīngmǎo,
there was a general amnesty.
6 Hàn Rén attacked and captured Dānchuān.
The defending generals Mèng Yàn, Liú Qí, and Lǐ Qiū all died.
Five years earlier,
Mèng Yàn had surrendered Jìanníng.
Dānchuān must be within the borders of Jìanníng.
7 Dài Wáng Shíyìjiān first established his capital at Shènglègōng in Yúnzhōng.
The Shuǐ Jīng Zhù says: The Báiqú River flows out of the Yúnzhōng pass,
northwest past Chénglè Gù
[City].
The Wèi Tǔdì Jì says: Eighty li east of Yúnzhōng City is Chénglè City.
It is now the seat of Yúnzhōng Commandery,
also known as Shílú City.
The Báiqú River then flows west past the south of Wèi Yúnzhōnggōng.
The Wèi Tǔdì Jì says: Yúnzhōnggōng is forty li east of the old Yúnzhōng City.
Wèi’s Shènglè [palace]
is the Hàn Chénglè County.
The Wèi Shū says: Yīlú established Shènglè City as the northern capital.
Dù Yòu said: Yúnzhōu Yúnzhōng Commandery governs Yúnzhōng County.
Later, Wèi Dàowǔ moved his capital from Yúnzhōng to Píngchéng,
which is this place.
The northern Píngchéng of present-day Mǎyì Commandery,
which is the present commandery,
was Yúnnèi Commandery’s Héng'ān Garrison during the Suí dynasty.
Within the county boundaries are Báidēngshān, Báidēngtái, Gāoliǔchéng, and Cānhébō.
Later, Wèi’s Shènglè County was also within the present commandery boundaries.
The Chányútái is over a hundred li northwest of the present county.
8 Zhào Wáng Hǔ sent a letter to Hàn Zhǔ Shòu,
proposing to ally their armies to invade [the Jìn],
and agreeing to divide Jiāngnán in half.
Shòu was greatly pleased,
and dispatched Sànqí Chángshì Wáng Gǔ and Zhōngchángshì Wáng Guǎng as envoys to Zhào.
Sàn (散),
read as xī dǎn.
Qí (騎),
read as qí jì.
Shǐ (使),
read as shū lì.
[Zhào] did not listen.
Shòu extensively repaired boats and ships,
and stockpiled weapons and provisions.
In autumn,
the ninth month,
he appointed Shàngshūlìng Mǎ Dāng as the Grand Commander of the Six Armies,
conscripting over seventy thousand soldiers for the naval force.
A grand review was held in Chéngdū,
with drums beating and shouts filling the river.
During the Qín dynasty,
the governor of Shǔ, Lǐ Bīng, had dug two rivers through Chéngdū,
both navigable by boat.
He harbored ambitions of swallowing Jiāngnán.
Xiè Sīmíng remonstrated, saying:
“Our state is small and our army weak.
Wú and Kuàijī are dangerous and distant.
It will not be easy to conquer them.”
Shòu then ordered his close ministers to extensively discuss the advantages and disadvantages.
Gōng Zhuàng said:
“Your Majesty, associating with the Hú,
how does that compare to associating with the Jìn?
The Hú are jackals and wolves.
Once they destroy Jìn,
you will have no choice but to serve them facing north.
If you contend with them for天下 (the empire),
then the strong and weak will be unmatched,
leading to a situation of danger and demise.
The affair of Yú and Guó
is an existing warning.”
The Zuǒ Zhuàn says: Jìn Xiàngōng borrowed a path through Yú to attack Guó.
After destroying Guó,
he then destroyed Yú.
All the close ministers considered Zhuàng’s words correct.
Shòu then ceased.
The soldiers all cheered “Long live!”
When soldiers have no desire to fight,
driving them to their deaths
has never resulted in anything but defeat.
If Lǐ Shòu had not heeded Gōng Zhuàng’s words,
Shǔ would have fallen even before Lǐ Shì.
Gōng Zhuàng believed that among human actions, none were greater than loyalty and filial piety.
Having avenged his father and uncle,
he meant to use Shòu to wipe out the descendants of Lǐ Tè.
Xíng (行),
read as xià mèng.
Shòu did not comply.
He then feigned deafness,
and claimed his hands could not control objects.
His hands could not control objects,
as if suffering from paralysis due to wind disease.
He amused himself with books
and never returned to Chéngdū for the rest of his life.
9 Zhào Shàngshūlìng Kuí Ān passed away.
Zhào Wáng Hǔ (趙王虎) ordered that three out of every five able-bodied men from the seven provinces of Sī (司), Jì (冀), Qīng (青), Xú (徐), Yōu (幽), Bìng (幷), and Yǒng (雍),
and two out of every four,
be conscripted.
Together with the old troops in Yèchéng (鄴城), they numbered fifty thousand.
They prepared ten thousand boats,
which travelled from the Yellow River to the sea,
transporting eleven million hú (斛) of grain to Lè'ānchéng (樂安城).
The *Shuǐ Jīng Zhù* (水經註) says: The Rú Shuǐ (濡水) flows southeast past Hǎiyáng (海陽) County in Liáoxī (遼西),
then passes south of Mùchéng (牧城),
where it divides into two streams: the northern stream is called Xiǎo Rú Shuǐ (小濡水),
which flows east past north of Lè'āntíng (樂安亭),
then southeast into the sea.
The Rú Shuǐ (濡水) flows southeast past south of Lè'āntíng (樂安亭),
then merges eastward with the old channel of the Xīn Hé (新河),
which was dug by Wèi Tàizǔ (魏太祖) when he campaigned against Tàdùn (蹋頓).
*Rú* (濡)
is pronounced *guān* (官) for *fān* (翻).
Shí Hǔ (石虎) established Sīzhōu (司州) in Yè (鄴),
and made the Jìn's (晉) Sīzhōu (司州) into Luòzhōu (洛州).
*Yǒng* (雍)
is pronounced *yú yòng* (於用) for *fān* (翻).
Báiláng (白狼) County,
in the Hàn (漢) dynasty, belonged to Běipíng (北平) Commandery;
it was abolished in the Jìn (晉) dynasty.
The *Shuǐ Jīng Zhù* (水經註) says: The Báiláng Shuǐ (白狼水) flows out from southeast of Báiláng (白狼) County,
north past Báiláng Shān (白狼山),
then northeast past west of the old city of Chānglí (昌黎) County,
then north past east of Huánglóngchéng (黃龍城),
then flows out northeast,
flowing east to form two streams,
the right stream is the Yú Shuǐ (渝水).
The *Dìlǐ Zhì* (地理志) says: The Yú Shuǐ (渝水) flows from south of the frontier into the sea.
One stream flows out northeast of the frontier,
becoming the Báiláng Shuǐ (白狼水),
then flows southeast to Fáng (房) County,
where it empties into the Liáo (遼).
All the people's horses were confiscated;
anyone daring to secretly hide one would be cut in half at the waist.
In total, more than forty thousand horses were obtained.
A grand review was held at Wǎnyáng (宛陽).
The *Shuǐ Jīng Zhù* (水經註) says: The Zhāng Shuǐ (漳水) flows from north of the Xīmén Bào (西門豹) temple past west of Zhào Yuèmǎ Tái (趙閱馬臺).
The platform was fifty *zhàng* (丈) high,
with viewing galleries on top;
Shí Hǔ (石虎) practiced military drills below it,
and viewed them from the galleries.
Yān Wáng Huàng (燕王皝) said to his generals:
"Shí Hǔ (石虎) believes Lè'ānchéng (樂安城) is heavily fortified,
and therefore will certainly not fortify Jìchéng (薊城) to the north or south.
If we take an unexpected route now,
we can completely defeat him."
In winter,
tenth month,
Huàng (皝) led his armies into Zhào (趙) through Yē'ōng Sài (蠮螉塞)
and attacked them.
The frontier generals who blocked their path were all captured,
and they advanced directly to Jìchéng (薊城).
Zhào Yōuzhōu Cìshǐ (趙幽州刺史) Shí Guāng (石光) had tens of thousands of troops,
but he shut himself inside the city and dared not sally forth.
The Yān (燕) army advanced and broke through Wǔsuìjīn (武遂津).
Wǔsuì (武遂) County,
in the Former Hàn (前漢) dynasty, belonged to Hérjiānguó (河間國);
in the Later Hàn (後漢) and Jìn (晉) dynasties, it belonged to Ānpínguó (安平國);
at this time, it belonged to Wǔyì (武邑) Commandery.
The Yì Shuǐ (易水) passed south of it,
hence it was called Wǔsuìjīn (武遂津).
Wherever they went, they burned accumulated provisions
and carried off more than thirty thousand households before departing.
The *Kǎoyì* (考異) states: The *Yān Shū* (燕書) says:
"They carried off several thousand men and women from the two commanderies of Yān (燕) and Fànyáng (范陽) and returned."
Now following the accounts in the *Hòu Zhào Zàijì* (後趙載記) and *Yān Zàijì* (燕載記).
Zhào Wáng Hǔ (趙王虎) appointed Qín Gōng Tāo (秦公韜) as Tàiwèi (太尉),
and had him and Tàizǐ Xuān (太子宣) alternately review memorials and imperial rescripts from the Shangshū (尚書) office each day.
*Diérì* (迭日)
means alternate days.
*Shěng* (省)
is pronounced *xī jǐng* (悉景) for *fān* (翻).
There was no need to report to him again.
Sītú Shēn Zhōng (司徒申鍾) admonished:
"Rewards and punishments are the great authority of a ruler,
and cannot be delegated to others.
This is to prevent minor evils from growing and to suppress rebellion before it occurs.
The crown prince's duty is to attend to your meals,
not to participate in governance;
the commoner Suì (邃) failed due to participating in governance,
as seen in the previous volume, Xiánkāng (咸康) third year.
Furthermore, when two powers share authority,
it rarely avoids disaster.
The *Zuǒ Zhuàn* (左傳) says: Xīn Bó (辛伯) advised Zhōu Huán Gōng (周桓公) saying:
'When a consort is equal to the principal wife,
and two administrations are paired in a state,
it is the root of chaos.'
'Two administrations'
refers to Xuān (宣) and Tāo (韜) taking turns to decide matters.
*Xiǎn* (鮮)
is pronounced *xī qiǎn* (息淺) for *fān* (翻).
This is precisely how you harm him."
Hǔ (虎) did not listen.
This laid the groundwork for Xuān (宣) to kill Tāo (韜).
Zhōng Yèzhě Lìng Shēn Biǎn (中謁者令申扁)
The Zhong Yèzhě Lìng (中謁者令)
was a eunuch.
Yáng Zhènghéng (楊正衡) says: *Biǎn* (扁)
is pronounced *fāng lián* (芳蓮) for *fān* (翻).
Xuān (宣) also grew close to him,
making him in charge of confidential matters.
Since Hǔ (虎) no longer attended to affairs,
and Xuān (宣) and Tāo (韜) both loved heavy drinking and hunting;
consequently, all appointments, dismissals, executions, and pardons were decided by Biǎn (扁).
From the Nine Ministers downwards, most knelt at the mere sight of his dust.
Tàizǐ Zhànshì Sūn Zhēn (太子詹事孫珍) suffered from an eye ailment,
and sought a remedy from Shìzhōng Cuī Yuē (侍中崔約).
Yuē (約) joked:
"If you urinate into it, it will heal."
A joke that if urine gets in his eye, the illness will be cured.
*Nì* (溺)
is pronounced *nǎi diào* (乃弔) for *fān* (翻).
"How can I urinate into my eye?"
Yuē (約) said:
"Your eyes are wide and staring,
perfectly suited for urination."
Zhēn (珍) resented this,
and reported it to Xuān (宣).
Xuān (宣) had the most foreign-looking deep-set eyes among his brothers,
and hearing this, he became enraged
and executed Yuē (約) and his son.
Thereafter, all officials from the dukes downwards feared Zhēn (珍) and dared not look him directly in the eye.
Yān Gōng Bīn (燕公斌) supervised the border provinces.
Bīn (斌) worked with Zhāng Hèdù (張賀度),
presumably supervising the northern border provinces.
*Bīn* (斌)
is pronounced *bīn* (彬).
He often entered with the gate bolt hanging.
The *guǎn* (管)
refers to the gate bolt and key of the city gate;
wanting to exit conveniently,
he often left the bolt hanging.
Bīn (斌) became angry
and insulted Hèdù (賀度).
Hǔ (虎) heard of this
and sent the Zhǔshū Lǐ Yí (主書禮儀) with a *jié* (節) to supervise him.
Since the Eastern Hàn (東漢) dynasty,
each division of the Shangshū (尚書) had its own Zhǔshū (主書),
which was an official position;
by the Qí (齊) and Liáng (梁) dynasties,
their power and responsibility became very significant.
Lǐ (禮)
is the surname;
Yí (儀)
is the given name.
During the Spring and Autumn period,
there was a Dàfū (大夫) named Lǐ Zhì (禮至) in Wèi (衞).
*Jiān* (監)
is pronounced *gǔ xián* (古銜) for *fān* (翻).
Bīn (斌) also wanted to kill Hèdù (賀度),
but Hèdù (賀度) rushed to report it with a strict guard.
Hǔ (虎) dispatched Shangshū Zhāng Lí (尚書張離) to lead cavalry to pursue Bīn (斌),
whipped him three hundred times,
removed him from office and sent him back to his residence,
and executed over ten of his close associates.
The historian remarks that Hǔ (虎) had no worthy sons.
Zhāng Jùn (張駿) sent his Biéjià (別駕) Mǎ Shēn (馬詵) to offer tribute to Zhào (趙).
His memorial was arrogant and rude;
Hǔ (虎)
was enraged
and wanted to execute Shēn (詵).
Shìzhōng Shí Pú (侍中石璞) admonished:
"What the state should prioritize eliminating now
is the remnant Jìn (晉) dynasty;
Hexī (河西) is remote and insignificant.
If we execute Mǎ Shēn (馬詵) now,
we will surely attack Zhāng Jùn (張駿),
which will divide our military strength in two,
and Jiànkāng (建康) will gain a few more years of life."
Hǔ (虎) then desisted.
Pú (璞)
was the great-grandson of Bāo (苞).
Shí Bāo (石苞) served Jìn Wén Dì (晉文帝) and Wǔ Dì (武帝), and his achievements were instrumental in founding the dynasty.
13 In the beginning,
Hàn general Lǐ Hóng (李閎) was captured by Jìn (晉),
the details of which are seen in the previous year.
Hàn (漢) ruler Lǐ Shòu (李壽) sent a letter to Zhào (趙) King Shí Hǔ (石虎) to request his return,
addressing it as
"Zhào (趙) King Shí (石) Gentleman."
Shí Hǔ (石虎) was displeased,
and handed it over for external discussion.
The Central Secretariat Supervisor, Wáng Bō (王波), said:
"Let Lǐ Hóng (李閎) swear an oath unto death, saying: 'If I can but return my bones to Shǔ (蜀),
I will surely gather my relatives
and assimilate into the King's transforming influence.'
If he is sincere,
then it would not require a single 'lǚ' (旅);
in ancient times, when an army marched,
five hundred men constituted a 'lǚ' (旅).
Should there be an advance and a retreat,
an advance and a retreat,
which is like people today speaking of having a mind for both progress and withdrawal.
What harm is that to Zhào (趙)?
Lǐ Shòu (李壽) has already usurped a great title,
and now if we issue an imperial edict to him,
he will surely reciprocate and respond,
chóu (酬)
means to answer.
fǎn (返)
means to return.
At that time, the Yìlóu (挹婁) kingdom presented hù (楛) arrows and stone arrowheads to Zhào (趙).
Yìlóu (挹婁)
was the ancient kingdom of the Sùshèn (肅慎) clan.
Hù (楛) arrows were one chí (尺) and one zhǐ (咫) long.
In their country, northeast of a mountain, stones emerged
whose sharpness could penetrate iron,
which were taken to make arrowheads.
Dù Yòu (杜佑) said: The Yìlóu (挹婁) kingdom is north of Mount Bùxián (不咸山),
over a thousand lǐ (里) northeast of Fúyú (夫餘),
bordering the great sea.
To the south, it borders Běi Wòjǔ (北沃沮).
Its northern extent is unknown,
but its breadth and length span several thousand lǐ (里).
Though the population is small, they are very brave and strong,
dwelling in mountainous and perilous terrain,
and skilled in archery.
Their bows are four chí (尺) long,
with the power of a crossbow;
their arrows use hù (楛) wood,
eighteen cùn (寸) long;
blue stone is used for the arrowheads,
which are called stone arrowheads.
When they take stones,
they must first pray to the spirits.
Hù (楛),
pronounced hòu gǔ fān (侯古翻),
is the name of a tree,
similar to shī (蓍).
Nǔ (砮),
pronounced nǔ (奴),
is an arrowhead.
He said:
"This will let him know that I am capable of subduing distant regions."
Shí Hǔ (石虎) agreed,
and sent Lǐ Hóng (李閎) back,
treating him with great courtesy.
When Lǐ Hóng (李閎) arrived in Chéngdū (成都),

Shí Hǔ (石虎) heard of this,
was enraged,
and demoted Wáng Bō (王波),

Taking Jìchéng (薊城) as the northern border.

Zú (卒),

Lí (嫠),

Qí Huán Gōng (齊桓公) campaigned north against the Shānróng (山戎) and

Over a hundred white geese gathered south of the Mǎdào 馬道.
Mǎdào 馬道 means a built road where horses can gallop back and forth.
None were caught.
At this time, over a million soldiers from various prefectures had gathered.
The Grand Astrologer Zhào Lǎn 趙攬 secretly spoke to Hǔ 虎, saying:
"White geese gathering in the courtyard is an omen that the palace will become empty.
It is not advisable to travel south."
Hǔ 虎 believed him,
and so he held a grand review at Xuānwǔ Guān 宣武觀 and then dismissed the troops.
Shí Hǔ 石虎 imitated the system of the Luòdū 洛都,
building Xuānwǔ Guān 宣武觀 in Yè 鄴.
'Guān' 觀
is pronounced 'gǔ wán' 古玩.
The Hàn 漢 ruler Shì 勢 changed the era name to Tàihé 太和;
he honored his mother, Lady Yán 閻, as Empress Dowager,
and established his wife, Lady Lǐ 李, as Empress.
3 Yàn Wáng Mùróng Huǎng, with Zuǒ Sīmǎ Gāo Xǔ, plotted to attack Yǔwén Yìdòuguī.
Xǔ said:
"Yǔwén is strong and prosperous.
If we do not take them now,
they will surely become a national threat.
Attacking them will surely lead to victory;
however, it will be unfavorable for the general."
He went out and told others:
"I will surely not return from this expedition,
but a loyal minister does not avoid it."
Thereupon, Huǎng personally led the attack on Yìdòuguī.
He appointed Mùróng Hàn as qiánfēng jiāngjūn,
with Liú Pèi as his deputy.
He separately ordered Mùróng Jūn, Mùróng Kè, Mùróng Bà, and zhéchōng jiāngjūn Mùyú Gēn to lead troops,
advancing in three routes simultaneously.
When Gāo Xǔ was about to set off,
he could not find his wife,
so he sent someone to convey family matters and departed.
Yìdòuguī dispatched Nánluódà Shèyègān to lead elite troops to meet them in battle.
Nánluó
is a city name.
Dà
means "city chief."
After Mùróng conquered Yǔwén,
they renamed Nánluó City to Wēidé City.
Kǎoyì says: Mùróng Huǎng Zàijì writes
"Shèyìgān."
Now we follow Yànshū.
"Shèyègān is unmatched in valor among the three armies;
it is advisable to avoid him slightly."
Hàn said:
"Yìdòuguī has gathered all the elite troops from his country and entrusted them to Shèyègān.
Shèyègān has a long-standing reputation for bravery and
is relied upon by his entire nation.
If we defeat him now,
their country will collapse without being attacked further.
Moreover, I am very familiar with Shèyègān's character.
Shú
is the same as shú.
He is actually easy to deal with,
and we should not avoid him and thus dampen our troops' morale."
So, they advanced to battle.
Hàn personally charged into the formation,
and Shèyègān came out to meet him.
Mùróng Bà attacked from the flank,
and then decapitated Shèyègān.
When the Yǔwén soldiers saw Shèyègān dead,
they fled without fighting.
The Yàn army pursued them, capitalizing on their victory,
and then captured their capital city.
The Yǔwén state's
capital was in Liáoxī Zǐméngchuān.
The Yǔwén clan scattered and perished as a result.
Huǎng collected all their livestock and goods,
relocated their five thousand-plus households to Chānglí,
and expanded his territory by over a thousand lǐ.
He renamed the city where Shèyègān resided Wēidé City,
stationed his younger brother Biāo there, and returned.
Gāo Xǔ and Liú Pèi both died from stray arrows.
Xǔ was skilled in astronomy.
Huǎng once said to him:
"You have excellent books, but you do not show them to me.
How can that be considered loyalty and devotion?"
Xǔ said:
"I have heard that a ruler holds the essentials,
while a minister holds the responsibilities.
One who holds the essentials is at ease,
while one who holds responsibilities toils.
This is why Hòujì sowed seeds,
but Yáo did not participate.
Observing celestial phenomena and astronomy
is extremely arduous day and night;
it is not something suitable for the尊 to personally engage in.
How will Your Highness use it?"
Huǎng remained silent.
Previously,
Yìdòuguī served Zhào very diligently,
sending continuous tribute.
When the Yàn people attacked Yìdòuguī,
Zhào Wáng Hǔ sent Yòu Jiāngjūn Bái Shèng and Bīngzhōu Cìshǐ Wáng Bà from Gānsōng to rescue him.
Gānsōng is east of Rúyuán
and west of Tūménlǐng.
The Yǔwén clan had already perished,
so they then attacked Wēidé City.
They failed to capture it and returned.
Mùróng Biāo pursued and attacked them,
defeating them.
When Mùróng Hàn fought against the Yǔwén clan,
he was hit by a stray arrow,
and was bedridden for a long time.
Later, he gradually recovered
and tried galloping a horse at his home.
Someone reported that Hàn was feigning illness but secretly practicing riding,
suspecting he intended to rebel.
Although Yàn Wáng Huǎng relied on Hàn's bravery and strategy,
he secretly harbored resentment towards him in his heart,
and so he ordered Hàn to commit suicide.
Hàn said:
"I committed a crime and fled,
and later returned.
Hàn's flight is seen in volume 95, Emperor Chéng's Xiánhé eighth year;
his return is seen in the preceding volume, Xiánkāng sixth year.
Fù,
read fú yòu fān.
However, the Jié bandits occupy the Central Plains.
I overestimated myself,
wishing to pacify the entire realm for the state.
Since this ambition cannot be fulfilled,
I have no lingering regrets.
This is fate!"
He drank poison and died.
Kǎoyì says: Sānshí Guó Chūnqiū states:
"In the second year of Yǒnghé,
ninth month,
Hàn was killed."
Yànshū Hàn Zhuàn says:
"Hàn once faced a battle line
and was hit by a stray arrow,
falling ill and bedridden.
He did not go out for a year.
Later, he gradually recovered
and tried his horse."
According to this, after the campaign against Yǔwén,
Hàn never participated in any further battles.
From the first month of the second year of Jiànyuán to the ninth month of the second year of Yǒnghé,
more than a year had already passed.
Sānshí Guó Chūnqiū is probably mistaken.
We now follow Zàijì Hàn Zhuàn.

6 Previously,
Zhào Lǐngjūn Wáng Lǎng spoke to Zhào Wáng Hǔ, saying:
"It is deep winter, and the snow is cold,
yet the Crown Prince is sending people to cut lumber for the palace,
transporting it via the Zhāng River.
Tens of thousands of laborers are toiling,
their cries of distress filling the roads.
Your Majesty should use an outing as an excuse to halt this work."
Hǔ agreed.
Crown Prince Xuān was enraged.
It happened that Yínghuò guarded Fáng.
Tiānwénzhì says: The four stars of Fáng constitute the Míngtáng,
which is the palace where the Son of Heaven governs;
they are also the Four Assistants.
The lowest first star
is the supreme general;
the next
is the second general;
the next
is the second prime minister;
the uppermost star
is the supreme prime minister.
Yínghuò guarding Fáng and Xīn
is considered inauspicious for rulers.
Yínghuò
is the Son of Heaven's principle;
thus it is said,
even if there is an enlightened Son of Heaven,
he must carefully observe Yínghuò's position.
"Fáng represents the Heavenly King.
Now Yínghuò guards it,
so the disaster will be considerable.
It is advisable to have a noble minister surnamed Wáng bear the calamity."
Hǔ asked:
"Who is suitable?"
Lǎn said:
"No one is nobler than Wáng Lǐngjūn."
Hǔ was reluctant to sacrifice Lǎng,
so he told Lǎn to suggest someone else.
Lǎn had no one else to suggest,
so he said:
"The next is only Zhōngshū Jiān Wáng Bō."
Hǔ then issued an edict,
retroactively condemning Bō for his previous discussion about the kǔshǐ affair,
seen in the preceding volume, Emperor Chéng's Xiánkāng sixth year,
and his four sons,
and their bodies were thrown into the Zhāng River.
Afterward, regretting that they were innocent,
he posthumously appointed Bō as Sīkōng
and enfeoffed his grandson as a hóu.
