and joined forces with Dàofù (道覆) to descend.
In the fifth month,
on the Wùwǔ (戊午) day,
Yì (毅) fought Xún (循) at Sāngluòzhōu (桑落洲).
Yì’s (毅) army was utterly defeated,
abandoning several hundred boats,
and fled on foot.
The remaining troops were all captured by Xún (循),
and the abandoned supplies were piled up like mountains.
Initially,
when Xún (循) reached Xúnyáng (尋陽),
he heard that Yù (裕) had already returned,
but still did not believe it;
after defeating Yì (毅),
he was able to confirm it through inquiry,
and he and his associates looked at each other, their faces drained of color.
Xún (循) wanted to retreat to Xúnyáng (尋陽),
attack and capture Jiānglíng (江陵),
and occupy the two prefectures to resist the imperial court.
The two prefectures refer to Jīng (荊) and Jiāng (江).
[Xú Dàofù] strongly argued for it.
Xún (循) hesitated for several days,
then followed his advice.
On the Jǐwèi (己未) day,
a great amnesty was proclaimed.
Yù (裕) recruited men for the army,
rewarding them according to the same standard as those who had responded to the call for justice at Jīngkǒu (京口).
Yù (裕) had raised an army at Jīngkǒu (京口) to suppress Huán Xuán (桓玄),
and the rewards for those who responded to the call for justice were generous at that time.
Some deliberated that it would be advisable to divide the troops to guard various strategic points,
but Yù (裕) said:
“The rebels are numerous and we are few.
If we divide our troops to garrison and defend,
they will be able to ascertain our strengths and weaknesses;
moreover, a setback in one place
will dampen the morale of the entire army.
Now, by gathering our forces at Shítou (石頭),
and responding as circumstances require,
we not only prevent them from knowing our numbers,
but also keep our collective strength undivided.
If more troops gradually gather,
we can then discuss it further.”
When the court heard that Liú Yì had been defeated,
people's spirits were agitated with fear.
At this time, the northern army had just returned,
and many of the officers and soldiers were wounded or ill.
The warriors in Jiànkāng did not number more than a few thousand.
As Xún had already overcome the two garrisons,
the two garrisons
refer to Jiāng and Yù.
his boats and carriages stretched for a hundred *lǐ* without interruption.
His tower ships were twelve *zhàng* high.
Those who had fled back in defeat all spoke of his strength and might.
Mèng Chǎng and Zhūgě Chángmín wanted to escort the imperial carriage across the river,
but Yù did not agree.
At that time, there were no cities or fortifications to rely on in either the west or north of the Jiāng River.
Chǎng and Chángmín wanted to escort the Son of Heaven across the river,
but this would be nothing more than fleeing east to Guǎnglíng,
or occupying Lìyáng in the west.
Chǎng,
pronounced *chǒu liǎng fān* (variant reading).
When Hé Wú-jì and Liú Yì went south to suppress the rebellion,
Chǎng had predicted their inevitable defeat,
and it turned out to be so.
By this point,
he again said that Yù would surely be unable to resist Xún.
The crowd largely believed him.
Only the General of Spirited Cavalry, Yúqiū Jìn of Dōnghǎi, refuted Chǎng and others in court,
deeming it untrue.
The Army Superintendent, Wáng Zhòngdé, said to Yù:
"My lord, you were born to be a regent,
and have established great merits,
shaking the entire realm with your might.
The Wèi Shangshū Cáo had a Zhōngbīng Láng (Internal Army Gentleman),
and the various ducal mansions, commanders, and garrisons consequently also established Zhōngbīng Cānjūn (Army Superintendents).
'Established great merits'
refers to the destruction of Yàn.
Upon hearing of your victorious return,
the rebels will naturally collapse;
if we first flee ourselves,
then our position will be no different from that of commoners.
How can commoners' commands
inspire awe in others?
If this plan is adopted,
I beg to resign from here."
Yù was very pleased.
Chǎng insisted repeatedly,
so Yù said:
"Now, our important garrisons are defeated externally,
and a strong enemy is pressing internally.
People's spirits are in peril and alarm,
and none have a firm resolve.
If we were to move once,
we would immediately collapse and disintegrate,
and how could we even reach the north of the Jiāng River?
Even if we could reach it,
it would only prolong our existence by a few days.
Although our soldiers are few now,
they are enough for one battle.
If we succeed,
then both ruler and subject will enjoy peace together.
If a dire fate is inevitable,
I shall fall dead before the temple gate,
fulfilling my long-held ambition to devote my life to the state.
I cannot hide in the wilderness to seek a temporary survival.
My decision is made,
so you need not speak further!"
Chǎng was resentful that his words were not followed,
and moreover believed that they would surely be defeated,
so he requested to die.
Yù angrily said:
"You should fight again!"
*Shēn*
means 'again'.
Chǎng knew that Yù would ultimately not use his advice,
so he presented a memorial stating:
"When your subject Yù marched north,
the populace generally disagreed,
but only your subject supported Yù's plan;
this matter is recorded in the previous year.
The state is in peril,
and this is my fault.
I humbly accept the blame to apologize to the world."
After finishing the memorial,
he swallowed poison and died.
On the day *Yǐchǒu*,
Lú Xún reached the Huái Estuary.
This refers to the mouth where the Qínhuái River enters the Jiāng River.
Wáng Déwén of Lángyá was appointed Supervisor of the Palatial City Forces,
stationed at Zhōngtáng Huáng.
A *táng* (hall) without four walls is called *huáng*.
The various generals each had their own garrisons.
Yù's son Yìlóng was only four years old.
Yù ordered the Consulting Army Supervisor, Liú Cuì, to assist him,
and he was garrisoned at Jīngkǒu.
Cuì was a clansman and younger brother of Yì.
Yù saw the people standing by the water to watch the enemy,
and found it strange,
so he asked the Army Supervisor Zhāng Shào.
Shào replied:
"If the commander's authority had not yet returned,
the people would be too busy fleeing and scattering,
how could they watch?
Now, they must no longer be afraid."
Yù said to his aides:
"If the enemy advances directly at Xīntíng,
their momentum will be irresistible.
We should avoid them for now;
the outcome of victory or defeat cannot yet be determined.
If they turn and anchor on the west bank,
the west bank
is Cáizhōu,
Xú Dàofù requested to burn the boats and advance from Xīntíng to Báishí,
attacking Yù from several directions.
Xún wanted to plan for absolute safety,
and said to Dàofù:
"Our main army has not yet arrived,
and Mèng Chǎng has already taken his own life upon hearing the news.
Speaking of the general situation,
they will naturally collapse and fall into chaos within days.
To decide victory or defeat in one morning now,
seeking profit by taking risks,
is neither a sure way to win,
and moreover, it will cause casualties among our soldiers.
It is better to hold our troops and wait."
Dàofù, seeing Xún's excessive indecisiveness,
sighed and said:
"I will ultimately be misled by Lord Lú,
and nothing will be accomplished.
If only I could act as a hero,
the world would be easy to pacify."
Yù ascended Shítou City to observe Xún's army.
When he first saw them heading towards Xīntíng,
he looked at his attendants, and their faces turned pale.
But when they turned and anchored at Cáizhōu,
he was pleased.
Cáizhōu is on the west bank of Shítou.
Today, twenty-five *lǐ* west of Shàngyuán County, Jiànkāng Prefecture, there is Cáizhōu.
Fearing Xún's encroachment,
Yù followed Yúqiū Jìn's plan:
he cut down trees to build palisades at Shítou Huáikǒu,
repaired Yuèchéng,
and built three forts: Chápǔ, Yàoyuán, and Tíngwèi.
Chápǔ is on the south bank of the Great Jiāng River,
near the Qínhuái Estuary.
Yàoyuán
was likely a place for planting medicinal herbs.
Tíngwèi Temple was where the offices of the Grand Judge were located,
and thus became a place name.
Chá,
pronounced *zhuāng jiā fān* (variant reading).
According to the Jinshu Dìjì,
the three forts were all at the Huái Estuary.
Liú Yì traveled through lands inhabited by both barbarians and Jìn subjects.
The region above and below Xīyáng was inhabited by barbarians,
hence called 'barbarian';
those who were royal subjects and subject to rent, taxes, and conscription
were called 'Jìn'.
His followers were hungry and exhausted,
and seven or eight out of ten died.
On the day *Bǐngyín*,
he arrived at Jiànkāng,
awaiting punishment.
Yù comforted and encouraged him,
and made him responsible for internal and external affairs.
This refers to being responsible for the internal and external affairs of the various military commands.
An imperial edict demoted him to General of the Rear.
11 Wèi Zhǎngsūn Sōng reached Mòběi and returned.
The Rouran pursued and surrounded him at Niúchuān.
On the day *Rénshēn*,
the Wèi ruler Sì marched north to attack the Rouran.
Shèlún, the Khagan of the Rouran, heard of this
and fled,
dying on the way.
His son Dùbá was still young,
so the tribesmen enthroned Shèlún's younger brother Húlǜ,
styling him Àidòu
Khagan.
Sì led his troops back to Cānhégpō.
12 Lú Xún 盧循 ambushed troops on the south bank.
The south bank
was the south bank of the Qínhuái 秦淮 River mouth.
He declared that all his forces would advance from Báishí Bù 白石步.
Liú Yù 劉裕 left Cānjūn 參軍 Shěn Línzǐ 沈林子 and Xú Chìtè 徐赤特 to guard the south bank,
cut off Chápǔ 查浦,
and instructed them to hold fast and not move.
Yù 裕, along with Liú Yì 劉毅 and Zhūgě Chángmín 諸葛長mín, went north to resist him.
Línzǐ 林子 said:
"The words of this demon rebel
are not necessarily true.
We should prepare deeply against him."
Yù 裕 said:
"Shítóu Chéng 石頭城 is perilous,
and the Huái Zhà 淮柵 is very strong.
Leaving you behind
is sufficient to defend it."
Línzǐ 林子 was Mùfū 穆夫's son.
Shěn Mùfū 沈穆夫 was from Wúxīng Wǔkāng 吳興武康.
In the third year of Lóng'ān 隆安 (399),
Sūn Ēn 孫恩 plundered Kuàijī 會稽,
and the three Wú 吳 prefectures responded.
Mùfū 穆夫 was in Kuàijī 會稽.
Ēn 恩 made him Yúyáo Lìng 餘姚令.
Ēn 恩 was defeated by Liú Láozhī 劉牢之,
who also killed Mùfū 穆夫.
On the *gēngchén* 庚辰 day,
Lú Xún 盧循 burned Chápǔ 查浦 and
advanced to Zhānghóu Qiáo 張侯橋.
Xú Chìtè 徐赤特 was about to attack them.
Línzǐ 林子 said:
"The rebels claim to go to Báishí 白石 but repeatedly come to challenge us.
Their true intention is clear.
Our forces are outnumbered.
It is better to hold the perilous position and await the main army."
Chìtè 赤特 did not comply
and went out to battle.
The ambushing troops were unleashed,
and Chìtè 赤特 was greatly defeated,
fleeing to the north of the Huái 淮 in a single boat.
This was the north bank of the Qínhuái 秦淮 River.
Zhū Língshí 朱齡石 rescued him,
and the rebels then retreated.
Xún 循 led his elite troops and advanced greatly,
reaching Dānyáng Jùn 丹陽郡.
Dānyáng Jùn 丹陽郡 was the seat of the Dānyáng Yǐn 丹陽尹.
The character shàng 上
is read as chǎng 掌 at this time.
(Lú Xún 盧循) beheaded Xú Chìtè 徐赤特,
disarmed for a long time,
and then deployed his ranks at Nántáng 南塘.
Nántáng 南塘 was the south bank of the Qínhuái 秦淮 River.
The character chén 陳
is read as zhèn 陣.
13 In the sixth month,
Liú Yù 劉裕 was made Tàiwèi 太尉 and Zhōngshū Jiān 中書監, and granted the Yellow Battle-Axe (Huángyuè 黃鉞).
Yù 裕 accepted the Yellow Battle-Axe,
but firmly declined the rest.
Yǔ Yuè 庾悅, Cārjì Zhōngjūn Sīmǎ 車騎中軍司馬, was made Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ 江州刺史.
Yuè 悅 was Zhǔn 準's son.
Liú Yù 劉裕 was Chējì Jiāngjūn 車騎將軍.
Because Liú Jìngxuān 劉敬宣 had suffered a defeat in the campaign against Shǔ 蜀,
he requested to be demoted to Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn 中軍將軍.
Therefore, the Chējì 車騎 and Zhōngjūn 中軍 departments shared one Sīmǎ 司馬.
Yǔ Zhǔn 庾準 was Yǔ Liàng 庾亮's grandson.
14 Sīmǎ Guógūo Fán 司馬國璠 and his younger brothers Shú Fán 叔璠 and Shú Dào 叔道 fled to Qín 秦.
Qín Wáng Xīng 秦王興 said:
"Liú Yù 劉裕 is now executing Huán Xuán 桓玄 and
assisting the Jìn Shì 晉室.
Why have you come?"
They replied:
"Yù 裕 weakens the royal house.
Whenever any of our clan members tries to establish themselves,
Yù 裕 eliminates them.
He will become a national menace,
even worse than Huán Xuán 桓玄."
Xīng 興 made Guógūo Fán 國璠 Yángzhōu Cìshǐ 揚州刺史,
and Shú Dào 叔道 Jiāozhōu Cìshǐ 交
州刺史.
15 Lú Xún 盧循 plundered various counties but gained nothing.
He said to Xú Dàofù 徐道覆:
"Our army is weary.
It would be better to return to Xúnyáng 尋陽,
combine forces to take Jīngzhōu 荊州,
occupy two-thirds of the empire,
and then compete with Jiànkāng 建康."
In autumn,
the seventh month,
on the *gēngshēn* 庚申 day,
Xún 循 returned south from Càizhōu 蔡洲 to Xúnyáng 尋陽,
leaving his partisan Fàn Chóngmín 范崇民 with five thousand men to occupy Nánlíng 南陵.
Nánlíng 南陵 was west of Xuānchéng Xiàn 宣城縣 in Xuānchéng Jùn 宣城郡.
The Liáng 梁 dynasty established Nánlíng Jùn 南陵郡 and Nánlíng Xiàn 南陵縣.
It was probably the border of Shíchéng Xiàn 石城縣 in Hàn Dānyáng Jùn 漢丹陽郡.
Today, it is part of Guìchí Xiàn 貴池縣, Chízhōu 池州.
Xún 循 feared his troops might be sharp or dull,
and wanted to return south to Pānyú 番禺.
Therefore, he had Chóngmín 崇mín guard it to secure the entrance to Pénglǐ Hú 彭蠡湖.
Sòng Bái 宋白 said: The opposite bank of Zhàjiāng Kǒu 柵江口 was the old Nánlíng Xiàn 南陵縣 territory,
now Fánchāng Xiàn 繁昌縣.
On the *jiǎzǐ* 甲子 day,

Yù 裕 sent Fǔguó Jiāngjūn 輔國將軍 Wáng Zhòngdé 王仲德, Guǎngchuān Tàishǒu 廣川太守 Liú Zhōng 劉鍾, Héjiān Nèishǐ 河間內史 Lánlíng Kuǎién 蘭陵蒯恩, Zhōngjūn Zīyì Cānjūn 中軍諮議參軍 Mèng Huáiyù 孟懷玉, and others to lead forces to pursue Xún 循.
16 On the *yǐchǒu* 乙丑 day,
Wèi Zhǔ Sī 魏主嗣 returned to Píngchéng 平城.
17 Xī Qín Wáng Gān Guī 西秦王乾歸 attacked Yuè Zhì 越質, Qū Jī 屈機, and more than ten other tribes.
Yuè Zhì 越質 was of Xiānbēi 鮮卑 stock.
His chieftain was called Chì Lí 叱黎.
Chì Lí 叱黎's son was called Jié Guī 詰歸,
who surrendered to Gān Guī 乾歸 in the sixteenth year of Xiàowǔ Tàiyuán 孝武太元 (391)
and rebelled to surrender to Qín 秦 in the twenty-first year (396).
Qū Jī 屈機 was Jié Guī 詰歸,
the pronunciation was slightly corrupted.
(They were) resettled in Yuànchuān 苑川.
In the eighth month,
Gān Guī 乾歸 again made Yuànchuān 苑川 his capital.
The Qǐfú Shì 乞伏氏 originally had their capital at Dùjiān Shān 度堅山.
When Gān Guī 乾歸 became powerful,
he first made Yuànchuān 苑川 his capital.
After being defeated by Qín 秦 and surrendering to Qín 秦,
Qín 秦 made him garrison Yuànchuān 苑川.
He rebelled again,
fearing an attack by Qín 秦,
and returned to defend Dùjiān Shān 度堅山.
Now, his tribal forces were gradually growing,
and he no longer feared Qín 秦,
so he again made Yuànchuān 苑川 his capital.
18 Jǔqú Méngxùn 沮渠蒙遜 attacked Xī Liáng 西涼,
defeating Xī Liáng Shìzǐ 西涼世子 Xīn 歆 at Mǎmiào 馬廟.
In ancient times, the Horse Ancestor (Mǎzǔ 馬祖) was worshipped.
Later generations built temples to worship him,
hence the place was named Mǎmiào 馬廟.
Liáng Gōng Gǎo 涼公暠 redeemed Yuánhǔ 元虎 with two thousand *jin* 斤 of silver and two thousand *liǎng* 兩 of gold.
Méngxùn 蒙遜 returned him,
then formed an alliance with Gǎo 暠 and returned.
19 Liú Yù 劉裕 returned to Dōngfǔ 東府.
After Lú Xún 盧循 retreated,
Yù 裕 returned to Dōngfǔ 東府.
He sent Jiànwēi Jiāngjūn 建威將軍 Kuàijī Sūn Chǔ 會稽孫處 and Zhènwǔ Jiāngjūn 振武將軍 Shěn Tiánzǐ 沈田子 to lead three thousand men to attack Pānyú 番禺 by sea.
Tiánzǐ 田子 was Línzǐ 林子's elder brother.
Everyone thought:
"The sea route is difficult and distant,
and will surely lead to trouble.
Moreover, dividing our current strength
is not an urgent need at present."
Yù 裕 did not listen.
He instructed Chǔ 處, saying:
"The main army will surely defeat the demon rebels around the twelfth month.
When you arrive,
first destroy their lair,
so that they have nowhere to return."
20 Qiáo Zòng 譙縱 sent Shìzhōng 侍中 Qiáo Liáng 譙良 and others to meet with Qín 秦,
requesting troops to attack Jìn 晉.
Zòng 縱 made Huán Qiān 桓謙 Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ 荊州刺史 and Qiáo Dàofú 譙道福 Liángzhōu Cìshǐ 梁州刺史,
leading twenty thousand men to attack Jīngzhōu 荊州.
Qín Wáng Xīng 秦王興 sent Qián Jiāngjūn 前將軍 Gǒu Lín 苟林 to lead cavalry to join them.
Since Lú Xún 盧循 descended east from Jiānglíng 江陵,
no news from Jiànkāng 建康 could be obtained,
and bandits arose everywhere.
Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ 荊州刺史 Liú Dàoguī 劉道規 sent Sīmǎ 司馬 Wáng Zhènzhī 王鎮之 to lead Tiānmén Tàishǒu 天門太守 Tán Dàojì 檀道濟.
In the sixth year of Sūn Xiū Yǒng'ān 孫休永安 (263), Wú 吳 established Tiānmén Jùn 天門郡 by dividing Wǔlíng 武陵.
In Chōng Xiàn 充縣, there was Sōngliáng Shān 松梁山.
On the mountain, there were rocks.
Where the rocks opened, for dozens of *zhàng* 丈 high,
it was so high
that an arrow shot upwards from a crossbow could not reach it.
The top was named Tiānmén 天門,
and thus the commandery was named.
The Yúdì Zhì 輿地志 says: Lǐzhōu Shímén Xiàn 澧州石門縣 was the ancient Tiānmén Jùn 天門郡.
The character shuài 帥
is read as lǜ 率;
same below.
Dàojì 道濟 was Zhī 祗's younger brother.
Zhèn arrived at Xúnyáng,
and was defeated by Gǒu Lín.
Lú Xún heard of this,
appointed Lín as the Nánmán 校尉 (Commandant of the Southern Man),
allocated troops to him,
and ordered him to take advantage of the victory to attack Jiānglíng,
spreading word that Xú Dàofù had already captured Jiànkāng.
Huán Qiān recruited his old loyalists on the way.
The Huán clan had resided in Jīngchǔ for generations,
bound by old favors.
Righteousness dictated they not forget each other,
hence they were called "old loyalists."
Qiān encamped at Zhījiāng.
Zhījiāng County had belonged to Nánjùn since the Hàn dynasty.
It was the state of Luó in the Spring and Autumn period.
The Jiāng River at the west of the county splits off to form the Tuó,
and then rejoins the Jiāng to the east,
hence it is called Zhījiāng (Branch River).
In the sixth year of Xīníng of our dynasty,
Zhījiāng was abolished as a county and made a township,
incorporated into Sōngzī County.
With the two bandits pressing hard,
many of Jiānglíng's gentry and commoners harbored disloyal intentions.
Dàoguī then assembled his generals and soldiers and announced to them:
"Huán Qiān is now nearby.
I hear that many elders are considering changing their allegiance.
The civil and military officials who came with me from the east are sufficient to accomplish the task;
'civil and military officials from the east'
refers to the generals, advisors, and soldiers accompanying Dàoguī.
They were not originally forbidden to leave."
He then opened the city gates at night,
and they remained open until dawn.
Everyone was awed and submitted,
and none left.
Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Lǔ Zōngzhī led several thousand troops from Xiāngyáng to Jiānglíng.
Some said that Zōngzhī's intentions were unpredictable,
but Dàoguī met him alone on horseback.
Zōngzhī was moved and pleased.
Dàoguī made Zōngzhī stay and defend,
entrusting him with important responsibilities,
while he himself led the armies to attack Qiān.
All the generals and advisors said:
"Now to go far out to attack Qiān,
victory is not certain.
Gǒu Lín is close by at Jiāngjīn,
watching our every move.
If he comes to attack the city,
Zōngzhī may not be able to hold it;
if there is any mishap,
the great cause will be lost."
Dàoguī said:
"Gǒu Lín is foolish and cowardly,
with no other clever schemes.
Because I will not be far away,
he will certainly not dare to approach the city.
I will now take Qiān,
and will conquer him as soon as I arrive;
in the short time I am gone,
I will have already returned.
If Qiān is defeated, Lín will lose heart;
how could he have time to come?
Moreover, Zōngzhī, defending alone,
why would he not be able to hold out for a few days?"
He then swiftly went to attack Qiān,
advancing by both land and water.
Qiān and others deployed a large fleet,
along with infantry and cavalry,
and fought at Zhījiāng.
Tán Dàojì advanced first and broke their formation,
and Qiān and the others were routed.
Qiān fled on a single boat to Gǒu Lín,
and Dàoguī pursued and beheaded him.
Returning,
he reached Yǒngkǒu.
Shuǐjīngzhù: The Yǒng Water flows south from the Xià Water to connect with the Jiāng,
which is called Yǒngkǒu.
This is what Zuo's Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals calls "Yán'áo wandered in Yǒng and escaped,"
located east of Jiānglíng City.
Dù Yù says: The Yǒng Water is in Huáróng County, Nánjùn.
Yǒng,
pronounced yǒng.
Lín fled,
and Dàoguī sent the Cányì Cānjūn (Consultative Staff Officer) Liú Zūn of Línhuái to lead troops in pursuit.
Initially,
when Qiān arrived at Zhījiāng,
all the gentry and commoners of Jiānglíng had sent letters to Qiān,
detailing the city's strengths and weaknesses,
intending to act as internal agents.
By this time, these letters were found,
but Dàoguī burned them all without looking,
and the people were greatly reassured.
21 Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ Yǔ Yuè made Póyáng Tàishǒu Yúqiū Jìn his vanguard,
repeatedly defeating Lú Xún's troops,
and advanced to Yùzhāng,
cutting off Xún's supply route.
In the ninth month,
Liú Zūn beheaded Gǒu Lín at Bālíng.
Huán Shísuí, taking advantage of Xún's invasion,
raised an army at Luòkǒu.
Shuǐjīngzhù: The Hàn Water passes through Ānyáng County, Wèixīng,
then east to south of Tǎngchéng,
where it meets the Luògǔ Water.
The water flows north out of Luògǔ,
and the valley connects north to Cháng'ān.
Its water flows south into the Hàn Water,
which is called Luòkǒu.
Zhēngyáng Lìng Wáng Tiān'ēn proclaimed himself Liángzhōu Cìshǐ.
"Zhēngyáng"
should be
"Wēiyáng."
Jìn Geography Record: Wēiyáng County belonged to Shàngyōng Commandery.
Shěn Yuè says: Wèi established Jiànshǐ County,
and Emperor Wǔ of Jìn changed its name to Wēiyáng.
When King Wǔ of Zhōu attacked Zhòu,
the eight states of Yōng, Shǔ, Qiāng, Máobù, Wēi, Lú, Péng, and Pú followed him.
I speculate that Wēiyáng County was named after the ancient Wēi state,
but history offers no basis for this.
Liángzhōu Cìshǐ Fù Sháo sent his son, Wèixīng Tàishǒu Hóngzhī, to attack Shísuí and others,
beheading them all,
and the Huán clan was thus extinguished.
Sháo was Chàng's grandson.
22 Xī Qín Wáng Gān Guī attacked the Qín commanderies of Luèyáng, Nán'ān, and Lǒngxī,
conquering them all,
and relocated twenty-five thousand households to Yuànchuān and Báohǎn.
23 On the day of Jiǎyín,
Wèi Zhǔ Guī was buried at Jīnlíng, Shènglè,
posthumously named Xuānwǔ,
and given the temple name Lièzǔ.
In the first year of Yǒngchū of Sòng Gāozǔ,
Wèi changed Guī's posthumous name to Dàowǔ Huángdì.
24 Liú Yì stubbornly insisted on pursuing and attacking Lú Xún.
Chángshǐ Wáng Dàn secretly advised Liú Yù, saying:
"Since Yì has already been defeated,
it is not suitable to let him achieve merit again."
Yù followed his advice.
In winter,
tenth month,
Yù led Yǎnzhōu Cìshǐ Liú Pān, Níngshuò Jiāngjūn Tán Sháo, Guànjūn Jiāngjūn Liú Jìngxuan, and others
to attack Lú Xún in the south,
appointing Liú Yì as Jiān Tàiwèi Líufǔ (Supervisor of the Grand Commandant's Deputy Office),
entrusting all subsequent matters to him.
On the day of Guǐsì,
Yù departed Jiànkāng.
25 Xú Dàofù led thirty thousand troops towards Jiānglíng,
suddenly arriving at Pòzhǒng.
Pòzhǒng is east of Jiāngjīn.
Qù (趣),
pronounced qīyù.
The attempt to recall them failed, and public sentiment was greatly shaken.
Some even spread rumors that Xún had already pacified Jīngyì,
and sent Dàofù to be the Cìshǐ.
The gentry and commoners of Jiāng and Hàn, grateful for Liú Dàoguī's kindness in burning the letters,
no longer harbored disloyal intentions.
Dàoguī made Liú Zūn a separate mobile force,
and he himself resisted Dàofù at Yùzhāngkǒu.
The vanguard suffered a defeat;
Zūn attacked from the flank,
severely defeating them,
beheading over ten thousand and driving most of the rest into the water to drown.
Dàofù fled on a single boat back to Pénkǒu.
Initially,
when Dàoguī made Zūn a mobile force,
everyone thought that with a strong enemy ahead,
the only concern was too few troops,
and that they should not divide their existing strength
and place it in a useless position.
When Dàofù was defeated,
the mobile force proved decisive,
and everyone was convinced.
26 The Xiānbēi Bùhún, Qiāng Jùqǐ, Shūbào, Dèngruò, and others
led twenty thousand households to surrender to Xī Qín.
The Xiānbēi had the Bùhún tribe;
Jùqǐ, Shūbào, and Dèngruò were Qiāng clans.
Jù (句),
pronounced gǔhóu.
27 Wáng Zhòngdé and others, hearing that Liú Yù's large army was approaching,
advanced to attack Fàn Chóngmín at Nánlíng.
Chóngmín's warships were moored abreast along the west
bank.
In the eleventh month,
Liú Zhōng went personally to scout the enemy.
It was foggy,
and the enemy hooked his boat.
Zhōng then led his retinue to attack the crew of the warship.
Jiànhù (艦戶),
what boatmen now call mǎmén.
Zhōng then slowly returned,
and together with Zhòngdé attacked Chóngmín.
Chóngmín fled.
When Chóngmín fled,
Yù could advance directly, and Xún lost the strategic advantage of Húkǒu.
On the 28th day, *guǐchǒu*,
Bāo Lòu (鮑陋), the Inspector of Yìzhōu, died.
Qiáo Dàofú (譙道福) captured Bādōng
and killed its defending generals, Wēn Zuò (溫祚) and Shí Yánzǔ (時延祖).
Wēn Zuò was originally the Administrator of Bādōng.
Shí Yánzǔ, since Liú Jìngxuān's (劉敬宣) and Huáng Hǔ's (黃虎) retreat, had been garrisoned in Bādōng.
The character '將' (jiāng)
is pronounced as 'liàng' (亮).
Those of Lú Xún's (盧循) troops guarding Guǎngzhōu did not consider the sea route a threat.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Sūn Chǔ (孫處) arrived by sea unannounced.
Amidst a great fog,
he attacked them from four sides,
and captured the city that very day.
Chǔ comforted its old residents,
executed Xún's close associates,
disciplined his troops to maintain strict guard,
and dispatched Shěn Tiánzǐ (沈田子) and others to attack the various commanderies south of the mountains.
Liú Yù's (劉裕) army reached Léichí (雷池).
Lú Xún spread the rumor that he would not attack Léichí,
but would follow the current directly downstream.
Yù knew he intended to fight.
In the twelfth month,
on the *jǐmǎo* day,
the army advanced to Dàléi (大雷).
Dù Yòu (杜佑) said: "The Jìn (晉) fortress of Dàléi
is in Wàngjiāng (望江) County, Shūzhōu (舒州).
To the west of modern Wǎn Kǒu (皖口) is Léijiāng Kǒu (雷江口),
which is that very place."
The *Sòngshū Zhì* (宋書志) states: "To the west of Wàngjiāng County is Dàléi Jiāng (大雷江),
which flows 300 *lǐ* (里) from Xúnyáng (尋陽) and Cháicāng (柴桑) into the Jiāng (江),
which is Wàngjiāng County."
On the *gēngchén* day,
Lú Xún and Xú Dàofù (徐道覆) led tens of thousands of troops, blocking the river as they descended,
such that one could not see the ends of their prows and sterns.
Yù brought out all his light ships,
and led his troops to attack them with full force.
He also divided his infantry and cavalry to be stationed on the west bank,
having first prepared fire-making tools.
Yù used strong crossbows to shoot at Xún's army,
pressing them with the advantage of wind and water.
Xún's ships all anchored on the west bank.
The troops on the bank threw fire to burn them,
and smoke and flames filled the sky.
The character '烟' (yān)
is the same as '煙'.
The character '炎' (yán)
is pronounced as 'yàn' (燄).
Xún retreated to Xúnyáng.
Intending to proceed to Yùzhāng (豫章),
he then exerted all his strength to block Zuǒlǐ (左里) with a barricade.
Zuǒlǐ was so named because the place was to the left of Zhāngjiāng (章江).
Dù Yòu said: "Zuǒlǐ is the mouth of Pénglǐ Hú (彭蠡湖) in Xúnyáng County, Jiāngzhōu (江州)."
The character '斷' (duàn)
is pronounced as 'dīngguǎn' (丁管).
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Yù's army reached Zuǒlǐ,
but could not advance.
As Yù brandished his banner to signal battle,
the pole of the banner he held broke,
and the pennant sank into the water.
The troops were all surprised and fearful.
Yù laughed and said:
"In the battle of the overturned boat last year,
(referring to the time when he fought against Huán Xuán (桓玄) and Huán Qiān (桓謙) while suppressing Huán Xuán's rebellion),
the character '折' (zhé)
is pronounced as 'éshè' (而設).
The character '沈' (chén)
is pronounced as 'chílín' (持林).
Now it is happening again;
the bandits will certainly be defeated."
He immediately attacked the barricade and advanced.
Although Xún's troops fought to the death,
they could not stop him.
Xún fled in a single boat.
Those killed or drowned totaled more than ten thousand.
Yù accepted those who surrendered,
pardoned those who had been forced to join,
and dispatched Liú Fān (劉藩) and Mèng Huáiyù (孟懷玉) with light troops to pursue him.
Xún gathered his scattered soldiers,
still numbering several thousand,
and returned directly to Pānyú (番禺).
Dàofù fled to secure Shǐxīng (始興).
Yù appointed Chǔ Yùzhī (褚裕之) as Acting Inspector of Guǎngzhōu, with the title of Jiànwēi Jiāngjūn (建威將軍).
Yùzhī
was the great-grandson of Púzhī (裒之).
Chǔ Póu (褚裒)
was the father of Empress Dowager Chóngdé (崇德太后).
The character '裒' (póu)
is pronounced as 'póuhóu' (蒲侯).
Liú Yì (劉毅) disliked Liú Mùzhī (劉穆之).
He often subtly spoke to Yù about Mùzhī's excessive power,
but Yù trusted and relied on him even more.
Mànní (萬泥), Duke of Guǎngchuān (廣川), and Rǔchén (乳陳), Duke of Shànggǔ (上谷), of Yàn (燕),
considered themselves members of the imperial clan
and had great achievements.
When Mùróng Xī (慕容熙) died,
Mànní and Rǔchén both had merits.
Bál (跋), King of Yàn, considered the two vassal states to have great responsibilities,
and for a long time did not summon them.
Bál appointed Mànní as the Governor of Yōu (幽) and Píng (平) Prefectures,
garrisoned at Féirú (肥如);
and Rǔchén as the Governor of Bīng (幷) and Qīng (青) Prefectures,
garrisoned at Báiláng (白狼).
This year,
Rǔchén secretly sent someone to tell Mànní:
"Rǔchén has a great plan,
and wishes to consult with you, uncle, to achieve it."
Mànní then defected to Báiláng,
and rebelled together with Rǔchén.
Bál dispatched Hóng (弘), Duke of Jízhùn (汲郡), and Zhāng Xīng (張興) with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to suppress them.
Hóng first sent an envoy to explain the consequences of their actions;
Mànní wanted to surrender,
but Rǔchén refused.
Xīng said to Hóng:
"The bandits will come out to fight tomorrow.
Tonight, they will surely try to surprise our camp.
We should prepare for it."
Hóng then secretly ordered men to prepare ten bundles of straw each,
accumulate fire, and conceal soldiers to wait for them.
That night,
Rǔchén indeed sent over a thousand brave men to cut down the camp.
All the fires ignited at once,
and the hidden soldiers ambushed them,
capturing and slaying all of them.
Mànní and Rǔchén were frightened and surrendered,
but Hóng executed them both.
Bál appointed Sùfú (素弗), Duke of Fànyáng (范陽), as Dàsīmǎ (大司馬),
and re-enfeoffed him as Duke of Liáoxī (遼西);
Hóng was appointed Piàojì Dàjiāngjūn (驃騎大將軍),
and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Zhōngshān (中山).
Punctuation by Niè Chóngqí (聶崇岐), collated by Wáng Chóngwǔ (王崇武)
Edited by Sīmǎ Guāng (司馬光)
by imperial decree
Hòu Xué Tiāntái (後學天台)
Ān Huángdì Xīn (安皇帝辛)
Yìxī (義熙) 7th year (Xīnhài (辛亥), 411 CE)
1. Spring,
first month,
on the *jǐwèi* day,
Liú Yù returned to Jiànkāng.
2. Bì (弼), Duke of Guǎngpíng (廣平) of Qín (秦), was favored by Qín King Xīng (興).
He was appointed Inspector of Yōngzhōu,
garrisoned at Āndìng (安定).
The Yáo Qín (姚秦) established the Inspector of Yōngzhōu over five commanderies north of the mountains,
garrisoned at Āndìng.
The character '雍' (yōng)
is pronounced as 'yúyòng' (於用).
Bì was advised to befriend Xīng's close attendants in order to seek an imperial audience.
Xīng summoned Bì to be Shàngshū Lìng (尚書令), Shìzhōng (侍中), and Dàjiāngjūn (大將軍).
Bì then devoted himself to befriending court officials,
gathering famous and influential people,
to subvert the Eastern Palace;
the people of the state disliked him.
At that time, Xīng, seeing many rebellions in the northwest,
wished to appoint a high-ranking general to govern and pacify the region.
Guō Bō (郭播), Administrator of Lǒngdōng (隴東), requested that Bì be sent out to garrison the area.
The *Wèi Shōu Dìxíng Zhì* (魏收地形志) mentions Lǒngdōng Commandery,
which administered Jīngyáng (涇陽), Zǔlì (祖厲), and Fǔyí (撫夷) three counties.
It does not record the beginning of its establishment,
so it was probably set up by Fú (苻) or Yáo (姚).
The Western Wèi (西魏) established Lǒngdōng at Qiānyuán (汧源),
which is modern Táng (唐) Lǒngzhōu.
Sǒ Líng (索稜), the Tàicháng (太常), was appointed Tàiwèi (太尉) and concurrently Lǒngxī Nèishǐ (隴西內史),
and instructed to recruit and pacify Western Qín.
This was to lay the groundwork for Sǒ Líng's surrender to Western Qín.
The character '索' (suǒ)
is pronounced as 'xīgè' (昔各).
He apologized and requested surrender.
This refers to the prefects and administrators obtained last year when Nán'ān (南安), Luèyáng (略陽), and the various commanderies of Lǒngxī were captured.
The character '使' (shǐ)
is pronounced as 'shūlì' (疏吏).
The character '降' (jiàng)
is pronounced as 'hùjiāng' (戶江).
(He was appointed) Director of Various Affairs of the Mixed Barbarian Tribes, Grand General of the Expedition to the West, Governor of Hézhōu, Chányú, and King of Hénán.
Crown Prince Chìpán (熾磐) was appointed General Who Guards the West, Left Worthy King, and Duke of Píngchāng (平昌).
Xīng ordered his officials to search for and recommend worthy talents.
Liáng Xǐ (梁喜), Right Servant-at-Large, said:
"I have repeatedly received imperial edicts but have not yet found such persons.
This can be called a world lacking talent."
Xīng said:
"Since ancient times, when emperors and kings rose,
they never sought prime ministers from the past,
or waited for generals from the future.
They appointed talents according to the times,
and all were able to achieve good governance.
You yourself are not discerning in your selection;
how can you falsely accuse the four seas (the entire world)? "
All the officials were pleased.
Yáo Xīng's rebuke of Liáng Xǐ was indeed correct.
Who among the officials truly understood Xīng's intention and publicly praised the humble and obscure?
This is what is called pursuing an empty reputation without practical use.
3 Qín Yáo Xiáng (秦姚詳) was garrisoned at Xìngchéng (杏城) and
was besieged by Xià Wáng Bó-bó (夏王勃勃).
He fled south to Dàsū (大蘇).
Bó-bó (勃勃) dispatched Píngdōng Jiāngjūn Lù Yìgān (平東將軍鹿弈干) to pursue and decapitate him,
capturing all his troops.
Bó-bó (勃勃) then attacked Āndìng (安定) from the south,
defeating Shàngshū Yáng Fó-sōng (尚書楊佛嵩) at Qīngshí Běiyuán (青石北原),
and gaining the surrender of forty-five thousand of his men.
He advanced to attack Dōngxiāng (東鄉),
capturing it,
and relocating over three thousand households to Èrchéng (貳城).
Qín Zhènběi Cānjūn Wáng Mǎidé (秦鎮北參軍王買德) defected to Xià (夏).
Xià Wáng Bó-bó (夏王勃勃) asked him for a strategy to destroy Qín (秦).
Mǎidé (買德) said:
"Although Qín's (秦) virtue has declined,
its provincial garrisons are still strong.
I suggest we first accumulate strength and wait for the right moment."
Bó-bó (勃勃) appointed Mǎidé (買德) as Jūnshī Zhōnglángjiàng (軍師中郎將).
Mǎidé (買德) thus became a strategist for Xià (夏).
Before long,
he was garrisoned at Xìngchéng (杏城).
4 Liú Fān (劉藩), leading generals like Mèng Huáiyù (孟懷玉) and others, pursued Lú Xún (盧循) to Lǐngbiǎo (嶺表).
In the second month,
on the day Rénwǔ (壬午),
Huáiyù (懷玉) captured Shǐxīng (始興)
and beheaded Xú Dàofù (徐道覆).
5 Hénán Wáng Gān-guī (河南王乾歸) relocated over three thousand households of the Xiānbēi Púhún (鮮卑僕渾) tribe to Dùjiānchéng (度堅城).
Púhún's (僕渾) surrender to Gān-guī (乾歸) was recorded in the previous volume, previous year.
Dùjiānchéng (度堅城) was the Dùjiān Shānchéng (度堅山城) where Qǐfú Xiān (乞伏先) had established his capital.
Qǐfú Gān-guī (乞伏乾歸) had originally named his state Qín (秦),
so he established Qínxīng Jùn (秦興郡) at Dùjiān Shān (度堅山).
6 Jiāo Lǎng (焦朗) still held Gūzāng (姑臧).
Lǎng's (朗) holding of Gūzāng (姑臧) was recorded in the previous volume, previous year.
Lǎng (朗) was captured but pardoned.
His younger brother, Ná (拏), was appointed Qínzhōu Cìshǐ (秦州刺史)
and garrisoned at Gūzāng (姑臧).
Subsequently, an expedition was launched against Nánliáng (南涼),
besieging Lèdū (樂都).
It was not captured for thirty days.
Nánliáng Wáng Rǔtán (南涼王傉檀) offered his son Ānzhōu (安周) as a hostage,
and only then did the forces return.
7 Tǔyùhún Shùluògān (吐谷渾樹洛干) attacked Nánliáng (南涼)
and defeated Nánliáng Tàizǐ Hǔtái (南涼太子虎臺).
8 Nánliáng Wáng Rǔtán (南涼王傉檀) wished to attack Jǔqú Méngxùn (沮渠蒙遜) again.
Hánchuān Hùjūn Mèng Kǎi (邯川護軍孟愷) advised him, saying:
"Méngxùn (蒙遜) has newly annexed Gūzāng (姑臧),
and his fierce power is at its peak.
He cannot be attacked."
Rǔtán (傉檀) did not listen,
and advanced along five routes,
reaching Fānhé (番禾) and Tiáodiào (苕藋),
plundering over five thousand households before returning.
Jiāngjūn Qū Yòu (將軍屈右) said:
"Since we have now gained profit,
we should double our pace and withdraw our troops,
crossing the dangerous passes quickly.
Méngxùn (蒙遜) is skilled in warfare.
If his light forces arrive suddenly,
with a great enemy pressing from without
and the relocated households rebelling from within,
this is a perilous path."
Wèiwèi Yīlìyán (衞尉伊力延) said:
"They are infantry, we are cavalry;
our strengths are not comparable.
To double our pace and retreat now would show weakness,
and moreover, we would abandon our possessions.
This is not a good plan."
Soon after, in a dense fog, wind, and rain,
Méngxùn's (蒙遜) army arrived in full force,
and Rǔtán (傉檀) was defeated and fled.
Méngxùn (蒙遜) advanced and besieged Lèdū (樂都).
Rǔtán (傉檀) defended the city staunchly,
offering his son Rǎgān (染干) as a hostage to request peace,
whereupon Méngxùn (蒙遜) returned.
9 In the third month,
Liú Yù (劉裕) first received the titles of Tàiwèi (太尉) and Zhōngshū Jiān (中書監).
His addition as Tàiwèi (太尉) was recorded in the previous volume, fifth year.
His addition as Zhōngshū Jiān (中書監) was recorded in the sixth year.
Yīn Jǐngrén (殷景仁) of Chénjùn (陳郡) became Xíng Cānjūn (行參軍).
Xíng Cānjūn (行參軍) meant not yet being on the same rank as Cānjūnshì (參軍事);
the note for this has already appeared earlier.
"Among Mèng Chǎng's (孟昶) subordinates, who is suitable to enter my office?"
Mùzhī (穆之) recommended Xiè Huì (謝晦),
former Jiànwēi Zhōngbīng Cānjūn (建威中兵參軍).
Huì (晦) was the great-grandson of Ān (安)'s brother Jù (據).
Mèng Chǎng (孟昶) was Jiànwēi Jiāngjūn (建威將軍)
and appointed Huì (晦) as Zhōngbīng Cānjūn (中兵參軍).
Yù (裕) once interrogated a prisoner.
That morning, the Xíngyù Cānjūn (刑獄參軍) was ill,
so Huì (晦) replaced him.
He glanced through the interrogation records in the carriage
and promptly ordered the proceedings to begin.
The prime minister's office had many affairs,
and the prisons were packed.
Huì (晦) responded and reasoned with every question,
making no errors.
Yù (裕) was thus impressed by him
and immediately appointed him Xíngyù Zéicáo (刑獄賊曹).
The Xíngyù (刑獄) department was probably divided into Míncáo (民曹) and Zéicáo (賊曹).
Zéicáo (賊曹) managed matters of theft and banditry.
The Sòng Zhì (宋志) states that the various government offices had Cānjūn (參軍) positions such as Chángliú Zéicáo (長流賊曹), Xíngyù Zéicáo (刑獄賊曹), and Chéngjú Zéicáo (城局賊曹).
There was no Míncáo (民曹) for Xíngyù (刑獄).
When Xiè Huì (謝晦) was Cānjūn (參軍),
he did not yet hold a departmental post;
now he was promoted to an appointment.
He was good at humor,
broad and well-versed in many things,
and Yù (裕) greatly appreciated and admired him.
10 Lú Xún (盧循) gathered troops as he reached Pānyú (番禺),
then besieged it.
Sūn Chǔ (孫處) resisted for over twenty days.
Shěn Tiánzǐ (沈田子) spoke to Liú Fān (劉藩), saying:
"Although Pānyú City (番禺城) is strategically strong,
it is originally the rebels' lair.
Now that Xún (循) is besieging it,
there might be an internal change.
Moreover, Sūn Jìgāo (孫季高)'s forces are weak.
Sūn Chǔ (孫處)'s courtesy name was Jìgāo (季高).
If the rebels regain control of Guǎngzhōu (廣州),
their fierce power will be revived."
In the summer,
the fourth month,
Tiánzǐ (田子) led his troops to relieve Pānyú (番禺),
attacking Xún (循)
and defeating him,
killing over ten thousand people.
Xún (循) fled.
Tiánzǐ (田子) and Chǔ (處) pursued him together,
and again defeated Xún (循) at Cāngwú (蒼梧), Yùlín (鬱林), and Níngpǔ (寧浦).
Cāngwú (蒼梧) and Yùlín (鬱林) were ancient Hàn (漢) commanderies.
Níngpǔ Jùn (寧浦郡) was established by Wú (吳) by dividing Hépǔ Jùn (合浦郡).
Cāngwú (蒼梧) was Táng's (唐) Yùzhōu (鬱州);
Yùlín (鬱林) was Táng's (唐) Yùlínzhōu (鬱林州);
Níngpǔ (寧浦) was Táng's (唐) Héngzhōu (橫州).
Unable to advance,
Xún (循) fled to Jiāozhōu (交州).
Initially,
the Grand Administrator of Jiǔzhēn, Lǐ Xùn, rebelled.
Jiǔzhēn
was an ancient Hàn commandery,
and in the Táng dynasty, it was Àizhōu.
Yuàn died,
and the imperial court appointed his son, Huìdù, as the Inspector of Jiāozhōu.
Before the imperial edict arrived,
Xún raided and captured Hépǔ.
Hépǔ
was an ancient Hàn commandery,
and in the Táng dynasty, it was Liánzhōu.
Huìdù led the civil and military officials of the prefecture to resist Xún at Shíqí
and defeated him.
Xún's remaining forces still numbered three thousand men.
Lǐ Xùn's remaining followers, Lǐ Tuō and others, gathered over five thousand Líláo people to join Xún.
On the day of Gēngzǐ,
Xún arrived at the southern ford of Lóngbiān at dawn.
Lóngbiān County in Jiāozhǐ Commandery
was where both the prefecture and commandery governments were located.
*Shuǐjīng Zhù* states: In the 23rd year of Jiàn'ān of Hàn,
at the beginning of the establishment of the prefecture,
a flood dragon coiled and intertwined (pán biān) between the north and south fords of the river,
hence Lóngyuān was changed to Lóngbiān.
I note that both *Èr Hàn Zhì* (Records of the Two Hàn Dynasties) refer to it as
"Lóngbiān."
Perhaps Shīgǔ and Zhānghuái also avoided the Táng taboo
and consequently changed
"yuān"
to
"biān"?
Huìdù engaged Xún in battle,
throwing pheasanth-tailed torches to burn his ships.
A pheasanth-tailed torch
was a bundle of straw, one end
fitted with an iron point,
the straw at the other end fanning out like a pheasant's tail.
Fire was set to it and then thrown at the enemy.
"Jiàn"
is pronounced Hù'àn.
All of Xún's ships caught fire,
and his forces suffered a great defeat.
Xún knew he could not escape,
so he first poisoned his wife and children.
He then summoned his courtesans and concubines and asked,
"Who among you is willing to die with me?"
Many said,
"Even sparrows and mice cling to life; it is truly difficult to face death."
Others said,
"Even the lord must die; how could I wish to live!"
He then killed all those who refused to die
and subsequently threw himself into the water.
Huìdù retrieved his body and beheaded him.
Together with the heads of his son and Lǐ Tuō and others,
seven heads were boxed and sent to Jiànkāng.
11 Initially,
Liú Yì was in Jīngkǒu,
impoverished.
He was practicing archery with acquaintances in the Eastern Hall.
Yú Yuè, who was the Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works,
arrived later
and took over their archery hall.
Everyone else made way for him,
but Yì alone did not leave.
Yuè's feast was very lavish,
but he did not offer any to Yì.
Yì asked Yuè for roasted goose,
but Yuè angrily refused to give it.
From this, Yì harbored resentment towards him.
By this time,
Yì requested to also supervise Jiāngzhōu,
and an imperial edict granted his request.
He then memorialized, stating:
"Jiāngzhōu is an interior region;
its duty is to govern the people.
A military headquarters should not be established there, wasting the people's resources.
It is appropriate to abolish the military headquarters and move the garrison to Yùzhāng.
However, Xúnyáng borders barbarian tribes,
so one thousand soldiers from the prefecture and commandery may be stationed there to assist the郡 garrison."
Thereupon, Yuè was relieved of his supervisory and general's posts,
and as Inspector, he was garrisoned in Yùzhāng.
Yì appointed his trusted general Zhào Huī to lead one thousand soldiers to guard Xúnyáng.
All three thousand civil and military officials under Yuè were transferred to Yì's command.
The summons and management were strict.
"Fúshè" means to issue a summons to Jiāngzhōu to arrest and take into custody.
Upon arriving in Yùzhāng,
Yuè died from a carbuncle on his back.
12 Qífú Gān’guī, the Prince of Hénán, relocated Qíang Jùqǐ and other tribal groups, over five thousand households, to Diélánchéng.
Jùqǐ's surrender to Gān’guī is mentioned in the previous volume, last year.
Diélánchéng is southwest of Dàxià and
northeast of Kāngliáo.
At the end of the Hàn dynasty,
Āguì, the Di king of Xìngguó, occupied Xìngguóchéng,
which was within the borders of Luèyáng Commandery.
Qífú used its place name to establish a commandery.
He again appointed his son, Mùyìgān, as the Grand Administrator of Wǔwēi,
garrisoned in Kāngliáochéng.
Kāngliáochéng
was built in the fourth year
by Qífú Chìpán.
"Fù"
is pronounced Fúyòu.
13 On the day of Dīngmǎo,
Tuòbá Sì, the Ruler of Wèi, visited Jīnlíng,
and Xī Jīn, the Marquis of Shānyáng, remained to guard the capital.
Mùróng Bó'ér, the Prince of Chānglí, plotted rebellion.
On the day of Jǐsì,
Xī Jīn, along with his confederates, captured and executed him.
14 In the autumn,
in the seventh month, Yàn Wáng Bà appointed Crown Prince Yǒng as the Grand Chányú
and established four assistants (sì fǔ).
The appointment of a Crown Prince as Grand Chányú began in the Liú Hàn dynasty,
at which time only the Left and Right Assistants were established.
Bà added the Front Assistant and Rear Assistant.
"Dān"
is pronounced Chán.
Húlǜ, the Khagan of Ròurán, sent an envoy to present three thousand horses to Bà.
"Kě"
is pronounced with the entering tone of kān.
"Hán"
is pronounced with the tone of Hán.
"Shǐ"
is pronounced Shūlì.
Bà ordered his close ministers to discuss it.
Sùfú, the Duke of Liáoxī, said:
"In previous generations, imperial kinswomen were given in marriage to the Six Barbarian tribes.
It is appropriate to promise him the daughter of a concubine.
Princess Lèlàng should not be married down to a non-kindred person."
Bà said:
"I am currently promoting trust with various foreign peoples;
how can I deceive them!"
So, he gave Princess Lèlàng in marriage to him.
Bà was diligent in governance,
encouraged agriculture and sericulture,
reduced corvée labor,
and lightened taxes.
Whenever he dispatched governors or magistrates,
he would personally grant them an audience,
inquire about the essentials of governance,
to observe their abilities.
The people of Yàn were pleased with him.
15 Qífú Gān’guī, the Prince of Hénán, dispatched Chìpán, the Duke of Píngchāng, and Shěnqián, the General of the Central Army, to attack Nánliáng.
Shěnqián was Gān’guī's son.
In the eighth month,
Chìpán's army crossed the river.
This refers to crossing the Jīnchéng River.
"Chì"
is pronounced Chāngzhì.
The Nánliáng army was defeated,
and over one hundred thousand cattle and horses were captured before returning.
16 Jǔqú Méngxùn led light cavalry to attack Xīliáng.
Gǎo, the Duke of Xīliáng, said:
"There are battles where the enemy is defeated without fighting,
by blunting their銳气.
Méngxùn has just allied with us;
the details are in the previous volume, last year.
If I close the gates and do not fight him,
waiting until his锐气 is exhausted to strike,
there is no doubt we will be victorious."
After a short while,
Méngxùn's provisions ran out, and he returned.
Gǎo sent Crown Prince Xīn to lead seven thousand cavalry to ambush him.
Méngxùn was greatly defeated,
and his general, Jǔqú Bǎinián, was captured.
17 Qífú Gān’guī, the Prince of Hénán, attacked Yáo Lóng, the Grand Administrator of Luèyáng of Qín, at Báiyángbǎo
and captured it.
In the winter, eleventh month,
he advanced to attack Wáng Jǐng, the Grand Administrator of Nánpíng, at Shuǐluòchéng.
*Shuǐjīng Zhù* states: Shuǐluòtíng is west of Lǒngshān,
within the boundaries of Hàn Luèyáng County.
Zhèng Jiǎn said: Shuǐluòchéng is located to the west of the strategic Lǒngdǐ, a thoroughfare connecting to Qínzhōu.
Two rivers of Lǒng encircle the city, flowing west,
winding around the Wèihé.
The plains are flat and the soil fertile,
extending for several hundred *lǐ*.
*Yuánfēng Jiǔyù Zhì* states: One hundred *lǐ* southwest of Déshùnjūn is Shuǐluòchéng,
built by Liú Hù, who was dispatched by Zhèng Jiǎn during the Rénzōng Emperor's reign.
"Jǐng"
is pronounced Jūyǒng.
He relocated over three thousand households to Tánjiāo.
Tánjiāo is northwest of the administrative city.
In the twelfth month,
Péng Lìfà, a Western Qiāng, raided and occupied Fāohǎn,
declaring himself Grand General and Governor of Hézhōu.
Gān’guī attacked him
but failed to defeat him.
18 In this year,
Liú Dàolián, the Inspector of Bìngzhōu, became the Inspector of Běixúzhōu
and moved his garrison to Péngchéng.
1 In spring,
in the first month,
Hénán Wáng Qián-guī again campaigned against Péng Lì-fà,
reaching Núkuí Gǔ.
Lì-fà abandoned his forces and fled south.
Qián-guī dispatched Zhènwēi Jiāngjūn Qǐfú Gōng-fǔ to pursue him to Qīngshuǐ,
where he was beheaded.
Thirteen thousand Qiāng households were brought in.
Qǐfú Shěn-qián was made Hézhōu Cìshǐ,
stationed at Páohǎn, and then Qián-guī returned.
2 In the second month,
on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Kǒng Jìng, the Grand Administrator of Wúxīng, was appointed Shàngshū Yòu Púyè.
3 Hénán Wáng Qián-guī moved his capital to Tánjiāo,
and ordered Píngchāng Gōng Chì-pán to be stationed at Yuànchuān.
Qián-guī attacked Tǔyùhún Ā Ruò-gān at Chìshuǐ
and subjugated them.
The Wǔdài Zhì states: In the fifth year of Dàyè of the Suí dynasty, Tǔyùhún was pacified,
and Héyuán Jùn was established at the ancient Chìshuǐ Chéng,
which is near Jīshí Shān.
Wèi Shōu's Dìxíng Zhì states: Líntáo Jùn has Chìshuǐ Xiàn.
The Shuǐjīng Zhù states: Chìshuǐ Chéng is also called Líntáo Dōngchéng.
"Jiàng" (subjugate),
Hù Jiāng fān.
4 In summer,
in the fourth month,
Liú Dào-guī requested to return due to illness,
which was granted.
Dào-guī had been in Jīngzhōu for many years;
in the first year,
Dào-guī was Cìshǐ of Jīngzhōu.
When he returned,
the government storehouses and ceremonial curtains
were all exactly as they had been.
When two armored guards accompanying him moved a mat onto his boat,
Dào-guī had them executed in the marketplace.
Yǐhòu Jiāngjūn Yùzhōu Cìshǐ Liú Yì was made Wèi Jiāngjūn, Dūdū of Jīng, Níng, Qín, and Yōng four prefectures' military affairs, and Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ.
Yì said to Zuǒwèi Jiāngjūn Liú Jìng-xuān:
"I am honored with the western post,
and wish to trouble you to be Changshǐ for Nánmán,
meaning Changshǐ of the Nánmán Xiàowèi Fǔ."
Jìng-xuān was afraid
and reported this to Tàiwèi Yù.
Yù laughed and said:
"Just let my elder brother be safe,
and there will surely be no cause for worry."
Yì was by nature headstrong and self-important.
He considered his achievements in the righteous uprising to be on par with Yù's,
and was deeply conceited.
Although he nominally deferred to Yù in matters of power, his heart did not submit;
this can be seen from his words to his younger brother Fán last year.
He was often discontented and unfulfilled.
Yù always treated him gently and compliantly,
which only made Yì's arrogance and indulgence worse.
He once said:
"I regret not having met Liú Bāng or Xiàng Yǔ,
to contend with them for the Central Plains!"
After his defeat at Sāngluò,
which is documented in the sixth year of the previous volume,
he became even more agitated.
Yù was uneducated,
while Yì was quite learned and cultured.
Therefore, many court officials with good reputations gravitated towards him,
and he formed deep alliances with Shàngshū Púyè Xiè Hùn
and Dānyáng Yǐn Xī Sēng-shī.
Sēng-shī
was Chāo's collateral nephew.
As Yì now held the upper reaches of the river,
he secretly harbored ambitions to overthrow Yù.
He sought to concurrently oversee Jiāo and Guǎng two prefectures,
which Yù granted.
Yì also memorialized to appoint Xī Sēng-shī as Nánmán Xiàowèi Hòujūn Sīmǎ
and Máio Xiū-zhī as Nánjùn Tàishǒu.
Yù also granted these appointments,
and appointed Liú Mù-zhī to replace Sēng-shī as Dānyáng Yǐn.
Yì requested permission to visit Jīngkǒu to pay respects at his ancestors' tombs.
Yù went to meet him at Nítáng.
Níngyuǎn Jiāngjūn Hú Fán said to Yù:
"Do you think Wèi Jiāngjūn Liú will ultimately remain beneath you?"
Yì was Wèi Jiāngjūn,
hence the稱.
After a long pause,
Yù said:
"What do you think?"
Fán replied:
"He leads millions of troops,
conquers whenever he attacks,
and wins whenever he fights;
Yì respects you for this.
As for his dabbling in records and biographies,
Shīgǔ said: 'Dabbling' (涉),
like wading in water;
'hunting' (獵),
like hunting beasts;
meaning to read through,
not to specialize.
'Chuán' (傳),
Zhí Liàn fān.
he considers himself a heroic figure;
because of this, many literati and scholars flock to him.
I fear he will never remain beneath you.
It would be better to take advantage of this meeting to deal with him."
Yù said:
"Yì and I both have achievements in restoring order.
His transgressions are not yet apparent,
so we cannot plot against each other."
Although Yù answered Fán with these words,
he secretly had a plan for how to handle Yì.
5 Qǐfú Chì-pán attacked Wú Yīn, the Grand Administrator of Sānhé for Southern Liáng, at Báitǔ,
conquered it,
and replaced him with Qǐfú Chū-lěi.
The Shuǐjīng states: The Yellow River flows south of Hánchuān Chéng,
then east past the north of Línjīn Chéng and south of Báitǔ Chéng.
Kàn Yīn's Shísānzhōu Zhì states: Sixty lǐ west of Zuǒnánjīn,
there is Báitǔ Chéng,
which is north of the Great River,
and serves as a crossing point along the river.
"Lěi" (累),
Lì Zhuī fān.
Wèi Shōu states: Báitǔ Xiàn,
in the Hàn dynasty belonged to Shàngjùn,
in the Jìn dynasty belonged to Jīnchéng Jùn,
and in the Later Wèi dynasty belonged to Xīnpíng Jùn.
I contend that the Báitǔ of Later Wèi Xīnpíng is the Báitǔ of Hàn Shàngjùn,
and the Báitǔ of Jìn Jīnchéng is the Báitǔ west of Zuǒnán,
each being a distinct place.
The Wǔdài Zhì states: Bīnzhōu Xīnpíng Xiàn,
formerly called Báitǔ, this is the Báitǔ of Hàn Shàngjùn and Later Wèi.
The Báitǔ of Southern Liáng should be within the bounds of Táng Shànzhōu.
In the sixth month,
Qǐfú Gōng-fǔ assassinated Hénán Wáng Qián-guī.
Gōng-fǔ
was Guórén's son;
because he was not made heir,
he committed the assassination.
He fled to secure Dàxià.
Píngchāng Gōng Chì-pán dispatched his younger brother Guǎngwǔ Jiāngjūn Zhì-dá and Yángwǔ Jiāngjūn Mù Yì-gān leading three thousand cavalry to attack him.
He appointed his younger brother Tán-dá as Zhèn Jīng
Jiāngjūn,
stationed at Tánjiāo.
Qǐfú made Tánjiāo their capital,
calling it the imperial capital,
hence the establishment of Zhèn Jīng Jiāngjūn to guard it.
"Shuài" (帥),
read as 'lǜ'.
Qí Jì fān;
same below.
"Tán" (曇),
Tú Hán fān.
Chì-pán led civil and military officials and over twenty thousand households of commoners to relocate to Páohǎn.
Many Qín people advised Qín Wáng Xīng to take advantage of the chaos to seize Chì-pán.
Xīng said:
"Attacking during someone's mourning
is against propriety."
Xià Wáng Bóbó wanted to attack Chì-pán.
Jūnshī Zhōnglángjiāng Wáng Mǎi-dé admonished him:
"Chì-pán
is our allied state.
Now that they are suffering from loss and chaos,
we cannot sympathize with them,
and instead rely on our strength to attack them.
Even an ordinary man would be ashamed to do so,
let alone a ruler of ten thousand chariots!"
Bóbó then ceased his plans.
6 In the intercalary month,
on the day Gēngzǐ,
Nánjùn Lièwǔ Gōng Liú Dào-guī passed away.
7 In autumn,
in the seventh month,
on the first day, Jǐsì,
Wèi Zhǔ Sì made an eastern tour.
He appointed Four-Flank Great Generals and Twelve Junior Generals.
Xī Jīn, the Marquis of Shānyáng, and Tuòbá Qū, the Marquis of Yuánchéng, were appointed acting Left and Right Chéngxiàng.
Xī Jīn was enfeoffed as Marquis of Shānyáng;
Tuòbá Qū was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuánchéng.
On the day Gēngyín,
Sì arrived at Rúrén,
touring the northwestern tribes.
8 Qǐfú Zhì-dá and others defeated Qǐfú Gōng-fǔ at Dàxià.
Gōng-fǔ fled to Diélán Chéng
to join his younger brother Ā-chái.
Zhì-dá and others attacked and captured it,
beheading Ā-chái and his five sons.
Gōng-fǔ fled to Kāngyàn Nánshān,
where he was pursued and captured,
along with his four sons.
They were dismembered at Tánjiāo.
In the eighth month,
Qǐfú Chì-pán proclaimed himself Dàjiāngjūn and Hénán Wáng.
Chì-pán
was Qián-guī's eldest son.
He changed the era name to Yǒngkāng.
He buried Qián-guī at Páohǎn,
giving him the posthumous title Wǔyuán
and temple name Gāozǔ.
9 Empress Wáng Shì passed away.
On the 10th day of the *gēngxū* (庚戌) cycle,
the Wèi (魏) ruler Sì (嗣) returned to Píngchéng (平城).
He had been on a tour and was now back.
In the 11th month,
Hénán (河南) King Chìpán (熾磐) appointed Wǔshǐ (武始) Zhái Qíng (翟勍), the *Shàngshū Lìng* (尚書令), as *Xiàngguó* (相國).
Shì Zhòng (侍中) and *Tàizǐ Zhānshì* (太子詹事) Zhào Jǐng (趙景) was appointed *Yùshǐ Dàfū* (御史大夫).
The offices of *Shàngshū Lìng* (尚書令), *Pú* (僕), *Shàngshū Liùqīng* (尚書六卿), and *Shì Zhòng* (侍中) were abolished.
On the 12th day of the *guǐyǒu* (癸酉) cycle,
Empress Xī (僖) was buried at Xiūpíng Líng (休平陵).
Liú Yì (劉毅) arrived in Jiānglíng (江陵),
making many changes to the provincial and district administrators.
He also arbitrarily took over ten thousand civilian and military personnel from Yùzhōu (豫州) and soldiers from Jiāngzhōu (江州) to accompany him.
At this time, Yì (毅) fell gravely ill.
Xī Sēngshī (郗僧施) and others feared Yì's (毅) death,
which would endanger his faction.
So they advised Yì (毅) to invite his cousin Fān (藩), the *Yǎnzhōu Cìshǐ* (兗州刺史), to be his deputy.
Grand Commandant Yù (裕) pretended to agree.
Fān (藩) came to the capital from Guǎnglíng (廣陵).
On the *jǐmǎo* (己卯) day,
Yù (裕) issued an imperial edict detailing Yì's (毅) crimes,
stating that he had conspired with Fān (藩) and Xiè Hùn (謝混) to rebel.
Fān (藩) and Hùn (混) were arrested and given death.
Initially, Hùn (混) and Liú Yì (劉毅) were very close.
Hùn's (混) elder cousin Dàn (澹) was always worried about this and gradually distanced himself from Hùn (混).
He said to his brother Pú (璞) and nephew Zhān (瞻):
"Yìshòu's (益壽) nature
will eventually ruin his family."
Yìshòu (益壽)
was Hùn's (混) childhood name.
He was the grandson of Ān (安).
On the *gēngchén* (庚辰) day,
an imperial edict proclaimed a general amnesty.
Sīmǎ Xiūzhī (司馬休之), formerly *Kuàijī Nèishǐ* (會稽內史), was appointed *Dūdū Jīng‧Yōng‧Liáng‧Qín‧Níng‧Yì Liùzhōu Zhūjūnshì* (都督荊‧雍‧梁‧秦‧寧‧益六州諸軍事) and *Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ* (荊州刺史).
Liú Dàolián (劉道憐), *Běixúzhōu Cìshǐ* (北徐州刺史), was appointed *Yǎn‧Qīng Èrzhōu Cìshǐ* (兗‧青二州刺史),
stationed at Jīngkǒu (京口).
The *Běixúzhōu Cìshǐ* (北徐州 Cìshǐ) usually governed from Péngchéng (彭城).
By stationing Dàolián (道憐) at Jīngkǒu (京口),
it was intended to serve as a crucial northern bulwark for Jiànkāng (建康).
Yù (裕) suspected that Chángmín (長民) could not be left alone,
so he appointed Liú Mùzhī (劉穆之) as *Jiànwǔ Jiāngjūn* (建武將軍),
assigning him aides and providing him with resources
to guard against Chángmín (長民).
At this time, Yù (裕) already had the intention of killing Chángmín (長民).
On the *rénwǔ* (壬午) day, Yù (裕) led his armies from Jiànkāng (建康).
His staff officer Wáng Zhèn'è (王鎮惡) requested a hundred boats to serve as the vanguard.
On the *bǐngshēn* (丙申) day,
they arrived at Gūshú (姑孰).
Zhèn'è (鎮惡) was appointed *Zhènnwǔ Jiāngjūn* (振武將軍).
He and *Lóngxiáng Jiāngjūn* (龍驤將軍) Kuí Ēn (蒯恩) led a hundred boats ahead.
Yù (裕) instructed them:
"If the enemy can be attacked,
attack them;
if not,
burn their ships,
and hold a position by the water's edge to await me."
Thereupon, Zhèn'è (鎮惡) traveled day and night,
spreading rumors that Governor Liú of Yǎnzhōu (兗州) had arrived.
In winter, the 10th month,
on the *jǐwèi* (己未) day,
Zhèn'è (鎮惡) reached Yùzhāngkǒu (豫章口),
twenty *lǐ* (里) from Jiānglíng (江陵) city.
They abandoned their boats and proceeded on foot.
Kuí Ēn's (蒯恩) army was in the front,
followed by Zhèn'è (鎮惡).
They left one or two men with the boats,
and placed six or seven flags on the bank by the boats.
Drums were placed under the flags.
They told the remaining men:
"When you estimate that we have reached the city,
beat the drums loudly
to make it seem like a large army is behind us."
"Beating the drums loudly"
means beating the drums.
Zhèn'è (鎮惡) advanced directly to assault the city.
He told the soldiers in the vanguard:
He told the soldiers in the vanguard.
"If anyone asks,
just say that Governor Liú of Yǎnzhōu (兗州) has arrived."
The garrisons at the ferry and the common people were all calm and unsuspecting.
About five or six *lǐ* (里) before reaching the city,
they met Zhū Xiǎnzī (朱顯之), a trusted general of Yì (毅).
A trusted general
refers to a close general
who commanded important troops.
He asked:
"Where is Governor Liú of Yǎnzhōu (兗州)?"
The soldiers replied:
"He is behind."
Xiǎnzī (顯之) went to the rear of the army but did not see Fān (藩).
Instead, he saw soldiers carrying *péngpái* (彭排) battle equipment.
*Péngpái* (彭排)
is the *pángpái* (旁排) of today,
used to ward off spearheads and arrows.
Sūn Mǐn (孫愐) said: *Lù* (樐)
is *péngpái* (彭排).
*Shìmíng* (釋名) says: *Péngpái* (彭排)
is a military implement.
*Péng* (彭)
means *páng* (旁),
used to line up and repel the enemy's attack.
The sound of the drums beating loudly was very intense.
Realizing that it was not Fān (藩) arriving,
he immediately spurred his horse and galloped away,
informing Yì (毅) to order the closing of all city gates.
Zhèn'è (鎮惡) also charged forward.
Before the gates could be locked,
his soldiers were able to enter the city.
Xiè Chún (謝純), *Wèijūn Chángshǐ* (衞軍長史), entered to attend to Yì (毅).
Officials of the provincial government referred to it as attending.
Yì's (毅) attendants wanted to pull his carriage away.
Chún (純) shouted at them:
"I
am a public servant."
Meaning he was an official for the people.
He galloped back into the office.
Chún (純)
was the grandson of Ān's (安) brother Jù (據).
Zhèn'è (鎮惡) fought with the city's defenders
and attacked the inner city (Jīnchéng 金城).
Any inner walled city
during the Jìn (晉) and Sòng (宋) dynasties was called Jīnchéng (金城).
The hour *shēn* (申) becomes *bū* (晡).
Mid-*bū* (晡)
is precisely the *shēn* (申) hour.
The end of *shēn* (申) is late *bū* (晡).
Zhèn'è (鎮惡) dug through the Jīnchéng (金城) and entered.
He sent someone to show Yì (毅) the imperial edict, the amnesty document, and Yù's (裕) personal letter.
Yì (毅) burned them all without looking
and, with *Sīmǎ* (司馬) Máo Xiūzhī (毛脩之) and others, commanded his troops to fight fiercely.
The people inside the city still did not believe Yù (裕) had come himself.
Soldiers who had come with Yì (毅) from the east
had many relatives by marriage or blood among the imperial army.
As they fought and conversed,
they learned that Yù (裕) had indeed come.
Public morale plummeted.
By nightfall,
all the soldiers in the front hall had dispersed.
Yì's (毅) brave general Zhào Cài (趙蔡) was beheaded.
Yì's (毅) remaining soldiers still barricaded the east and west side gates and resisted.
Fearing that they might accidentally injure each other in the darkness,
Zhèn'è (鎮惡) withdrew his troops, surrounded the Jīnchéng (金城),
and left its southern side open.
Yì (毅) feared there were ambushes to the south.
In the middle of the night,
he led about three hundred of his attendants
and burst out through the north gate.
Máo Xiūzhī (毛脩之) said to Xiè Chún (謝純):
"You just follow me."
Chún (純) did not comply
and was killed by someone.
That night, Yì (毅) sought refuge at Niúmù Fósì (牛牧佛寺).
Niúmù Sì (牛牧寺) was twenty *lǐ* (里) north of Jiānglíng (江陵) city.
When Huán Wèizhī (桓蔚之) was defeated,
the account can be found in Volume 114, First Year.
*Wèi* (蔚) is pronounced *yūwù*.
Chāng (昌) had hidden him,
but Yì (毅) killed Chāng (昌).
Now,
the temple monk refused him, saying:
"Our former master harbored Huán Wèi (桓蔚)
and was killed by Garrison General Liú (劉).
We truly dare not harbor another person."
Yì (毅) sighed, saying:
"To be undone by one's own laws
has come to this!"
The *Shǐjì* (史記) states that Shāng Jūn (商君), having offended Qín (秦),
fled to Guānxià (關下) and wished to stay at an inn.
The innkeeper, not knowing he was Shāng Jūn (商君),
said:
"According to Shāng Jūn's (商君) law,
innkeepers who fail to verify guests are to be punished."
Shāng Jūn (商君) sighed, saying:
"Alas!
To be undone by one's own laws,
it has come to this!"
The next day,
a resident reported him,
and he was beheaded in the marketplace.
His sons and nephews were also executed.
Yì's (毅) elder brother Mó (模) fled to Xiāngyáng (襄陽), but Lǔ Zōngzhī (魯宗之) beheaded him and sent his head.
Initially,
Yì's maternal uncle Zhènzhī lived in leisure at Jīngkǒu,
not responding to invitations for office.
He often said to Yì and Fān:
"Your talents and capacities
are sufficient to achieve your ambitions,
but I fear it will not last long.
I do not seek wealth or position from you,
nor will I share in your future suffering."
Whenever he saw Yì and Fān arrive at his door with an entourage,
he would scold them.
Yì respected and feared him greatly.
Hundreds of paces before reaching the residence,
he would dismiss all his guards and retinue,
and advance with only a few men in plain clothes.
After Yì's death,
Grand Commandant Yù memorialized to summon Zhènzhī as a Sanqí Chángshì and Guānglù Dàfū.
散 (sǎn),
is pronounced dàn.
騎 (qí),
is pronounced jījì.
14 Gōng Yáng Shèng of Chóuchí rebelled against Qín.
In the first year of Yìxī (405 CE),
Shèng surrendered to Qín;
now he has rebelled again.
Qín King Xīng dispatched Jiànwēi Jiāngjūn Zhào Kūn as the vanguard,
Lìjié Jiāngjūn Yáo Bóshòu to follow him,
Qián Jiāngjūn Yáo Huī to emerge from Jùxiá,
Qínzhōu Cìshǐ Yáo Sōng from Yángtóuxiá,
and Yòuwèi Jiāngjūn Hú Yìdù from Qīanchéng,
to attack Shèng.
Xīng himself went from Yōng to the front,
meeting his generals at Lǒngkǒu.
This refers to the mouth of the Lǒng path.
將 (jiāng),
is pronounced jíliàng.
The Grand Administrator of Tiānshuǐ, Wáng Sōnghū, said to Sōng:
"The late Emperor's divine strategy was boundless.
Xú Luòshēng, with his heroic martial prowess, assisted in establishing the dynasty,
twice entered Chóuchí,
but returned without success.
Yáo Cháng attacked Chóuchí twice,
this needs to be verified.
It is simply because the terrain is steep and fortified.
Now, with Zhào Kūn's forces and your Excellency's prestige,
compared to previous dynasties,
success has truly not been seen.
Your Excellency fully understands the situation;
why not report it?"
Sōng did not heed him.
Shèng led his troops and held Zhào Kūn in check.
Bóshòu, being timid and cowardly, did not advance.
Kūn's forces, outnumbered,
were defeated by Shèng.
Xīng executed Bóshòu and returned.
Xīng appointed Yáng Fósōng as Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ,
to lead the available troops north of the ridge to attack Xià.
Qín's Yōngzhōu governed five commanderies north of the ridge, with its seat at Āndìng.
見 (jiàn),
is pronounced xiánpiàn.
Xīng said to his ministers:
"Fósōng, whenever he encounters an enemy,
cannot control his bravery.
I always limited his troops to no more than five thousand men.
Now that he leads a large force,
he will surely be defeated if he encounters the enemy.
He has already gone far,
and it is too late to recall him.
What should be done?"
Fósōng fought against Xià King Bóbó,
and was indeed defeated,
captured by Bóbó,
and died by having his throat cut.
15 Qín established Lady Qí, a Zhāoyí, as Empress.
16 Jǔqú Méngxùn moved to Gūzāng.
17 In the eleventh month,
on the day Jǐmǎo,
Grand Commandant Yù arrived at Jiānglíng
and killed Xī Sēngshī.
Initially,
Máo Xiūzhī, although an aide to Liú Yì,
had secretly allied himself with Yù,
so Yù specifically pardoned him.
Wáng Zhèn'è was granted the title Hànshòuzǐ.
Yù asked Yì's Administrator for Consultation, Shēn Yǒng:
"What can be done today?"
Yǒng replied:
"Remove old grudges,
double the benefactions,
and arrange appointments by family rank.
Since the Wèi and Jìn dynasties,
the order of appointments has generally been based on the eminence of family background.
'Arranging appointments' means arranging them in order,
like stringing coins together.
That is all."
Yù accepted this,
issued an order to reduce rents and levies,
restrict conscription and pardon punishments,
and courteously invite renowned scholars.
The people of Jīng were pleased.
18 Zhūgě Chángmín was arrogant, extravagant, and greedy.
Many of his actions were unlawful,
causing distress to the common people.
He constantly feared that Grand Commandant Yù would investigate him.
When Liú Yì was executed,
Chángmín said to his confidants:
"'Last year, Péng Yuè was minced;
this year, Hán Xìn was killed.'
This was the saying of Xuē Gōng of Hàn.
被 (pī),
is pronounced píyì.
He then privately asked Liú Mùzhī:
"Common rumors
all say that the Grand Commandant and I are not on good terms.
How did it come to this?"
Mùzhī replied:
"Your Excellency went on a distant campaign upriver,
entrusting your aged mother and young children to his Lordship.
If there were even a tiny bit of ill will,
how could this be possible?"
Chángmín's mind then became slightly at ease.
Chángmín's younger brother, Fǔguó Dàjiāngjūn Lí Mín, advised Chángmín:
"The fall of the Liú clan
is also a source of fear for the Zhūgě clan.
You should plan against Yù before he returns."
Chángmín hesitated and did not act.
Then he sighed:
"Those who are poor and humble always think of wealth and nobility;
those who are wealthy and noble inevitably face crises.
Today, if I wished to be a commoner of Dāntú,
how could it be possible?"
Chángmín was from Yángdū, Lángxié,
and resided in Dāntú as a migrant.
"Pánlóng was fierce, headstrong, and autocratic,
bringing about his own destruction.
Deviant elements are about to be eliminated,
and the world's path is becoming smooth.
Matters of wealth and nobility,
let us share them together."
Jìngxuān replied:
"Since Yìxī,
your subordinate has undeservedly held three prefectures and seven commanderies.
Jìngxuān, returning from the north,
was appointed Grand Administrator of Jìnlíng,
then moved to Jiāngzhōu,
garrisoned Xúnyáng,
concurrently administering the commandery,
was summoned and appointed Xuānchéng Nèishǐ,
concurrently Grand Administrator of Xiāngchéng,
then moved to Zhènmán Hùjūn,
Grand Administrator of Ānfēng,
Nèishǐ of Liángguó,
and again moved to Qīngzhōu Cìshǐ,
soon after changed to Jìzhōu.
I wish to avoid excess and dwell in humility.
The essence of wealth and nobility
is not something I dare to accept."
He also sent a letter to Yù.
Yù said:
"Āshòu indeed did not let me down."
Jìngxuān's
courtesy name was Wànshòu,
hence Yù called him Āshòu.
Liú Mùzhī worried that Chángmín would cause trouble.
He privately asked Grand Commandant's Administrator for Consultation, Hé Chéngtiān of Dōnghǎi:
"Will the Duke's journey today be successful?"
Chéngtiān replied:
"There is no need to worry that Jīngzhōu will not be decided in time.
'Decided'
means resolved.
When the Duke returned from Zuǒlǐ to Shítou in previous years,
it was quite casual;
this refers to the time he returned after defeating Lú Xún.
'Casual'
means returning without strict precautions.
It is advisable to be more cautious."
Mùzhī said:
"Without you,
I would not have heard these words."
While Yù was in Jiānglíng,
Fǔguó Jiāngjūn Wáng Dàn requested to return first.
Yù said:
"Zhūgě Chángmín seems to have suspicions about himself.
How could you leave now?"
Dàn replied:
"Chángmín knows that I am favored by your Lordship.
If I now return lightly and alone,
he will surely think there is no danger,
which might slightly put his mind at ease."
Yù smiled and said:
"Your bravery surpasses that of Bēn and Yù."
He then allowed him to return first.
19 Jǔqú Méngxùn (沮渠蒙遜) took the throne of the King of Héxī (河西).
Jǔqú Méngxùn (沮渠蒙遜)
was a Hú (胡) person from Línsōng Lúshuǐ (臨松盧水).
His ancestors were the Zuǒ Jǔqú (左沮渠) of the Xiōngnú (匈奴),
and thus adopted the official title as their surname.
He changed the era name to Xuánshǐ (玄始),
and appointed officials according to the precedent of Lǚ Guāng (呂光) as King of Sānhé (三河).
Lǚ Guāng (呂光) was proclaimed King of Sānhé (三河);
this is recorded in Volume 107, Xiàowǔ Tàiyuán (孝武太元) 14th year.
20 Tàiwèi (太尉) Yù (裕) planned to attack Shǔ (蜀),
but found it difficult to select a commander-in-chief.
As Xīyáng (西陽) Tàishǒu (太守) Zhū Língshí (朱齡石) possessed both military capability
and administrative experience,
Yù (裕) wished to employ him.
Everyone thought that Língshí’s (齡石) reputation and standing were too low
to undertake such an important responsibility;
but Yù (裕) did not agree.
In the twelfth month,
Língshí (齡石) was appointed Yìzhōu Cìshǐ (益州刺史),
and was dispatched to attack Shǔ (蜀) with Níngshuò Jiāngjūn (寧朔將軍) Zāng Xī (臧熹), Héjiān Tàishǒu (河間太守) Kuǎi Ēn (蒯恩), Xiàpéi Tàishǒu (下邳太守) Liú Zhōng (劉鍾) and others,
allocating half of the main army, twenty thousand men, to him.
Xī (熹),
Yù’s (裕) brother-in-law,
ranked higher than Língshí (齡石),
but was also subordinate to him.
Yù (裕) secretly discussed the advance with Língshí (齡石),
saying:
"Last year Liú Jìngxúān (劉敬宣) went out through Huánghǔ (黃虎),
but retreated without achieving anything.
This event is recorded in Volume 114, 4th year.
He expects us to come from the inner water, taking him by surprise.
Yǔ Zhōngyōng (庾仲雍) said: Bājùn Jiāngzhōu (巴郡江州) County faces two river mouths,
the right is Fú (涪), the inner water;
the left is Shǔ (蜀), the outer water.
He will certainly use heavy forces to guard Fúchéng (涪城) to defend the inner route.
If we head towards Huánghǔ (黃虎), we will fall right into his trap.
Now, we will take the main force through the outer water to seize Chéngdū (成都),
while making a feint through the inner water;
this is a brilliant stratagem to defeat the enemy."
However, fearing that this plan would be known in advance,
and the enemy would discern the truth,
Yù (裕) separately sealed a letter and gave it to Língshí (齡石),
writing on the side of the envelope:
"Do not open until you reach Báidì (白帝)."
Although the various armies advanced,
they did not know the details of the disposition.
Máo Xiūzhī (毛脩之) strongly requested to go;
but Yù (裕) feared that upon reaching Shǔ (蜀), Xiūzhī (脩之) would execute many people,
and the local populace, having a grudge against the Máo (毛) clan,
would fight to the death to protect themselves,
so he did not permit it.
This was because Máo Qú's (毛璩) family had been destroyed by the people of Shǔ (蜀).
21 Ten commanderies of Jīngzhōu (荊州) were separated to establish Xiāngzhōu (湘州).
In the 3rd year of Chéngdì Xiánhé (成帝咸和),
Xiāngzhōu (湘州) was abolished and incorporated into Jīngzhōu (荊州);
now it was re-established.
22 Tàiwèi (太尉) Yù (裕) was additionally granted the titles of Tàifù (太傅) and Yángzhōu Mù (揚州牧).
23 On the Dīngsì (丁巳) day,
Wèi (魏) ruler Sī (嗣) went on a northern tour,
reaching the Great Wall before returning.
This was the Great Wall built by Qín (秦).
1 In spring,
in the second month,
on the Gēngxū (庚戌) day,
Wèi (魏) ruler Sī (嗣) went to Gāoliǔ Chuān (高柳川);
on the Jiǎyín (甲寅) day,
he returned to the palace.
2 Tàiwèi (太尉) Yù (裕) returned eastward from Jiānglíng (江陵),
sending his baggage trains downstream in succession,
but although he set an arrival date in advance,
he frequently delayed his progress.
Zhūgě Chángmín (諸葛長民) and the high officials had been waiting for him for several days at Xīntíng (新亭),
but he kept changing his schedule.
On the last day of the month, Yǐchǒu (乙丑),
Yù (裕) proceeded rapidly in a light boat,
secretly entering the Eastern Palace.
What Liú Mùzhī (劉穆之) and Hé Chéngtiān (何承天) had worried about,
Yù (裕) already understood perfectly.
On the morning of the first day of the month, Bǐngyín (丙寅),
Chángmín (長民) heard of it and rushed to the gate in surprise.
Yù (裕) hid a brave warrior, Dīng Wǔ (丁旿), behind the curtain,
then drew Chángmín (長民) back to converse privately,
covering all matters they had never fully discussed in their lives.
Chángmín (長民) was greatly pleased.
Dīng Wǔ (丁旿) emerged from behind the curtain,
seized and killed him in his seat,
and carried his body to the Tíngwèi (廷尉).
His younger brother Límín (黎民) was arrested;
Límín (黎民) had always been brave and fierce,
and died fighting.
Also killed were his youngest brother Dàsīmǎ Cānjūn (大司馬參軍) Yòumín (幼民) and his cousin Níngshuò Jiāngjūn (寧朔將軍) Xiùzhī (秀之).
3 On the Gēngwǔ (庚午) day,
Qín (秦) King Xīng (興) sent an envoy to Wèi (魏) to cultivate good relations.
4 Tàiwèi (太尉) Yù (裕) submitted a memorial stating:
"Dàsīmǎ (大司馬) Wēn (溫) believed that 'the people having no fixed abodes severely harms governance,'
and implemented the Gēngxū (庚戌) land division to unify their livelihoods;
the Gēngxū (庚xū) system is recorded in Volume 101, Āidì Xīngníng (哀帝興寧) 2nd year.
This truly stems from that.
From then until now,
it has gradually fallen into disuse,
so I request to re-enforce the previous system."
Thereupon, land was divided according to existing boundaries,
with the exception of residents of Xú (徐), Yǎn (兗), and Qīng (青) three zhōu (州) living in Jìnlíng (晉陵),
who were not subject to this rule;
the Dūdū (都督) of Xú (徐), Qīng (青), and Yǎn (兗) three zhōu (州) governed from Jìnlíng (晉陵),
making it difficult to implement land division there.
Duàn (斷), pronounced Dīngluàn (丁亂).
Bìng (併).
On the Wùyín (戊寅) day,
Yù (裕) was additionally appointed Yùzhōu Cìshǐ (豫州刺史).
Yù (裕) firmly declined the titles of Tàifù (太傅) and Zhōumù (州牧).
He was declining the additions made last winter.
5 Línyì (林邑) Fàn Húdá (范胡達) raided Jiǔzhēn (九真),
and Dù Huìdù (杜慧度) attacked and killed him.

6 Hénán (河南) King Chìpán (熾磐) sent Zhèndōng Jiāngjūn (鎮東將軍) Tándá (曇達) and Píngdōng Jiāngjūn (平東將軍) Wáng Sōngshòu (王松壽) to lead troops eastward to attack Xiūguān Quán Xiǎoláng (休官權小郎) and Lǚ Pòhú (呂破胡) at Báishí Chuān (白石川),
severely defeating them,
capturing over ten thousand men and women,
and advancing to occupy Báishí Chéng (白石城) and Xiǎnqīn (顯親).
Xiūguān Quán Xiǎochéng (休官權小成), Lǚ Nújiā (呂奴迦) and others, over twenty thousand households, held Báikēng (白阬) and refused to submit.
Tándá (曇達) attacked and killed them,
and all the Xiūguān (休官) in Lǒngyòu (隴右) surrendered.
Qín (秦) Tàiwèi (太尉) Suǒ Léng (索稜) surrendered Lǒngxī (隴西) to Chìpán (熾磐).
In the seventh year,
Qín (秦) ordered Suǒ Léng (索稜) to guard Lǒngxī (隴西) to attract and pacify the Qǐfú (乞伏).
Suǒ (索),
pronounced Xī Gè (昔各).
Jiàng (降),
pronounced Hù Jiāng (戶江).
7 Xià (夏) King Bóbó (勃勃) granted a general amnesty,
and changed the era name to Fèngxiáng (鳳翔);
he appointed Chìgān Ālì (叱干阿利) as Lǐng Jiàngzuò Dàjiàng (領將作大匠),
and conscripted one hundred thousand barbarians and Chinese from north of the ridge to build a capital city north of Shuòfāng Shuǐ (朔方水) and south of Hēishuǐ (黑水).
Commentary on the Water Classic says: The Shēyán Shuǐ (奢延水) is also called Shuòfāng Shuǐ (朔方水);
its source is southwest of Shēyán (奢延) County at Chìshā Fù (赤沙阜);
it flows northeast past the south of the old city of Shēyán (奢延) County.
Hèlián (赫連) built the Tǒngwàn Chéng (統萬城) south of this water.
The Shēyán Shuǐ (奢延水) flows further east,
and the Hēishuǐ (黑水) enters it;
the Hēishuǐ (黑水) originates from Hēijiàn (黑澗) in Shēyán (奢延) County,
flows southeast through Shālíng (沙陵),
and empties into the Shēyán Shuǐ (奢延水).
Tǒngwàn Chéng (統萬城) was the seat of the Xiàzhōu Dìngnán Jiédùshǐ (夏州定難節度使) during the Táng (唐) dynasty.
Xià (夏),
pronounced Hù Yǎ (戶雅).
"I am about to unify all under heaven
and rule over all nations,
so this new city should be named Tǒngwàn (統萬, 'Unifying Ten Thousand')."
Ālì (阿利) was skillful yet cruel;
when building the city with steamed earth, if a cone penetrated one inch,
he would kill the worker and bury him in the wall.
Bóbó (勃勃) considered this loyalty and entrusted him with responsibilities.
Whenever weapons were made and presented,
there was always a worker who died: if an arrow failed to pierce armor, the bowyer was executed;
if it did, the armor-maker was executed.
He also cast a large bronze drum,
along with statues of Fēilián (飛廉), Wēngzhòng (翁仲), bronze camels, dragons, and tigers,
adorned with gold,
and arranged them in front of the palace.
Thousands of artisans were killed,
and as a result, all artifacts were exquisite and sharp.
Bóbó (勃勃) claimed that his ancestors took their mother's surname, Liú (劉),
which was improper.
The Records of States (載記) say: Gāozǔ (高祖) of Hàn (漢) married a princess from the imperial clan to Chányú Màodùn (單于冒頓),
and agreed to be brothers,
hence their descendants adopted the surname Liú (劉).
He then changed his surname to Hèlián (赫連),
meaning that emperors are sons connected to heaven,
their brilliance (赫) and connection (連) to heaven;
those who were not of the legitimate lineage
all took the surname Tiěfá (鐵伐),
as Bóbó’s (勃勃) father Wèichén (衞辰) was originally of the Tiěfú (鐵弗) clan,
so he changed the surname of those not of the legitimate lineage to Tiěfá (鐵伐).
All were capable of conquering others.
