8 In summer,
in the fourth month,
on the Yǐmǎo day,
Wèi Zhǔ Sī made a western tour.
He ordered Zhèngbīng Jiāngjūn Xī Jǐn
— "Zhèngbīng"
is written as
"Dūbīng" in the *Běi Shǐ* —
and Dàfēi,
who was a Ròurán,
and Hóngfēi Jiāngjūn
— a title created by the Tuòbá clan —
to go.
The character 將 is pronounced *liàng* here.
The Ròurán's surname was Yùjiǔlǘ;
now it is written as Lǘ,
a simplification for convenience.
Bánà Shān is probably outside the borders of Guǎngníng Jùn.
9 Hénán Wáng Chìpán dispatched Ānběi Jiāngjūn Wūdìyán and Guānjūn Jiāngjūn Zhái Shào to attack the Tǔyùhùn separate commander Jùpáng at Qìqín
Chuān.
They greatly defeated him.
10 Héxī Wáng Méngxùn appointed his son Zhèngdé as Crown Prince,
and added the titles Zhènwèi Dàjiāngjūn and Lù Shàngshū Shì.
11 Nánliáng Wáng Nǔtán attacked Héxī Wáng Méngxùn.
Méngxùn defeated him at Ruòhòu Wù,
and again defeated him at Ruòliáng.
He then advanced to besiege Lèdū,
but failed to capture it after two *xún*.
Nánliáng Huánghé Tàishǒu Wén Zhī surrendered his commandery to Méngxùn.
Méngxùn appointed Wén Zhī as Guǎngwǔ Tàishǒu.
Méngxùn again attacked Nánliáng.
Nǔtán presented Tàiwèi Jù Yán as a hostage,
whereupon Méngxùn returned.
Méngxùn went west to Tiáodiào.
He sent Guānjūn Jiāngjūn Fú Ēn with ten thousand cavalry to attack the Bēihé and Wūtí tribes.
He greatly defeated them.
During the Hàn dynasty, there were Bēihé Qiāng
who lived by Xiānshuǐ Hǎi.
While Méngxùn was sleeping in Xīntái,
the eunuch Wáng Huáizǔ attacked and wounded Méngxùn's foot.
His wife, Mèng Shì, captured and beheaded him.
Méngxùn's mother, Chē Shì, died.
12 In the fifth month,
on the Yǐhài day,
Wèi Zhǔ Sī went to the old palace in Yúnzhōng.
The Táng's Dānyú Dūhù Fǔ governed Jīnhé county,
which was the Yúnzhōng of the Qín and Hàn dynasties.
The *Xīn Shū* says: Jīnhé was originally the capital of Hòu Wèi Dàowǔ.
On the Bǐngzǐ day,
there was a general amnesty.
The Hú of Xīhé, Zhāng Wài and others, gathered a crowd and became bandits.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
Sī dispatched Huìjī Gōng Chánglè Liú Jié and others to garrison Xīhé and suppress them.
Note that from Yǐhài to Bǐngzǐ is nearly forty days,
so there is clearly no Yǐmǎo in the fifth month.
It is probably Jǐmǎo.
The character 會
is pronounced *gōng wài* here.
Sī went to Wǔyuán.
13 Zhū Língshí and others reached Báidì and opened the sealed letter,
which said:
"All armies will proceed from the outer water to take Chéngdū;
Zāng Xī will take Guǎnghàn from the middle water."
The *Shuǐ Jīng Zhù* says: "The Luò Shuǐ originates from the south of Zhāng Shān in Luò Xiàn,
flows south past the old city of Luò Xiàn,
which was the seat of Guǎnghàn Jùn,
then flows further south past Xīndū Xiàn and joins the Bóshuǐ,
and also joins the Jiānshuǐ,
also called Pí Jiāng.
It then passes by the Niúbǐ Shuǐ in Jiànwéi,
and then eastward past Zīzhōng Xiàn,
where it is called Bóshuǐ."
The Bóshuǐ enters the Jiāng below Fāng Shān in Jiāngyáng Xiàn,
where it is called Bóshuǐkǒu,
which is the middle water.
"From the inner water, head towards Huánghǔ."
Thereupon, all armies marched twice the normal speed.
Qiáo Zòng indeed ordered Qiáo Dàofú to lead heavy troops to garrison Fúchéng,
to guard against the inner water.
Língshí reached Píngmó,
two hundred *lǐ* from Chéngdū.
Zòng sent Qínzhōu Cìshǐ Hóu Huī and Shàngshū Púyè Qiáo Shēn to lead over ten thousand troops to garrison Píngmó,
building fortifications on both banks to resist them.
Língshí said to Liú Zhōng:
"The weather is extremely hot today,
and the bandits are heavily armed and secured in a strong position.
Attacking them may not guarantee victory and will only increase our fatigue.
What if we preserve our strength and rest our troops to await an opportune moment?"
Zhōng replied:
"No.
Previously, we spread rumors that our main force was heading towards the inner water,
so Qiáo Dàofú would not dare to abandon Fúchéng.
Now, our heavy forces have arrived suddenly,
catching them off guard.
Hóu Huī and his ilk are already terrified.
Their obstruction and defense of a strong position
show that they are afraid to fight.
Taking advantage of their fear,
if we attack with all our might,
we are bound to win.
After capturing Píngmó,
we can advance unimpeded,
and Chéngdū will surely not be able to hold out.
If we delay and face them in a stalemate,
they will learn our strengths and weaknesses.
If the Fúchéng army suddenly arrives,
and they combine forces to resist us,
the morale of their people will have stabilized,
and their good generals will have assembled.
The 'good generals' refer to Qiáo Dàofú.
The character 即 is pronounced *liàng* here.
Then we will fail to achieve battle,
our military supplies will run out,
and our more than twenty thousand men will all become captives of Shǔ."
Língshí followed his advice.
The generals thought that the northern city across the river had difficult terrain and many soldiers,
and wanted to attack the southern city first.
Língshí said:
"Even if we capture the southern city,
it will not be enough to break the northern one.
If we exert all our strength to capture the northern city,
the southern city will disperse without even being signaled."
In autumn,
in the seventh month,
Língshí led all the armies to urgently attack the northern city.
They captured it
and beheaded Hóu Huī and Qiáo Shēn.
He led his troops back towards the southern city,
and the southern city collapsed on its own.
Língshí abandoned his boats and advanced on foot.
Qiáo Zòng's grand general Qiáo Fǔzhī was garrisoned at Niúbǐ.
"Niúbǐ"
should be
"Niúbǐ."
Mèng Kāng said: 鞞
is pronounced *bǐ*.
Shī Gǔ said: It is pronounced *bì ěr*.
Niúbǐ Xiàn has belonged to Jiànwéi Jùn since the Hàn dynasty.
Hé Chéngtiān said: During Jìn Mùdì's reign, it was transferred to Shǔ Jùn.
Today, on the west bank of Jiǎnzhōu, there is an ancient Niúbǐ garrison city.
Dábí Shān is about ten *lǐ* south of Péngshān Xiàn in present-day Méizhōu.
The mountain rises in isolation,
overlooking the Jiāng River to the east.
Locally it is said: In ancient times, the Zhōu tripods sank here,
and sometimes their noses were seen,
hence the name.
The character 塞
is pronounced *sì zé*.
He beheaded him.
Xiǎogōu, hearing of this,
also collapsed.
Thereupon, all of Zòng's camps and garrisons fled one after another at the mere sight of the enemy.
On the day Wùchén,
Qáo Zǒng abandoned Chéngdū and fled.
Shàngshū Lìng Mǎ Dān sealed the government treasuries to await the Jìn army.
On the day Rénshēn,
Liú Língshí entered Chéngdū.
He executed Qáo Zǒng's relatives of the same clan,
but the rest were settled in place,
and allowed to resume their occupations.
When Qáo Zǒng left Chéngdū,
he first bade farewell at his ancestors' tombs.
His daughter said:
"If you flee, you will certainly not escape,
and will only invite humiliation;
if death is inevitable,
it would be better to die at the tombs of our ancestors."
Qáo Zǒng did not heed her.
Qáo Dàofú heard that Píngmú was not held,
and led his troops from Fú to reinforce.
Qáo Zǒng went to him for refuge.
When Qáo Dàofú saw Qáo Zǒng,
he angrily said:
"A great man, having such achievements, and abandoning them,
where will you go?!
Who does not die?
Why are you so cowardly?!"
He then threw a sword at Qáo Zǒng,
striking his horse's saddle.
Qáo Zǒng then left,
and hanged himself.
Wáng Zhì of Bāxī cut off his head and sent it to Liú Língshí.
Qáo Dàofú said to his followers:
"The survival or destruction of Shǔ
truly depends on me,
not on Qáo Wáng.
Now that I am here,
we can still fight a battle."
All the followers agreed;
Qáo Dàofú distributed all his gold and silk to his followers,
who took it and fled.
Qáo Dàofú escaped into the territory of the Láos,
but Dù Jǐn, a commoner of Bá, captured and delivered him,
and he was executed at the army gate.
In the first year of Yìxī (405 CE),
Qáo Zǒng occupied Shǔ,
and was destroyed after nine years.
Jǐn,
pronounced "Qú Lìn fān".
Mǎ Dān said to his followers:
"Zhū Hóu will not send me to the capital,
wishing to silence me,
meaning that Liú Língshí took many items from the treasury,
and will kill Mǎ Dān to silence him."
So he bathed and lay down,
and strangled himself.
After a short while,
Liú Língshí's messenger arrived,
and mutilated his corpse.
An imperial edict promoted Liú Língshí to supervisor of military affairs for the six commanderies of Liáng and Qín provinces,
and granted him the title of Fēngchéng Xiàn Hóu.
14. Wèi's Xī Jīn and others defeated Yuèqín west of Bánà Shān,
and resettled over 20,000 households in Dàníng.
15. Cáo Lóng, a Hú of Héxī, leading a force of 20,000 men, entered Púzǐ.
Zhāng Wài surrendered to him,
and proclaimed Cáo Lóng as Dà Chányú.
16. On the day Bǐngxū,
Wèi Zhǔ Sī went to Dàluò Chéng in Dìngxiāng.
The chronicles of the two Hàn dynasties state: Dìngxiāng Commandery has Luò County.
17. Hé Nán Wáng Chìpán attacked Tǔyùhún's Zhīpáng at Chángliǔ Chuān,
captured Zhīpáng and over 5,000 households of his people, and returned.
18. In the eighth month,
on the day Guǐmǎo,
Wèi Zhǔ Sī returned to Píngchéng.
19. Cáo Lóng requested to surrender to Wèi,
captured and delivered Zhāng Wài,
and he was executed.
20. On the day Dīngchǒu,
Wèi Zhǔ Sī went to Cháishān Gōng;
on the day Guǐwèi,
he returned.
21. In the ninth month,
Tàiwèi Yù was again appointed Tàifù and Yángzhōu Mù;
he firmly declined.
22. Hé Nán Wáng Chìpán attacked Tǔyùhún's separate commander Jué Kuí at Kěhún Chuān,
decisively defeating him,
and capturing 23,000 men and women.
In winter,
tenth month,
Jué Kuí led his remaining followers and surrendered to Chìpán.
23. The Tújīng Hú and Lìshí Hú, along with Chū Yǐjuàn, rebelled against Wèi.
Wèi Zhǔ Sī ordered Yuánchéng Hóu Qū Dū to meet with Huìjī Gōng Liú Jié and Yǒng'ān Hóu Wèi Qín to suppress them.
On the day Dīngsì,
Chū Yǐjuàn led Xià troops to intercept and attack Liú Jié,
captured him and presented him to Xià;
Wèi Qín died in battle.
Sī, because Qū Dū lost two generals,
wanted to execute him;
but later pardoned him,
and made him acting Cìshǐ of Bìngzhōu.
When Qū Dū arrived at the province,
he indulged in drink and neglected his duties.
Sī accumulated his past and present crimes,
brought him back in a cage cart,
and executed him.
When Wèi Zhǔ Sī was installed,
Qū Dū's son Móhún had rendered meritorious service;
Qū Dū relied on this and became arrogant.
Accumulating his wickedness and then executing him is
not a way to protect the families of meritorious officials.
24. In the eleventh month,
Wèi Zhǔ Sī sent an envoy to request a marriage alliance with Qín,
and Qín Wáng Xīng agreed to it.
25. In this year,
Suǒ Miǎo of Dūnhuáng was appointed Cìshǐ of Liángzhōu,
and Fú Xuān then returned to Qiúchí.
Fú Xuān entered Hànzhōng;
see volume 114, first year.
Suǒ Miǎo had resided in Hànchuān,
and had a feud with Biéjià Jiāng Xiǎn,
which lasted fifteen years until Suǒ Miǎo took charge of Hànchuān;
Jiāng Xiǎn then went bare-chested to greet him,
but Suǒ Miǎo showed no resentment,
and treated him with increasing kindness.
He later said to others:
"When I resided here in the past,
I was disheartened for many years.
If I were to avenge myself on Jiāng Xiǎn,
not a few would be fearful.
But submitting is itself better,
why must one indulge one's will?"
Thereupon, everyone in the region rejoiced upon hearing this.
Jū Xiànzhī's An Dōnglái was also like this.
Those in the world who nurse grudges and bring about calamity
do so because they do not understand this principle.
1. In spring,
first month,
on the day Xīnyǒu,
Wèi issued a general amnesty,
and changed its era name to Shénruì.
On the day Xīnsì,
Wèi Zhǔ Sī went to Fánzhì;
in the second month,
on the day Wùxū,
he returned to Píngchéng.
2. Xià Wáng Bóbó invaded Wèi's Hédōng Púzǐ.
3. On the day Gēngxū,
Wèi Zhǔ Sī went to Cháishān Gōng.
4. Wèi's Bìngzhōu Cìshǐ Lóu
Fúlián attacked and killed the Tújīng Hùjūn and his garrison troops placed by Xià.
The Wèi Shū: Guānshì Zhì states: Among the surnames brought in, there was Pǐlóu Shì,
later changed to Lóu Shì.
Last year,
Xià defeated Tuòbá Qū,
and consequently placed garrison troops in Tújīng.
5. Sīmǎ Xiūzhī, in Jiānglíng,
gained considerable popular support from Jiāng and Hàn.
His son, Qáo Wáng Wénsī, was in Jiànkāng.
Wénsī
was Xiūzhī's eldest son.
Qáo Wáng Shàngzhī died in Huán Xuán's rebellion.
When the Emperor was restored,
he appointed Wénsī to inherit the title.
He was fond of associating with young ruffians;
Tàiwèi Yù disliked this.
In the third month,
the proper authorities memorialized that Wénsī had beaten and killed a state official.
An edict ordered the execution of his partisans but pardoned Wénsī.
Sīmǎ Xiūzhī submitted a memorial to apologize,
and requested to be relieved of his post,
but this was not granted.
Yù arrested Wénsī and sent him to Sīmǎ Xiūzhī,
ordering him to discipline him personally,
intending for Sīmǎ Xiūzhī to kill him;
but Sīmǎ Xiūzhī only memorialized to depose Wénsī,
and also sent a letter to Yù expressing his apologies.
Yù was displeased by this,
which set the stage for Yù's later campaign against Sīmǎ Xiūzhī.
The six commanderies of Yùzhōu were Xuānchéng, Xiāngchéng, Huáinán, Lújiāng, Ānfēng, and Lìyáng.
6. In summer,
fifth month,
on the day Xīnyǒu,
Wèi Zhǔ Sī returned to Píngchéng.
7. Qín's Hòu Jiāngjūn Liǎnx Chéng attacked rebellious Qiāng,
but was defeated by the Qiāng.
Fearing punishment,
he fled to Xià.
8. Qín Wáng Xīng was ill.
The demonic rebel Lǐ Hóng and the Dī Qíou Cháng rebelled at Èrchéng.
Xīng, though ill, went to suppress them,
executed Qíou Cháng,
captured Lǐ Hóng, and returned.
9 Qín’s Left General, Yáo Wénzōng 姚文宗, was favored by Crown Prince Hóng 泓.
Guǎngpíng Gōng Bì 廣平公弼 detested him,
and falsely accused Wénzōng 姚文宗 of having resentful remarks.
Qín Wáng Xīng 秦王興 was enraged,
and bestowed death upon Wénzōng 姚文宗.
From then on, the officials all feared Bì 廣平公弼 and looked at him askance.
Whatever Bì 廣píng Gōng Bì said to Xīng 秦王興,
there was nothing he did not follow.
He appointed Yǐn Chōng 尹沖 of Tiānshuǐ 天水, whom he was close to, as Gěishì Huángmén Shìláng 給事黃門侍郎,
and Táng Shèng 唐盛 as Zhìshū Shìyùshǐ 治書侍御史.
Those in charge of confidential matters around Xīng 秦王興
were all his partisans.
Right Minister Liáng Xǐ 梁喜, Palace Attendant Rèn Qiān 任謙, and Jīngzhào Yǐn 京兆尹 Yǐn Zhāo 尹昭 took advantage of an opportunity to speak to Xīng 秦王興, saying:
"The relationship between father and son
is something people find difficult to speak about.
However, the righteousness between ruler and minister
is no less profound than that between father and son,
so we, your subjects, cannot remain silent.
Guǎngpíng Gōng Bì 廣平公弼
secretly harbors the ambition to usurp the succession.
Your Majesty favors him excessively
and grants him great authority.
Treacherous and unreliable individuals flock to him.
Everyone on the roads says that Your Majesty intends to depose and establish a new heir.
Is this truly the case?"
Xīng 秦王興 said:
"How could such a thing be!"
Xǐ 梁喜 and others said:
"If it is truly not the case,
then Your Majesty's love for Bì 廣平公弼
is precisely what will bring disaster upon him.
We beg you to remove those around him,
and diminish his authority.
If you do this,
it will not only secure Bì 廣平公弼,
but also secure the imperial ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain."
Xīng 秦王興 did not respond.
Grand Minister of Agriculture Bǎo Wēn 寶溫
and Sītú Zuǒ Chángshǐ 司徒左長史 Wáng Bì 王弼 both secretly submitted memorials urging Xīng 秦王興 to establish Bì 廣平公弼 as Crown Prince.
Although Xīng 秦王興 did not follow their advice,
he did not rebuke them either.
When Xīng 秦王興 became gravely ill,
Bì 廣平公弼 secretly gathered several thousand men
and plotted a rebellion.
Yáo Yù 姚裕 sent an envoy to inform his elder brothers, who were in the frontier garrisons, of Bì's 廣平公弼 rebellious state.
Thereupon, Yáo Yì 姚懿 mustered troops at Púbàn 蒲阪,
and Zhèndōng Jiāngjūn Yùzhōu Mù Guāng 鎮東將軍豫州牧洸 mustered troops at Luòyáng 洛陽.
Yì 姚懿 and Guāng 洸
were both sons of Xīng 秦王興.
Zhì 治,
pronounced like zhí zhī.
Guāng 洸,
pronounced like gū huáng.
All wished to proceed to Cháng'ān 長安 to suppress Bì 廣平公弼.
Coincidentally, Xīng 秦王興's illness recovered.
When he met his officials,
Zhēnglǔ Jiāngjūn Liú Qiāng 征虜將軍劉羌 tearfully informed Xīng 秦王興.
Liáng Xǐ 梁喜 and Yǐn Zhāo 尹昭 requested to execute Bì 廣平公弼,
and furthermore said:
"If Your Majesty cannot bear to kill Bì 廣平公弼,
you should at least strip him of his authority."
Xīng 秦王興 had no choice but to
remove Bì 廣平公弼 from the position of Shàngshū Lìng 尚書令,
and ordered him to return to his residence as a general and duke.
Bì 廣平公弼 was Dà Jiāngjūn 大將軍
and enfeoffed as Guǎngpíng Gōng 廣平公.
Yì 姚懿, Guāng 洸, Chén 諶, and Yáo Xuān 姚宣 all came to court.
Yù 姚裕 was sent to report to Xīng 秦王興,
requesting an audience.
Xīng 秦王興 said:
"You just want to discuss Bì's 廣平公弼 matter,
I already know about it."
Yù 姚裕 said:
"If Bì 廣平公弼 has something to be discussed,
Your Majesty should listen to it.
If Yì 姚懿 and others' words are not correct,
then they should be punished.
How can you refuse them?"
Thereupon, he granted an audience to Yì 姚懿 and others in the Zīyì Táng 諮議堂.
Xuān 姚宣 tearfully spoke emphatically.
Xīng 秦王興 said:
"I will handle this myself,
it is not for you all to worry about."
Fǔjūn Dōngcáo Shǔ Jiāng Qiú 撫軍東曹屬姜虬 submitted a memorial, saying:
"Guǎngpíng Gōng Bì 廣平公弼's crimes have become obvious and his rebellion manifest,
everyone on the roads knows it.
In ancient times, the transformative influence of King Wén 文王
extended to his wife.
The Shī (Ode) Sī Qí 思齊 says: 'His influence extended to his wife,
and then to his brothers.'
This arises from the love for one's son;
even if one wishes to tolerate and conceal it,
the rebellious faction continuously incites and confuses,
how can Bì's 廣平公弼 rebellious heart be changed?
It is advisable to disperse the evil conspirators
to cut off the source of disaster."
Xīng 秦王興 showed Qiú's 姜虬 memorial to Liáng Xǐ 梁喜, saying:
"The people of the world all use my son as a topic of conversation."
Kǒng Ānguó 孔安國 said: "Kǒushí 口實 means something that is always on one's lips."
Xǐ 梁喜 said:
"Indeed, as Qiú 姜虬 says,
Your Majesty should make an early decision."
Xīng 秦王興 remained silent.
The historians say that Yáo Xīng 姚興 did not listen to his officials and sons,
thus fostering the disaster of Hóng 泓 and Bì 廣平公弼 contending for the throne.
10 The Tuòqìhàn 唾契汗, Yǐfú 乙弗, and other tribes all rebelled against Nánliáng 南涼.
Nánliáng Wáng Rǔtán 南涼王傉檀 wished to suppress them.
Hánchuān Hùjūn Mèng Kǎi 邯川護軍孟愷 admonished him, saying:
"Now, for successive years, there has been famine.
To the south, we are pressed by Chìpán 熾磐,
and to the north by Méngxùn 蒙遜.
The people are restless.
Even if a distant expedition is successful,
there will certainly be future troubles.
It is better to form an alliance with Chìpán 熾磐 and trade grain,
appease the various tribes,
ensure sufficient food, equip the army,
and await the opportune moment to act."
Rǔtán 傉檀 did not listen,
and said to Crown Prince Hǔtái 虎臺:
"Méngxùn 蒙遜 recently left,
and cannot return suddenly.
What we have to worry about day and night
is only Chìpán 熾磐.
However, Chìpán's 熾磐 army is small and easy to defend against.
You guard Lèdū 樂都 carefully.
I will definitely return in less than a month."
Thereupon, he led seven thousand cavalry to attack Yǐfú 乙弗,
greatly defeating them,
and capturing over 400,000 horses, cattle, and sheep.
Hénán Wáng Chìpán 河南王熾磐 heard of this
and wished to attack Lèdū 樂都.
All his officials thought it was inadvisable.
Tàifǔ Zhǔbù Jiāo Xí 太府主簿焦襲 said:
"Rǔtán 傉檀 disregards nearby dangers for distant gains.
Nearby dangers
refer to Méngxùn 蒙遜 and Chìpán 熾磐;
distant gains
refer to Yǐfú 乙弗.
Cut off his western route,"
the western route of Lèdū 樂都
is Rǔtán's 傉檀 return route from Yǐfú 乙弗 to Lèdū 樂都.
"Then Hǔtái 虎臺 will be left to defend a desolate city alone,
and can be captured easily.
This is Heaven's time for his demise,
and it must not be missed."
Chìpán 熾磐 followed his advice,
and led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Lèdū 樂都.
Hǔtái 虎臺 relied on the city walls to defend.
Chìpán 熾磐 attacked it from all four sides.
Nánliáng Fǔjūn Cóngshì Zhōngláng Wèi Sù 南涼撫軍從事中郎尉肅 spoke to Hǔtái 虎臺, saying:
"The outer city is vast and difficult to defend.
Your Highness had better gather the common people to defend the inner city."
Guórén 國人
refers to the Tuòfà 禿髮 branch of the Xiānbēi 鮮卑.
"Even if there is no victory,
it is still enough to preserve ourselves."
Hǔtái 虎臺 said:
"Chìpán 熾磐 is a petty brigand;
he will flee any moment.
Why are you so overly concerned?"
Hǔtái 虎臺 suspected the Jìn Rén 晉人 (Han Chinese) of having ulterior motives.
The barbarians referred to the Han Chinese as Jìn Rén 晉人.
Mèng Kǎi 孟愷 tearfully said:
"Chìpán 熾磐 has taken advantage of our weakness to invade;
the state is in extreme peril.
We, your subjects, wish to repay your kindness,
and also consider our wives and children.
Everyone is ready to die for you.
Yet Your Highness suspects us like this!"
Hǔtái 虎臺 said:
"How could I not know your loyalty and sincerity?
I only fear that others might harbor unforeseen thoughts,
so I rely on you all to reassure them."
One night,
the city walls crumbled.
Chìpán 熾磐 entered Lèdū 樂都,
and dispatched Píngyuǎn Jiāngjūn Jié Qián 平遠將軍捷虔 to lead five thousand cavalry to pursue Rǔtán 傉檀.
He appointed Zhènnán Jiāngjūn Qiāntún 鎮南將軍謙屯 as Dūdū Héyòu Zhū Jūnshì Liángzhōu Cìshǐ 都督河右諸軍事涼州刺史,
to garrison Lèdū 樂都.
Jié Qián 捷虔 and Qiāntún 謙屯
were both of the Qífú 乞伏 clan.
[He appointed him] to garrison Xīpíng 西平;
he appointed Zhào Huī 趙恢 as Guǎngwǔ Tàishǒu 廣武太守,
to garrison Guǎngwǔ 廣武;
Yàowǔ Jiāngjūn Wáng Jī 曜武將軍王基 as Jìnxīng Tàishǒu 晉興太守,
to garrison Hàowěi 浩亹.
He relocated Hǔtái 虎臺 and his civil and military officials and over ten thousand households to Páohǎn 枹罕.
Fú Dāi 赴單 was the son of Wū Gū 烏孤.
11 Chǔ Kuāng (褚匡) of Héjiān (河間) spoke to Yàn (燕) King Féng Bá (馮跋), saying:
"Your Majesty has soared like a dragon from Liáo (遼) and Jié (碣).
Your old clans and parties
all turn their heads towards the morning sun,
saying that the sun rises in the east,
just as Féng Bá (馮跋) rose in Liáo (遼) and Jié (碣).
His clans and parties who are in Chánglè (長樂)
turn their heads and gaze eastward.
Jié (碣)
is pronounced *yè* (謁).
I request to go and welcome them."
Bá (跋) said:
"The road is several thousand *lǐ*,
and furthermore it is separated by foreign countries.
How can they be brought here?"
Kuāng (匡) said:
"Zhāngwǔ (章武) borders the sea.
Bá's (跋) ancestors
were from Xìndū (信都), Chánglè (長樂),
and Zhāngwǔ (章武) Commandery was established by Jìn (晉) by dividing Hàn's (漢) Bóhǎi (勃海) Commandery.
From Xìndū (信都) to Zhāngwǔ (章武),
one can float across the sea to Liáoxī (遼西).
Coming out from Liáoxī (遼西) at Línyú (臨渝)
is not difficult."
Línyú (臨渝) County
belonged to Liáoxī (遼西) Commandery in Hàn (漢).
Shī Gǔ (師古) said: Yú (渝)
is pronounced *yù* (喻).
The *Shuǐ Jīng* (水經) says: Jiéshí (碣石) is south of the county.
Bá (跋) appointed Kuāng (匡) as General of Agile Cavalry and Central Secretariat Gentleman,
providing him generously and sending him off.
Kuāng (匡), along with Bá's (跋) paternal cousin Mǎi (買) and younger paternal cousin Dǔ (睹),
led over five thousand households from Chánglè (長樂) to return to Hélóng (和龍).
Emperor Gāozǔ (高祖) of Hàn (漢) established Xìndū (信都) Commandery.
In the second year of Emperor Jǐng (景), it became Guǎngchuān (廣川) Kingdom.
Emperor Míng (明) renamed it Lèchéng (樂成).
Emperor Ān (安) changed it to Ānpíng (安平).
Jìn (晉) changed it to Chánglè (長樂).
Lè (樂)
is pronounced *luò* (洛).
Shuài (帥)
is read as *shuài* (率).
Bá (跋) appointed their chieftains as Guīshàn Wáng (歸善王).
Bá's (跋) younger brother Pī (丕) had taken refuge in Gāogōulì (高句麗).
Bá (跋) summoned him,
made him Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat,
and enfeoffed him as Duke of Chángshān (常山).
12 Húliǜ (斛律), the Khagan of Rourán (柔然), was about to marry his daughter to Yàn (燕).
Kě (可)
has the entering tone of *kān* (刊).
Hán (汗)
is pronounced *hán* (寒).
"[I am] worried about my young daughter marrying far away.
I request to send the daughters of ministers like Shùlí (樹黎) as accompanying concubines."
Húliǜ (斛律) did not consent.
Bùlùzhēn (步鹿真) came out
and said to Shùlí (樹黎) and others:
"Húliǜ (斛律) wants to take your daughters as accompanying concubines,
to be married far away to another country."
Shùlí (樹黎) was afraid,
and conspired with Bùlùzhēn (步鹿真) to have brave warriors hide at night behind Húliǜ's (斛律) yurt.
They waited for him to come out and seized him,
sending him and his daughter to Yàn (燕).
They established Bùlùzhēn (步鹿真) as Khagan and made him their prime minister.
At first,
when Shèlún (社崙) migrated the Gāochē (高車) (this event is detailed in Volume 112, Yuánxīng (元興) 1st year),
Lún (崙)
is pronounced *lúkūn* (盧昆).
Bìng (⿰亻併)
Shèlún (社崙) appreciated him
and made him a chieftain.
Bùlùzhēn (步鹿真) and Shèlún's (社崙) son Shèbá (社拔) went together to Chìluòhóu's (叱洛侯) house
and committed adultery with his young wife.
The wife told Bùlùzhēn (步鹿真):
"Chìluòhóu (叱洛侯) wants to enthrone Dàtán (大檀) as lord."
Dàtán (大檀) was
the son of Shèlún's (社崙) youngest paternal uncle Púhún (僕渾).
He led a separate tribe and guarded the western frontier,
and had always enjoyed popular support.
Bùlùzhēn (步鹿真) returned and dispatched troops to besiege Chìluòhóu (叱洛侯).
Chìluòhóu (叱洛侯) committed suicide.
Then, he led his troops to attack Dàtán (大檀).
Dàtán (大檀) counterattacked,
defeated them,
captured Bùlùzhēn (步鹿真) and Shèbá (社拔),
killed them,
and established himself as Khagan,
styling himself Móhàn Gēshēnggài (牟汗紇升蓋) Khagan.
Wèi Shōu (魏收) said: In Wèi (魏) language, this means "victorious ruler."
Upon Húliǜ (斛律) arriving at Hélóng (和龍),
Yàn (燕) King Bá (跋) granted Húliǜ (斛律) the title of Marquis of Shànggǔ (上谷),
housed him in Liáodōng (遼東),
treated him with the courtesy due to a guest,
and took his daughter as his Zhāoyí (昭儀).
Húliǜ (斛律) submitted a memorial requesting to return to his country.
Bá (跋) said:
"Now you have abandoned your country a myriad *lǐ* away,
and have no internal support.
If I send a large army to escort you,
then provisions and transport would be difficult to sustain.
If the troops are few, they will not be sufficient for success.
How can you return?"
Húliǜ (斛律) insisted on his request,
saying:
"There is no need for a large army.
I wish to be given three hundred cavalry
and be escorted to the Chìlè (敕勒) country.
People will surely come to welcome me gladly."
Bá (跋) then sent Chányú (單于) former aide Wàn Líng (萬陵) to lead three hundred cavalry to escort him.
Líng (陵) was wary of the long expedition.
Upon reaching Hēishān (黑山) (Hēishān (黑山) is outside the northern frontier of Táng (唐)'s Zhènwǔ (振武),
also known as Shāhúshān (殺胡山)),
he killed Húliǜ (斛律). Dàtán (大檀) also sent an envoy to offer three thousand horses and ten thousand sheep to Yàn (燕).
13 In the sixth month,
Liú Yán (劉研) and others, the Administrator of Tàishān (泰山), led over seven thousand refugee households; Liú Zhē (劉遮) and other Hú (胡) chieftains of Héxī (河西) led over ten thousand tribal households.
All surrendered to Wèi (魏).
14 On the day of Wùshēn (戊申),
Wèi (魏) ruler Sì (嗣) went to Cáishān (豺山) Palace.
On the day of Dīnghài (丁亥),
he returned to Píngchéng (平城).
15 When Lèdū (樂都) was defeated,
Fán Ní (樊尼), Nánliáng's (南涼) General of the Pacified West, fled from Xīpíng (西平) to inform Nánliáng (南涼) King Rǔtán (傉檀).
Rǔtán (傉檀) said to his followers:
"Now our wives and children have all been captured by Chìpán (熾磐).
Retreating, we have nowhere to return.
Can you all, with me, use Yǐfú's (乙弗) resources
to capture Qìhàn (契汗) to ransom our wives and children?"
Thereupon, he led his troops west.
Many of his followers deserted and returned.
Rǔtán (傉檀) sent General of the Pacified North Duàn Gǒu (段苟) to pursue them,
but Gǒu (苟) also did not return.
At this, the officers and soldiers all dispersed.
Only Fán Ní (樊尼), General of the Central Army Gēbó (紇勃), General of the Rear Army Luò Gōng (洛肱), and Gentleman of the Cavalier Attendants Yīn Lìlù (陰利鹿) did not leave.
Sǎn (散)
is pronounced *sìdǎn* (悉亶).
Qí (騎)
is pronounced *qíjì* (奇寄).

"[Mèngxùn (蒙遜) and Chìpán (熾磐) both once pledged allegiance to me (Mèngxùn (蒙遜) declared himself a vassal to Lìlùgū (利鹿孤), see Volume 112, Lóng'ān (隆安) 5th year; Chìpán's (熾磐) father and son submitted to Lìlùgū (利鹿孤), see Volume 111, 4th year).
Zhì (質)
is pronounced *zhīrì* (之日).
Is this not despicable!
The world is vast,
yet there is no place for me to find refuge.
How painful this is!
Rather than gathering and dying together,
it is better to separate and perhaps survive.
Fán Ní (樊尼) is the son of my eldest brother (Fán Ní (樊尼) was likely the son of Wūgū (烏孤)).
Zhǎng (長)
is pronounced *zhīliǎng* (知兩).
My followers in the north number nearly ten thousand households.
Mèngxùn (蒙遜) is now inviting and comforting officers and common people,
preserving the living and continuing the extinct.
You should follow him.
Gēbó (紇勃) and Luò Gōng (洛肱) should also go with Ní (尼).
I am old now,
and wherever I go, I will not be tolerated.
I would rather see my wife and children and die!"
So he returned to Chìpán (熾磐).
Only Yīn Lìlù (陰利鹿) followed him.
Rǔtán (傉檀) said to Lìlù (利鹿):
"All my relatives have dispersed.
Why do you alone remain?"
Lìlù (利鹿) replied:
"My old mother is at home,
it is not that I do not wish to return.
However, having pledged allegiance as a minister,
the way of loyalty and filial piety
cannot easily be fulfilled simultaneously.
I am untalented,
unable to weep blood for Your Majesty and seek aid from neighboring countries.
How dare I leave your side!"
Rǔtán (傉檀) sighed and said:
"Indeed, knowing people is not easy.
All my ministers and relatives have abandoned me.
Today, you are the only one whose loyalty and righteousness remain unblemished from beginning to end!"
All the cities of Nŭtán surrendered to Chìpán,
except for Wèi Xiánzhèng, who garrisoned Hàowěi
and held out steadfastly.
Chìpán sent a person to him, saying:
"Lèdū has already fallen,
your wife and children are all in my custody.
What will you achieve by defending a single city alone?"
Xiánzhèng said:
"I have received great kindness from the King of Liáng and
served as a protective screen for the state.
Although I know Lèdū has fallen
and my wife and children are captives,
those who surrender first receive rewards,
while those who submit later are executed;
yet, I do not know if my sovereign is alive or dead.
My sovereign,
refers to Nŭtán.
My wife and children are minor matters,
how can they sway my heart!
If I were to covet momentary gain
and forget the heavy trust placed in me,
what use would Your Majesty have for me?"
Chìpán then sent Hŭtái with a handwritten letter to persuade him.
Xiánzhèng said:
"You, as the heir apparent,
failed to uphold your integrity,
allowed yourself to be bound by others,
abandoned your father and forgot your sovereign,
thus ruining a legacy for ten thousand generations.
I, Xiánzhèng, am a righteous man,
how could I emulate you!"
When he heard that Nŭtán had reached Zuǒnán,
he then surrendered.
Kànhuīn's Shísānzhōuzhì states: Zuǒnán City is sixty *lǐ* east of Báitŭ County in Jīnchéng.
Jìnzhì: The Zhāng family established Jìnxīng Commandery,
and Zuǒnán County belonged to it.
This county was also likely established by the Zhāng family.
When Chìpán heard that Nŭtán had arrived,
he sent envoys to welcome him in the suburbs
and treated him with the courtesy of a distinguished guest.
In autumn,
in the seventh month,
Chìpán appointed Nŭtán as General-in-Chief of the Agile Cavalry (Piàojì Dàjiàngjūn),
and granted him the title Duke of Zuǒnán.
The civil and military officials of Nánliáng
were ranked and assigned according to their talents.
After more than a year,
Chìpán sent someone to poison Nŭtán.
His attendants requested an antidote,
but Nŭtán said:
"How can my illness be treated?"
He then died,
and was posthumously given the title King Jǐng.
Zàijì states: From Tūfà Wūgū to Nŭtán, three generations,
the state was destroyed after nineteen years.
Nŭtán's sons Bǎozhōu and Hè,
Jùyán's son Fùlóng,
Lìlùgū's grandson Fùzhōu,
and Wūgū's grandson Chéngbō,
all fled to Hèxī King Méngxùn.
After a long time,
they again fled to Wèi.
Wèi appointed Bǎozhōu as King of Zhāngyè,
Fùlóng as Duke of Jiŭquán,
Hè as Duke of Xīpíng,
Fùzhōu as Duke of Yǒngpíng,
and Chéngbō as Duke of Chāngsōng.
Wèi Lord Sì admired Hè's talent,
and said to him:
"Your ancestors share the same origin as Ourself,"
and bestowed upon him the surname Yuán.
This established the foundation for the prosperity of the Yuán clan in Wèi.
16In the eighth month,
on the *wùzǐ* day,
Wèi Lord Sì sent the Marquis of Mǎyì, Lòusūn, as an envoy to Qín.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
he sent the Usher Yú Shímén as an envoy to Yàn,
and Yuèlìyán as an envoy to Ròurán.
Yú Shímén reached Hélóng,
but refused to enter for an audience,
saying:
"The Great Wèi Emperor has an imperial edict,
it requires King Féng to come out to receive it;
only then dare I enter."
Yàn King Bá sent men to forcefully drag him in;
Shímén did not bow when he saw Bá.
Bá ordered men to press his neck,
but Shímén said:
"King Féng is to bow and receive the edict;
I, as a guest to a host, merely offer respect.
Why must I be forced?"
Bá was enraged,
and detained Shímén, refusing to let him go.
Shímén frequently insulted the multitude.
His attendants requested to kill him,
but Bá said:
"Each acts for his own lord."
He then imprisoned Shímén,
intending to make him surrender,
but Shímén never surrendered.
After a long time,
his clothes and cap were almost completely worn out and ruined,
swarming with lice and fleas.
Bá sent him new clothes and a cap,
but Shímén refused them all.
17Wèi Lord Sì appointed Doctor Wáng Liàng as Pingnán Cānjūn,
and sent him to convey a letter from General Pingnán and Inspector of Xiāngzhōu, Wèi Tàizhēn, to Grand Commandant Yù.
Tàizhēn
was the younger brother of Gŭzhēn.
18In the ninth month,
on the *dīngsì* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
19In winter,
in the tenth month,
King of Hénán, Chìpán, again proclaimed himself King of Qín
and established his bureaucracy.
Upon succeeding to the throne, Chìpán
had styled himself King of Hénán;
now, having annexed Nánliáng,
he again styled himself King of Qín.
20Yàn Lord Bá allied with Xià.
Xià King Bóbó sent Imperial Censor-in-Chief Wūluògū to Yàn to oversee the covenant.
In the Spring and Autumn period,
when various states resolved enmities and established good relations,
and the two rulers could not meet to form an alliance,
they would certainly send their ministers to oversee the covenant.
The *Zuǒzhuàn* states: Chén Wŭfù went to Zhèng to oversee a covenant, which is this.
Dù Yù said: *lì*
means to supervise.
21In the eleventh month,
on the *rénwŭ* day,
Wèi Lord Sì sent envoys to tour the various *zhōu*,
to inspect the assets of the administrators and prefects.
Anything not brought from home
was all registered as ill-gotten gains.
22Xīqín King Chìpán established a woman of the Tūfà clan as queen.
She
was the daughter of Nŭtán.
23In the twelfth month,
on the *bǐngxū* day, the first day of the month,
Ròurán Khagan Dàtán invaded Wèi.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Wèi Lord Sì attacked them in the north.
Dàtán fled.
Xī Jīn and others were sent to pursue them,
but they encountered heavy snow,
and two or three tenths of the soldiers died from freezing or lost fingers to frostbite.
24Sīmǎ Shùnzǎi of Hénèi proclaimed himself King of Jìn.
The Wèi people attacked him,
but failed to defeat him.
25Yàn Duke of Liáoxī, Sùfú, died.
Yàn King Bá visited his funeral seven times during the burial.
In ancient times, when a high minister died,
the ruler would visit his funeral three times.
*Bǐ*
is pronounced *bì mèi fān*,
meaning "and" or "up to."
26In this year,
Sīmǎ Guófán and his brothers gathered several hundred men and secretly crossed the Huái River,
entering Guǎnglíng City at night.
Zhīzhuàn says: They crossed the Huái from the border of Běixúzhōu.
*Fán*
is pronounced *fú yuán fān*.
Guófán's troops went straight to the administrative office.
Zhī was startled and came out,
intending to resist them. He was shot and wounded, then retreated inside,
and said to his attendants:
"The bandits entered under cover of darkness,
intending to surprise us unprepared;
but just beat the fifth drum,
and they will fear the dawn
and surely flee."
His attendants did as he said,
and Guófán's troops indeed fled.
27Wèi Doctor of the Libations Jìjiǔ Cuī Hào lectured Wèi Lord Sì on the *Yì* and *Hóngfàn*.
Sì then questioned Hào about astronomy and numerology;
Hào's predictions were often accurate,
and thus he gained favor,
participating in all military and state confidential matters.
28Xià King Bóbó established Lady Liáng as queen,
and his son Guī as Crown Prince.
He enfeoffed his son Yán as Duke of Yángpíng,
Chāng as Duke of Tàiyuán,
Lún as Duke of Jiŭquán,
Dìng as Duke of Píngyuán,
Mǎn as Duke of Hénán,
and Ān as Duke of Zhōngshān.
