Emperor Ān, the *rén* year
Yìxī Eleventh Year (Year of the Wood Rabbit, 415 CE)
1 In spring,
the first month,
on the day Bǐngchén,
Wèi Zhǔ Sī returned to Píngchéng.
He had returned from his campaign against the Rouran.
2 Tàiwèi Yù arrested Sīmǎ Xiūzhī's second son Wénbǎo and his nephew Wénzǔ, and granted them death;
he dispatched troops to attack him.
An imperial edict conferred upon Yù the honor of Huángyuè,
and he was made Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
3 On the day Dīngchǒu,
Shè Yù, Shàngshū of Lìbù, was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè.
4 On the day Xīnsì,
Tàiwèi Yù departed from Jiànkāng.
He appointed Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn Liú Dàolián to oversee matters of the留府 (liúfǔ),
and Liú Mùzhī as concurrent Yòu Púyè;
all matters, whether great or small,
were decided by Mùzhī.
He also appointed Gāoyáng Nèishǐ Liú Zhōng to oversee the garrison at Shítou,
and to station troops at Yětíng.
Yětíng
is now called Dōngyětíng,
located behind Bànshān Sì.
From Jiànkāng's east gate, traveling towards Jiǎngshān,
it is halfway there,
hence its name.
Wáng Ānshí's poem says:
"From afar I gaze at the peaks of Zhōngshān,
and thereby know the Yěchéng road."
Lù Yóu said: "Today the Tiānqìng Guān is at the foot of Yěchéng Shān."
All fled back to Jiànkāng.
Yù was
Shào's elder brother.
Zhāng Shào is mentioned in volume 115, year 5.
He and his son, Jìnglíng Tàishǒu Guǐ, raised troops to support Xiūzhī.
In the second month,
Xiūzhī submitted a memorial enumerating Yù's crimes,
and assembled his troops to resist him.
Yù secretly wrote to Hán Yánzhī of Nányáng, who was the Lùshì Cānjūn of Xiūzhī's administration,
and Yánzhī replied:
"I learn that you are personally leading your forces,
traveling far into the western Qí.

According to the Rítuals of Zhōu: beyond a thousand *lǐ* of the royal domain (wángqí) are the domains of the marquises (hóuqí), the imperial demesne (diànqí), the feudal lords (nánqí), the appanages (cǎiqí), the guards (wèiqí), the barbarians (mánqí), the eastern barbarians (yíqí), the frontier garrisons (zhènqí), and the tributaries (fānqí).
They are called *qí* [domains]
because they are responsible for presenting royal taxes and tributes.
Hán Yánzhī refers to Jīngchǔ as the western Qí,
taking this meaning.
The character 帥 is read as *shuài*.
None are not terrified.
I have received your letter,
and learned about the former incident concerning Qiáowáng,
which truly makes me sigh with emotion.
Sīmǎ Píngxī, with his loyalty and steadfastness to the state,
Xiūzhī was Píngxī Jiāngjūn, hence he is referred to as such.
Considering your meritorious service in restoring the state,
on which the family and country rely,
he extended his trust and sincerity,
consulting and looking up to you in every matter.
When Qiáowáng was impeached for a minor matter in the past,
he still memorialized to resign;
the matter is seen in the previous volume, previous year.
劾 (hái) is pronounced *hùgài* (hù-gài) or *hùdé* (hù-dé).
And should he remain silent then!
Previously, he had already memorialized for his removal,
what remains unspoken is only his life.
To trust and rely on each other
should be exactly like this;
推寄 (tuī jì) means to place one's heart into another's belly.
This is what is called,
'If one wishes to condemn someone,
will he lack an excuse!'
This is a saying by Lì Kè, a grandee of Jìn, from the Zuǒzhuàn.
Among the people within the Four Seas,
who does not see your intentions,
yet you still wish to deceive the nation's gentry!
Your letter states, 'harboring intentions and expecting things [from others]
has its own origin.'
Now, to attack another's lord,
and entice people with profit,
can truly be called 'harboring intentions and expecting things,
which has its own origin,'
can it!
Liú Fān died at the gates of Chānghé,
and Zhūgě perished at the hands of his subordinates;
the matter of Liú Fān is seen in the previous volume, year 8;
the matter of Zhūgě is seen in year 9.
To attack him with light forces;
this refers to attacking Liú Yì.
The matter is seen in the previous volume, year 8.
詫 (chà) is pronounced *chǒu'yà* (chǒu-yà).
To have no trustworthy vassals beyond the borders,
and to consider this a clever strategy,
is truly shameful!
The generals and aides of your administration, and the virtuous gentlemen of the court,
are merely living day by day, staking their lives.
I am truly humble and inferior,
but I have learned the Way from gentlemen,
and with Píngxī's supreme virtue,
how could there be no loyal ministers ready to sacrifice their lives for him!
Surely, I cannot throw myself into the tiger's den,
following the example of Xī Sēngshī and his ilk, this is clear.
The matter of Xī Sēngshī is seen in the previous volume, year 8.
郗 (xī) is pronounced *chǒu zhī* (chǒu-zhī).
The Nine Streams are turbid.
Tàishǐ Tán (Tán) listed the Nine Streams in his preface.
Bān Gù said: The stream of the Ruists (Rújiā) probably originated from the office of Sītú,
assisting the ruler in conforming to Yin and Yang,
and clarifying teachings.
The stream of the Daoists (Dàojiā) probably originated from the scribal office (shǐguān),
recording the successes and failures, misfortunes and blessings, and the ways of ancient and modern times;
this is the art of a ruler facing south.
The stream of the Legalists (Fǎjiā) probably originated from the judicial office (lǐguān),
meting out certain rewards and punishments,
to assist the ritual system.
The stream of the Yin-Yang school (Yīnyángjiā) probably originated from the office of Xīhé,
reverently following the August Heaven,
and charting the sun, moon, and stars.
The stream of the Logicians (Míngjiā) probably originated from the ritual office (lǐguān);
in ancient times, ranks and positions differed,
and rituals also varied accordingly.
Confucius said:
"Surely, it is to rectify names!"
The stream of the Mohists (Mòjiā) probably originated from the guardians of the pure temple.
Thatch-roofed houses and raftered eaves,
this is why they valued frugality;
supporting the three elders and five venerable persons,
this is why they practiced universal love;
selecting scholars and holding grand archery contests,
this is why they honored worthies;
ancestral sacrifices to stern fathers,
this is why they revered ghosts.
The stream of the Political Strategists (Cónghéngjiā) probably originated from the office of the traveler (xíngrén).
The stream of the Eclectics (Zájiā) probably originated from the deliberative office (yìguān).
The stream of the Agronomists (Nóngjiā) probably originated from the office of agriculture (nóngjì).
All are branches and descendants of the Six Classics,
beneficial to the art of governance,
but not without flaws;
if they become turbid,
then there will be nothing to take as a balanced mean.
長 (zhǎng) is pronounced *zhīliǎng* (zhī-liǎng).
喪 (sàng) is pronounced *xìlàng* (xì-làng).
The matter of Zāng Hóng is seen in volume 61, Han Xiàndì Xīngpíng year 2.
Yù sighed upon seeing the letter,
and showed it to his generals and aides, saying:
"To serve a person, one should be like this!"
Yánzhī, because Yù's father's given name was Qiáo and his courtesy name was Xiǎnzōng,
changed his own courtesy name to Xiǎnzōng
and named his son Qiáo,
to show his refusal to submit to the Liú clan.
5 Lángyá Tàishǒu Liú Lǎng led over two thousand families to surrender to Wèi.
6 On the day Gēngzǐ,
Héxī Hú Liú Yún and others led tens of thousands of households to surrender to Wèi.
7 Tàiwèi Yù sent Cānjūn Tán Dàojì and Zhū Chāoshí to lead infantry and cavalry out of Xiāngyáng.
Chāoshí was
Língshí's younger brother.
Jiāngxià Tàishǒu Liú Qiánzhī led troops to garrison Sānlián,
building bridges and stockpiling grain to await Dàojì and others,
but they did not arrive for many days.
Lǔ Guǐ attacked Qiánzhī,
and killed him.
Yù sent his son-in-law, Zhènwēi Jiāngjūn Xú Kuízhī of Dōnghǎi, to command Cānjūn Kuǎi Ēn, Wáng Yǔnzhī, and Shěn Yuānzǐ as the vanguard,
to exit Jiāngxiàkǒu.
The Shuǐjīng says: "The Jiāngshǔi passes south of Jiānglíng city,
then goes east to west of Huáróng County,
where the Xiàshuǐ flows out;
then goes east past north of Gōng'ān County,
then goes east to join the Zǐxiàkǒu on the left."
The commentary says: "The Jiāngshǔi veers left to the north,
connecting with the Xiàshuǐ,
hence it is called Zǐxià."
蒯 (kuǎi) is pronounced *kǔguài* (kǔ-guài).
The army was defeated;
Kuízhī, Yǔnzhī, and Yuānzǐ all died,
only Kuǎi Ēn commanded his troops and did not move.
Guǐ, taking advantage of his victory, fiercely attacked them,
but could not overcome them,
and so he retreated.
Yuānzǐ was
Línzǐ's elder brother.
Liú Yù's (劉裕) army was at Mǎtóu (馬頭).
According to the Commentary on the Water Classic,
Mǎtóu Bank (馬頭岸) was on the south bank of the Great River,
facing Jiāngjīn Shù (江津戍) of Jiānglíng (江陵) to the north.
Yù (裕) was furious.
In the third month,
on the Rénwǔ (壬午) day,
he led his generals across the river.
Lǔ Guǐ (魯軌) and Sīmǎ Wénsī (司馬文思) commanded Xīu zhī (休之)'s (休之) army of forty thousand men,
arrayed along the steep bank,
and no soldier was able to ascend.
Yù (裕) himself donned armor and wished to ascend,
but his generals remonstrated.
He did not comply,
growing even more furious.
Xiè Huì (謝晦), the Grand Commandant's chief clerk, stepped forward and held Yù (裕).
Yù (裕) drew his sword and pointed it at Huì (晦), saying:
"I will strike you down!"
Huì (晦) said:
"The world can do without Huì (晦),
but it cannot do without you, my lord!"
This is what Yù (裕) meant when he said Huì (晦) was quite discerning of opportune changes.
Yù (裕) called Hú Fān (胡藩) to ascend.
Fān (藩) showed a hesitant look.
Yù (裕) ordered his attendants to seize him,
intending to execute him.
Lù (錄) [seize],
means shōu (收) [take].
"I am just about to attack the rebels,
I cannot obey your instruction!"
He then used the tip of his saber to pierce the bank,
barely enough to fit his toes,
and sprang up.
Liè (劣) [barely]
means shǎo (少) [little].
Shàng (上) [ascend],
at this time pronounced pān (攀).
Once he ascended the bank,
he charged straight ahead and fought vigorously.
Xiū zhī (休之)'s (休之) troops could not withstand him
and gradually retreated.
When Hú Fān (胡藩) first ascended,
a few dozen elite cavalry could have stopped him,
but Xiū zhī (休之)'s (休之) troops did not move.
Thus, he was able to charge straight ahead and fight vigorously.
Moreover, the hearts of the people had always been intimidated and submissive to Yù (裕),
so once Fān (藩) advanced, they could not withstand him.
Xiū zhī (休之)'s (休之) army was utterly routed,
and Jiānglíng (江陵) was captured.
Xiū zhī (休之) and Zōng zhī (宗之) both fled north,
while Guǐ (軌) remained in Shíchéng (石城).
Yù (裕) ordered Lángzhōnghóu (閬中侯) Zhào Lúnzhī (趙倫之) of Xiàpī (下邳) and Grand Commandant's staff officer Shěn Línzǐ (沈林子) to attack him;
he dispatched Wǔlíng Nèishǐ (武陵內史) Wáng Zhèn'è (王鎮惡) with a naval force to pursue Xiū zhī (休之) and others.
There were several hundred bandits who
attacked Yětíng (冶亭) at night, shaking the capital;
Liú Zhōng (劉鍾) suppressed them.
Qín (秦) Guǎngpíng Gōng (廣平公) Bì (弼) slandered Yáo Xuān (姚宣) to Qín (秦) King Xīng (興).
Last year, when Xuān (宣) came to court,
he vehemently spoke of Bì's (弼) crimes.
Bì (弼) harbored resentment and slandered him.
Xīng (興) reproached Xuān (宣) for his inability to assist and guide,
and intended to execute him.
Pī (丕) was afraid
and falsely accused Xuān (宣) of crimes and evils to exonerate himself.
Xīng (興) was enraged,
and sent an envoy to Xìngchéng (杏城) to arrest Xuān (宣) and imprison him.
He ordered Bì (弼) to lead thirty thousand men to garrison Qínzhōu (秦州).
Yǐn Zhāo (尹昭) said:
"Guǎngpíng Gōng (廣平公) is not on good terms with the Crown Prince.
Now, holding strong troops outside,
if Your Majesty should unexpectedly pass away,
the state will surely be imperiled.
'If one is intolerant in small matters,
one will spoil a great plan.'"
This is recorded as the words of Kǒngzǐ (孔子) in the Analects.
Xīng (興) did not comply.
Xià (夏) King Bóbó (勃勃) attacked Qín (秦)'s Xìngchéng (杏城),
captured it,
seized its defending general Yáo Kuí (姚逵),
and massacred two thousand soldiers.
Qín (秦) King Xīng (興) went to Běidì (北地),
and dispatched Guǎngpíng Gōng (廣平公) Bì (弼) and Fǔguó Jiāngjūn (輔國將軍) Liǎn Mànwéi (斂曼嵬) towards Xīnpíng (新平).
Xīng (興) then returned to Cháng'ān (長安).
Héxī (河西) King Méngxùn (蒙遜) attacked Xī Qín (西秦)'s Guǎngwǔ Jùn (廣武郡),
and captured it.
Xī Qín (西秦) King Chìpán (熾磐) sent General Qífú Tuíníyín (乞伏魋尼寅) to intercept Méngxùn (蒙遜) at Hàowěi (浩亹).
Méngxùn (蒙遜) attacked and killed him.
He also sent General Zhéfěi (折斐) and others to lead ten thousand cavalry to hold Lèjiě Lǐng (勒姐嶺).
According to Kàn Yīnzhì (闞駰志),
east of Ānyí Xiàn (安夷縣) in Jīnchéng (金城) there is Lèjiě Hé (勒姐河),
which joins Jīnchéng Hé (金城河).
Lèjiě Lǐng (勒姐嶺) is likely the mountain where Lèjiě Hé (勒姐河) originates.
During the Hàn (漢) dynasty,
the Lèjiě Qiāng (勒姐羌) resided there,
hence the name.
Jiě (姐) is
pronounced zǐ (子) again,
also sound zǐ (紫).
Starving Hú (胡) people from Héxī (河西) gathered at Shàngdǎng (上黨),
and enthroned the Hú (胡) man Bái Yàlìsī (白亞栗斯) as Chányú (單于),
changing the era name to Jiànpíng (建平).
They made Sīmǎ Shùnzǎi (司馬順宰) their chief strategist.
Shùnzǎi (順宰) had raised an army,
as seen in Volume 2 of the previous scroll.
In summer,
the fourth month,
Wèi (魏) Lord Sì (嗣) ordered Gōngsūn Biǎo (公孫表) and four other generals to suppress them.
Sīmǎ Dàocì (司馬道賜), a staff officer to Liú Jìngxuan (劉敬宣), the Inspector of Qīng (青) and Jì (冀) provinces,
was a distant relative of the imperial clan.
Hearing that Grand Commandant Yù (裕) was attacking Sīmǎ Xiūzhī (司馬休之),
Dàocì (道賜), along with Pìlǘ Dàoxiù (辟閭道秀) of the same office,
Dàocì (道賜) and Dàoxiù (道秀) were both subordinates of Jìngxuan (敬宣),
hence it is said "of the same office."
seized Guǎnggù (廣固) to respond to Xiūzhī (休之).
On the Yǐmǎo (乙卯) day,
Jìngxuan (敬宣) summoned Dàoxiù (道秀),
and spoke to him privately, dismissing all his attendants from the room.
Měngzǐ (猛子) lingered behind,
and took Jìngxuan's (敬宣) personal knife to kill him.
The civil and military officials immediately attacked Dàocì (道賜) and his accomplices,
and executed them all.
On the Jǐmǎo (己卯) day,
Wèi (魏) Lord Sì (嗣) went on a northern tour.
Xī Qín (西秦) King Chìpán's (熾磐) son Yuánjī (元基) fled from Cháng'ān (長安) back home.
Yuánjī (元基) had likely followed Chìpán (熾磐) into Qín (秦) to pay respects at court,
and subsequently stayed in Cháng'ān (長安).
In the fifth month,
on the Dīnghài (丁亥) day,
Wèi (魏) Lord Sì (嗣) went to Dàníng (大甯).
Zhào Lúnzhī (趙倫之) and Shěn Línzǐ (沈林子) defeated Lǔ Guǐ (魯軌) at Shíchéng (石城).
Sīmǎ Xiūzhī (司馬休之) and Lǔ Zōngzhī (魯宗之) arrived too late to rescue him,
and so fled with Guǐ (軌) to Xiāngyáng (襄陽).
Zōngzhī's (宗之) staff officer Lǐ Yìngzhī (李應之) closed the gates and refused them entry.
On the Jiǎwǔ (甲午) day,
Xiūzhī (休之), Zōngzhī (宗之), Guǐ (軌), as well as Qiáo (譙) King Wénsī (文思) and Xīncài (新蔡) King Dàocì (道賜),
this is another Sīmǎ Dàocì (司馬道賜).
Xīncài (新蔡) King Huǎng (晃) was deposed due to the affair of Wǔlíng (武陵) King Xī (晞),
and later Dàocì (道賜) inherited the title.
Zōngzhī (宗之) had always enjoyed the support of the gentry and common people,
who vied to escort him out of the territory.
Wáng Zhèn'è (王鎮惡) and others pursued them,
returning once they reached the border.
They dared not exhaust their troops in pursuit,
fearing an ambush if they crossed the border.
Initially,
Xiūzhī (休之) and others had sought aid from Qín (秦) and Wèi (魏).
Qín (秦)'s Zhēnglǔ Jiāngjūn (征虜將軍) Yáo Chéngwáng (姚成王) and Sīmǎ Guóyáng (司馬國璠) led troops to Nányáng (南陽).
Wèi (魏)'s Zhǎngsūn Sōng (長孫嵩) reached Hédōng (河東).
Hearing of the defeat of Xiūzhī (休之) and others,
they all withdrew.
When Xiūzhī (休之) arrived in Cháng'ān (長安),
Qín (秦) King Xīng (興) appointed him Inspector of Yángzhōu (揚州),
and sent him to harass Xiāngyáng (襄陽).
Shìyùshǐ (侍御史) Táng Shèng (唐盛) said to Xīng (興):
"According to the texts of prognostications,
the Sīmǎ (司馬) clan is destined to regain the Hé (河) and Luò (洛) regions.
Now to send Xiūzhī (休之) with troops outside
is like releasing a fish into the abyss.
It would be better to keep him in the capital
with high titles and generous gifts."
Xīng (興) said:
"In the past, King Wén (文) was finally released from Yǒulǐ (羑里).
Zhòu (紂) imprisoned King Wén (文) at Yǒulǐ (羑里),
then released him.
Fù (復) [regain],
pronounced fú yòu fān (扶又翻).
Zú (卒) [finally],
pronounced zǐ xù fān (子恤翻).
See Volume 9, Hàn (漢) Gāozǔ (高祖) first year.
Who can resist destiny!
If it is as the prognostications say,
keeping him here would only cause harm."
So he sent him away.
The historian says Yáo Xīng (姚興) understood fate.
An imperial edict added the titles Grand Preceptor and Inspector of Yángzhōu (揚州) to Grand Commandant Yù (裕),
granting him the privilege to enter the hall with swords and shoes on,
to not hurry when entering court,
and to have his name not called when bowing.

Liú Dàolián (劉道憐), Inspector of Yǎn (兗) and Qīng (青) provinces, was appointed Overall Commander of military affairs in the seven provinces of Jīng (荊), Xiāng (湘), Yì (益), Qín (秦), Níng (寧), Liáng (梁), and Yōng (雍), General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of Jīngzhōu (荊州).
Dàolián (道憐) was greedy, petty,
and lacked talent. Yù (裕) appointed Xiè Fāngmíng (謝方明), Central Army Chief Clerk and Administrator of Jìnlíng (晉陵), as Chief Clerk of the Agile Cavalry and Grand Administrator of Nánjùn (南郡).
All matters in Dàolián's (道憐) administration were decided after consulting Fāngmíng (方明).
Fāngmíng (方明) was Chōng zhī (沖之)'s son.
Xiè Chōng (謝沖) was Yì (奕)'s cousin.
Fāngmíng (方明) was Yù's (裕) paternal cousin (from his father's generation).
Zhū Língshí (朱齡石), Inspector of Yìzhōu (益州), sent an envoy to Héxī (河西) King Méngxùn (蒙遜),
to explain the prestige and virtue of the imperial court.
Méngxùn (蒙遜) sent his attendant Huáng Xùn (黃迅) to Língshí (齡石),
and also submitted a memorial saying:
"I humbly hear that General of Chariots and Cavalry Yù (裕) wishes to pacify the Central Plains.
I wish to be his right flank,
to drive out the barbarians."
Xià (夏) King Bóbó (勃勃) sent the Imperial Censor-in-chief Wūluògū (烏洛孤) to form an alliance with Méngxùn (蒙遜).
Méngxùn (蒙遜) sent his younger brother, Huánghé Tàishǒu (湟河太守) Hàn Píng (漢平), to conclude the alliance in Xià (夏).
In the 20th year, Qīpán (熾磐), King of Western Qín, led a force of 30,000 to attack Huánghé (湟河).
Jǔqú Hànpíng (沮渠漢平) resisted them.
He dispatched Sīmǎ Wěi Rén (司馬隗仁) to sortie at night and attack Qīpán (熾磐),
defeating him.
Qīpán (熾磐) was about to withdraw,
when Hànpíng's (漢平) Chángshǐ Jiāo Chǎng (長史焦昶) and Jiāngjūn Duàn Jǐng (將軍段景) secretly invited Qīpán (熾磐) back.
Qīpán (熾磐) attacked again.
Chǎng (昶) and Jǐng (景) then persuaded Hànpíng (漢平) to surrender.
Wěi Rén (隗仁) commanded over a hundred brave warriors to hold the southern gate tower.
For three days, it did not fall.
When their strength was exhausted,
Wěi Rén (隗仁) was captured by Qīpán (熾磐).
Qīpán (熾磐) intended to execute him.
Sànqí Chángshì (散騎常侍) Duàn Huī (段暉) of Wǔwēi (武威) remonstrated, saying:
"Rén (仁) did not fear death in the face of peril.
It is fitting to pardon him to encourage loyalty to one's lord."
So, he was imprisoned.
Qīpán (熾磐) appointed Zuǒwèi Jiāngjūn (左衞將軍) Pǐ Dá (匹達) as the Grand Administrator of Huánghé (湟河).
He then attacked Yǐfú Kūgān (乙弗窟乾),
subjugating over 3,000 households before returning.
He appointed Shàngshū Yòupúyè (尚書右僕射) Chūlián Qián (出連虔) as Dūdū Lǐngběi Zhū Jūnshì (都督嶺北諸軍事).
Lǐngběi (嶺北)
refers to the north of Hóngchí Lǐng (洪池嶺).
He appointed Liángzhōu Cìshǐ (涼州刺史) Qiān Tún (謙屯) as Zhèn Jūn Dà Jiāngjūn (鎮軍大將軍) and Hézhōu Mù (河州牧).
Wěi Rén (隗仁) remained in Western Qín for five years.
Duàn Huī (段暉) again pleaded on his behalf.
The history books refer to Duàn Huī (段暉) of Wǔwēi (武威)
to distinguish him from Duàn Huī (段暉) of Southern Yàn.
He was then allowed to return to Gūzāng (姑臧).
On the day of Wùwǔ (戊午),
Wèi Zhǔ Sī (魏主嗣) traveled to Rúyuán (濡源),
then reached Shànggǔ (上谷), Zhuōlù (涿鹿), and Guǎngníng (廣甯).
Zhuōlù (涿鹿) county
belonged to Shànggǔ (上谷) Commandery during the Hàn dynasty.
Jìn divided it to belong to Guǎngníng (廣甯) Commandery.
According to Wèi Tǔdì Jì (魏土地記), sixty lì southeast of Xiàluò (下洛) county is Zhuōlù (涿鹿) City.
One hundred and thirty lì northwest is Dàníng (大甯) City,
which is the Hàn Guǎngníng (廣甯) county.
This was probably within the borders of Táng Guīzhōu (唐媯州).
In the seventh month,
on the day of Guǐwèi (癸未),
he returned to Píngchéng (平城).
Qīpán (熾磐), King of Western Qín, appointed Qínzhōu Cìshǐ (秦州刺史) Tán Dá (曇達) as Shàngshū Lìng (尚書令).
Guānglù Xūn (光祿勳) Wáng Sōngshòu (王松壽) was appointed Qínzhōu Cìshǐ (秦州刺史).
On the last day of Xīnhài (辛亥),
there was a solar eclipse.
In the eighth month,
on the day of Jiǎzǐ (甲子),
Tàiwèi Yù (太尉裕) returned to Jiànkāng (建康).
He firmly declined the titles of Tàifù (太傅) and Zhōumù (州牧),
but accepted the other appointments.
Yùzhāng Gōng (豫章公) Shìzǐ Yìfú (世子義符) was appointed Yǎnzhōu Cìshǐ (兗州刺史).
On the day of Dīngwèi (丁未),
Xiè Yù (謝裕) died.
Liú Mùzhī (劉穆之) was appointed Zuǒpúyè (左僕射).
In the ninth month,
on the day of Jǐhài (己亥),
a general amnesty was declared.
For successive years, Wèi experienced frost and drought.
Many people in Yún (雲) and Dài (代) died of starvation.
Yún (雲) and Dài (代)
refer to the regions of Yúnzhōng (雲中) and Dàijùn (代郡) commanderies.
"According to the prognostication texts,
Wèi should establish its capital at Yè (鄴),
then it can achieve abundance and happiness."
Sī (嗣) asked his ministers about this.
Bóshì Jìjiǔ (博士祭酒) Cuī Hào (崔浩) and Tèjìn (特進) Zhōu Dàn (周澹) of Jīngzhào (京兆) replied:
"Moving the capital to Yè (鄴)
might relieve this year's famine,
but it is not a long-term plan.
The people east of the mountains
consider our state to be situated in a vast land,
"Guǎnghàn" (廣漢)
is rendered as "Guǎngmò" (廣漠) in the 'Biography of Cuī Hào' in the Běi Shǐ;
this should be followed.
Mò (漠) means 'vast'.
They call us 'the myriad as ox hair'.
If we now leave troops to guard the old capital,
referring to Píngchéng (平城),
they will not be able to fill the lands of the various prefectures.
When mixed among the counties and districts,
our true situation will be revealed,
and we fear that all four directions will harbor contempt.
Moreover, the common people will not be accustomed to the climate and soil,
and there will certainly be many deaths and injuries from illness and epidemics.
Furthermore,
with few troops guarding the old capital,
Qūgài (屈丐) and Ròurán (柔然) will harbor intentions of prying and invading.
If they come with their entire nation,
Yúnzhōng (雲中) and Píngchéng (平chéng) will surely be in peril.
The court will be separated by the thousand-lì barrier of Héng (恆) and Dài (代).
From Héngshān (恆山) to Dài (代),
there are the passes of Fēihú (飛狐) and Dàomǎ (倒馬),
and the strategic points of Xiàwū (夏屋), Guǎngchāng (廣昌), and Wǔhuí (五迴).
This would result in a loss of both reputation and actual strength.
If we remain in the north,
suppose there is a change in the east of the mountains,
our light cavalry can move south,
spreading through the forests and thickets.
Who would know their numbers?
The common people would be awestruck at the sight of dust,
this is how our state exerts its authority over the Central Plains.
Next spring, when the grass grows,
milk and cheese will be produced.
The Western Hàn dynasty had an official subordinate to the Grand Coachman called Dòngmǎ (挏馬).
Yīng Shào (應劭) said: He was in charge of milking horses and extracting their juice.
He would agitate and process it,
and it would taste sour and be drinkable, hence the name of the office.
Rú Chún (如淳) said: He was in charge of milking horses, using a leather pouch that held several dòu.
He would put horse milk in it,
agitate it to extract the rich cream on top,
and thus it was named Dòngmǎ (挏馬).
Today, in Liángzhōu (梁州), fermented horse milk is called horse wine.
Shī Gǔ (師古) said: Dòng (挏)
is pronounced as 'tú kǒng'.
If we can wait until the autumn harvest,
then the matter will be resolved."
Sī (嗣) said:
"Our granaries are now empty.
We have no means to wait until next autumn.
If next autumn there is still famine,
what shall we do?"
They replied:
"It is advisable to select the poor and hungry households
and send them to the three prefectures east of the mountains for food.
If there is still famine next autumn,
we should then make further plans,
but for now, the capital cannot be moved."
Sī (嗣) said with pleasure:
"Only these two share my opinion."
Thereupon, he selected the poorest among the people of the state and sent them to the three prefectures east of the mountains for food.
The Tuòbá (拓跋) clan originated in the Mòběi (漠北),
governing thirty-six states
and ninety-nine surnames.
After Dàowǔ (道武) unified the Central Plains,
he moved their elites to Yún (雲) and Dài (代),
where they mixed with the northern people.
Their northern tribal people were called 'people of the state'.
The three prefectures east of the mountains
were Dìng (定), Xiāng (相), and Jì (冀).
In the early Wèi,
eight senior officials were set up in the four cardinal and four intercardinal directions,
divided into East, West, South, North, Left, Right, Front, and Rear.
Later, eight Department Heads were also set up.
According to the Wèi Shū Guānshì Zhì (魏書官氏志), Tuòbá Lín (拓跋鄰) made his second elder brother into the Pǔ (普) clan,
which was later changed to the Zhōu (周) clan.
It is likely that when Wèi established Dàidū (代都),
Zhōu Jǐ (周幾) became a person of Dài (代).
He also ordered officials to encourage farming and sericulture.
The following year,
there was a great harvest,
and the people became prosperous and secure.
In the summer, Hèlián Jiàn (赫連建) led troops to attack Qín (秦).
He captured Píngliáng (平涼) Grand Administrator Yáo Jūn (姚軍)
and then entered Xīnpíng (新平).
Guǎngpíng Gōng (廣平公) Bì (弼) fought him at Lóngwěi Bǎo (龍尾堡).
Liú Xù's (劉昫) Dìlǐ Zhì (地理志) states: In Fèngxiáng Fǔ (鳳翔府), Qíshān (岐山) county,
in the seventh year of Táng Wǔdé (唐武德),
the administrative seat was moved to Lóngwěi Chéng (龍尾城).
29 Qín Wáng Yáo Xīng became ill.
Guǎngpíng Gōng Yáo Bì feigned sickness and did not attend court,
gathering soldiers at his residence.
Xīng heard of this,
and in a rage,
arrested Bì's associates, Táng Shèng and Sūn Xuán, among others,
and killed them.
Crown Prince Yáo Hóng pleaded, saying:
"Your unworthy servant
has been unable to harmonize relations among his brothers.
'Jī' (緝)
should be 'jí' (輯).
All are your servant's faults.
If your servant's death would bring peace to the state,
I wish you would grant me death;
if Your Majesty cannot bear to kill your servant,
I beg to retire to a fief."
Xīng felt a pang of pity for him,
and summoned Yáo Zàn, Liáng Xǐ, Yǐn Zhāo, and Liǎn Mànwéi to consult with them.
He imprisoned Bì,
intending to kill him,
and thoroughly investigate his associates.
Hóng tearfully pleaded earnestly,
so Xīng pardoned Bì and his associates.
Hóng treated Bì as before,
showing no signs of resentment.
30 The Wèi Grand Astrologer reported:
"Yínghuò (Mars) is within the Gourd constellation (Páoguā),
according to the astronomical treatise of the Jìnshū: the Gourd constellation is south of the Heavenly Ford (Tiānjīn),
with the Heavenly River (Tiānhàn) dividing and flowing between them.
Zhāng Yuān's commentary on the 'Guānxiàng Fù' states: The five stars of the Gourd are north of Lìzhū,
and the nine stars of the Heavenly Ford are north of the Gourd.
By rule, it should enter a state facing danger and ruin,
first with children's rhymes and ominous rumors,
and then its calamity and punishment will follow."
'Fǎ' (法)
refers to the regular method of astrological prediction.
'Yāo' (妖)
is pronounced 'yú jiāo fān'.
Cuī Hào responded:
"According to the Zuǒzhuàn of the Chūnqiū: 'A spirit descended upon Shēn,'
and by the day of its arrival, its nature could be deduced.
Hào probably referred to the 'Wàizhuàn' (External Commentary) of the Zuǒzhuàn of the Chūnqiū.
The 'Wàizhuàn' says:
'In the fifteenth year of King Huì of Zhōu,
a spirit descended upon Shēn.
The King asked the Grand Scribe Guò.
He replied: "Is it Dānzhū?"
The King asked: "Who will receive it?"
He replied: "In the land of Guó."
The King asked: "How long will Guó last?"
He replied: "In the past, Yáo ruled the people with the five virtues.
Now his descendant appears.
The appearance of the spirit
does not exceed its nature.
If we look at it this way,
it will not be more than five years."
In the nineteenth year,
Jìn conquered Guó."
'Zhuàn' (傳)
is pronounced 'zhí liàn fān'.
On the Gēngwǔ
and Xīnwèi days,
the sky was cloudy;
the disappearance of Yínghuò
must have occurred on those two days.
Gēng and Wǔ
both correspond to Qín;
Xīn represents the Western barbarians.
The astronomical treatise of the Jìnshū states: From the sixteenth degree of Dōngjǐng (Eastern Well) to the eighth degree of Liǔ (Willow) is Qúnshǒu,
corresponding to Zhū in the earthly branches,
which is the celestial division of Qín.
From the ninth degree of Liǔ to the twelfth degree of Zhāng (Extended Net) is Qúnhuǒ,
corresponding to Wǔ in the earthly branches,
which is the celestial division of Zhōu.
At that time, Yáo Qín also held the lands of Guān and Luò,
hence it is said that 'both correspond to Qín.'
Gēng and Xīn are the west,
hence they represent the Western barbarians.
Yínghuò will certainly enter Qín."
Everyone angrily said:
"A star disappears from the heavens,
how can humans know where it goes!"
Hào laughed and did not respond.
More than eighty days later,
Yínghuò emerged from Dōngjǐng,
lingered at Gōují,
and then departed after a long time.
The astronomical treatise of the Xīntángshū states:
"To depart and return is called Gōují."
The astronomical treatise of the Jìnshū states:
"Yínghuò brings disorder,
brings bandits,
brings sickness,
brings mourning,
brings famine,
brings war,
and the country it dwells in suffers calamity.
If it circles Gōují,
and its rays shake and change color,
sometimes moving forward, sometimes backward,
sometimes left, sometimes right,
its calamity is even more severe."
'Jù' (句)
is pronounced 'gōu'.
Gōují
means to circle and move like a hook,
and also forms the character 'jǐ'.
The Kūnmíng Pond dried up,
children's rhymes and rumors spread,
'tú gē' (徒歌) is called 'yáo' (謠).
One year later, Qín perished.
Only then did everyone admire Hào's profound insight.
31 In winter,
in the tenth month,
on the day Rénzǐ,
Qín Wáng Yáo Xīng sent the Sanqí Chángshì Yáo Chǎng and others to escort his daughter, Princess Xīpíng, to Wèi.
'Sǎn' (散)
is pronounced 'xī dǎn fān'.
'Qí' (騎)
is pronounced 'qí jì fān';
the same below.
The gold figures were not successfully cast.
When Wèi established an heir or a empress,
they would cast gold figures to divine for it.
Yet, she was treated with great favor.
32 On the day Xīnyǒu,
Wèi Zhǔ Tuòbá Sì went to Jǔrùchéng;
on the day Guǐhài,
he returned to Píngchéng.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīnghài,
he again went to Cháishān Gōng;
on the day Gēngzǐ,
he returned.
33 Xīqín Wáng Qífú Chìpán dispatched Xiāngwǔ Hóu Tán Dá and others to lead ten thousand cavalry to attack the Southern Qiāng Míjiě and Kāngbó at Chìshuǐ,
and subjugated them.
The Shuǐjīng Zhù states: Chìtíngshuǐ flows out from the eastern mountains of Nán'ān Jùn at Chìgǔ,
flows west,
passes north of the city,
and enters the Wèishuǐ from the south.
'Tán' (曇)
is pronounced 'tú hán fān'.
'Jiāng' (將)
is pronounced 'jí liàng fān'.
'Jiě' (姐)
is pronounced 'zǐ yě fān',
also 'zǐ' (紫).
'Jiàng' (降)
is pronounced 'hù jiāng fān'.
He garrisoned Chìshuǐ.
34 Yān Shàngshū Lìng Sūn Hù's younger brother Bó Rén was the Yin of Chānglí.
He and his younger brother Chìzhī Yǐbá were both talented and brave,
having rendered meritorious service when they joined Yān Wáng Fēng Bá's uprising.
This refers to the time when Muróng Xī was killed; the event is recorded in volume 114, third year.
They uttered discontented remarks,
and Bá killed them both.
He promoted Hù to Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, Lù Shàngshū Shì,
to appease him,
but Hù remained sullen and displeased.
Bá poisoned him to death.
Liáodōng Tàishǒu Wù Yíntí, considering himself meritorious,
was sent out to a border commandery.
He harbored resentment and harbored intentions of external rebellion,
so Bá also killed him.
Since Wàn Ní and Rǔ Chén had already died,
and Sūn Hù's brothers and Wù Yíntí were also executed,
Fēng Bá was indeed lacking in benevolence.
35 Línyì raided Jiāozhōu,
and the provincial governor defeated them.
1 In spring,
in the first month,
on the day Jiǎshēn,
Wèi Zhǔ Tuòbá Sì went to Cháishān Gōng;
on the day Wùzǐ,
he returned to Píngchéng.
2 Tàiwèi Liú Yù was given the additional title of Yǎnzhōu Cìshǐ and Dūdū Nánqínzhōu,
overseeing twenty-two provinces in total.
The twenty-two provinces are: Xú, Nánxú, Yù, Nányù, Yǎn, Nányǎn, Qīng, Jì, Yōu, Bìng, Sī, Yǐng, Jīng, Jiāng, Xiāng, Yōng, Liáng, Yì, Níng, Jiāo, Guǎng, and Nánqín.
3 Qín Wáng Yáo Xīng sent Lǔ Zōngzhī to lead troops to raid Xiāngyáng,
but Zōngzhī died before arriving.
His son, Lǔ Guǐ, led the troops to raid the area,
but Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Zhào Lúnzhī defeated them.
4 Xīqín Wáng Qífú Chìpán attacked Qín Táoyáng Gōng Péng Lìhé at Qiāngchuān,
and Jǔqú Méngxùn attacked Shíquán to rescue him.
Chìpán reached Tàzhōng
and then withdrew.
In the second month,
Chìpán sent Xiāngwǔ Hóu Tán Dá to rescue Shíquán,
and Méngxùn also withdrew.
Méngxùn then made a peace alliance with Chìpán.
Since Chìpán had annihilated the Tūfǎ clan,
he had become a neighbor and enemy to Méngxùn,
engaging in battles year after year,
but now they formed an alliance.
5 Emperor Yáo Xīng 姚興 of Qín 秦 went to Huá'yīn 華陰,
and sent Crown Prince Yáo Hóng 姚泓 to supervise the state,
residing in the Western Palace.
The Crown Prince usually resided in the Eastern Palace;
the Western Palace
was where Emperor Yáo Xīng 姚興 lived.
He then returned to Cháng'ān 長安.
Huángmén Shìláng 尹沖 Yǐn Chōng plotted to kill Yáo Hóng 姚泓 when he came out to welcome Yáo Xīng 姚興.
When Yáo Xīng 姚興 arrived,
Yáo Hóng 姚泓 was about to go out to welcome him,
but his palace officials advised him, saying:
All officials of the Eastern Palace are called palace officials.
"The sovereign is seriously ill,
and treacherous officials are at his side.
'Treacherous officials' refers to Yǐn Chōng 尹沖 and others.
We cannot see the sovereign to advance,
and when we retreat, there will be unforeseen disaster."
Yáo Hóng 姚泓 said:
"As a subject and son, when I hear that my lord and father is gravely ill, how can I sit still and not go out [to see him]?
How can I feel at ease!"
They replied:
"To preserve one's body to secure the state is the greatest filial piety."
Yáo Hóng 姚泓 then stopped.
Shàngshū 姚沙彌 Yáo Shāmí said to Yǐn Chōng 尹沖:
"Since the Crown Prince is not coming out to welcome him,
we should escort the imperial carriage to the residence of Gǔangpíng Gōng 廣平公;
when the imperial guards hear where the imperial carriage is,
they will naturally gather.
Who will the Crown Prince guard with?
Moreover, because of Gǔangpíng Gōng 廣平公,
we have already incurred the name of rebels.
Where will we find refuge?
Now, by escorting the imperial carriage to carry out our plan,
we are acting with great righteousness.
Not only will this save Gǔangpíng's 廣平 disaster,
but our previous crimes will also be completely cleared."
Yǐn Chōng 尹沖, however, did not know if Yáo Xīng 姚興 was dead or alive,
and wished to follow Yáo Xīng 姚興 into the palace to cause chaos,
so he did not use Yáo Shāmí's 姚沙彌 words.
Yáo Xīng 姚興 entered the palace,
and ordered Crown Prince Yáo Hóng 姚泓 to record the affairs of the Shàngshū 尚書,
and Dōngpíng Gōng 姚 Shào 東平公紹 and Yòuwèi Jiāngjūn 胡翼度 Hú Yìdù to command troops within the forbidden palace,
controlling internal and external matters.
Yáo Shào 姚紹
was Yáo Xīng's 姚興 brother.
[He] entered the arsenal.
Jìn 晉 first established the Diànzhōng Jiāngjūn 殿中將軍,
and Yáo Qín 姚秦 later had the Diànzhōng Shàngjiāngjūn 殿中上將軍,
who commanded all the principal commanders within the palace.
Yáo Xīng's 姚興 illness worsened.
His younger sister, Nán'ān Cháng Gōngzhǔ 南安長公主, asked about his illness,
but he did not respond.
His youngest son Gēng'ér 耕兒 came out
and told his elder brother Nányáng Gōng Yáo Yīn 南陽公姚愔:
"The sovereign has already passed away;
we should quickly decide on a plan."
Yáo Yīn 姚愔 immediately led armored soldiers with Yǐn Chōng 尹沖 to attack the Duānmén 端門,
while Liǎn Mànwéi 斂曼嵬, Hú Yìdù 胡翼度, and others mustered troops and closed the gates to resist.
Yáo Yīn 姚愔 and his group sent brave men to climb the gate
and enter via the rooftops,
reaching the Mǎdào 馬道.
Yáo Hóng 姚泓 was attending to the sick Yáo Xīng 姚興 in the Zīyì Táng 諮議堂.
Tàizǐ Yòuwèi Shuài 姚和都 Yáo Hédū led the Eastern Palace troops to garrison the south of the Mǎdào 馬道.
Yáo Yīn 姚愔 and his group could not advance,
so they burned the Duānmén 端門.
Yáo Xīng 姚興, despite his illness, went to the front hall
and granted Bì 弼 death.
When the forbidden troops saw Yáo Xīng 姚興,
they rejoiced and eagerly rushed forward to attack the rebels.
The rebel forces were shocked and disturbed;
Yáo Hédū 姚和都 attacked them from behind with the Eastern Palace troops,
and Yáo Yīn 姚愔 and his group were greatly defeated.
Yáo Yīn 姚愔 fled to Líshān 驪山.
His accomplice, Jiànkāng Gōng Lǚ Lóng 建康公呂隆, fled to Yōng 雍,
and Yǐn Chōng 尹沖 and his younger brother Yáo Hóng 姚泓 came to surrender.
Yáo Xīng 姚興 summoned Dōngpíng Gōng Yáo Shào 東平公紹 and Yáo Zàn 姚讚, Liáng Xǐ 梁喜, Yǐn Zhāo 尹昭, Liǎn Mànwéi 斂曼嵬 into his inner chambers
to receive his last will and assist in governance.
The next day,
Yáo Xīng 姚興 died.
He was fifty-one years old.
The Kǎoyì 考異 says: "The Jìn Běnjì 晉本紀 and Sānshí Guó Jìn Chūnqiū 三十國·晉春秋 all state that Yáo Xīng 姚興 died in the second month of the eleventh year of Yìxī 義熙;
the Wèi Běnjì 魏本紀 and Běi Shǐ Běnjì 北史本紀,
and the Yáo Xīng Zàijì 姚興載記 and Yáo Hóng Zàijì 姚泓載記 all state the twelfth year."
According to the Hòu Wèi Shū 后魏書, Cuī Hóng Zhuàn 崔鴻傳: "In the second year of Tàizǔ Tiānxīng 太祖天興,
Yáo Xīng 姚興 changed his reign title,
which Cuī Hóng 崔鴻 considered the first year.
Therefore, all events after Hóngshǐ 弘始 in the Jìn Běnjì 晉本紀 and Sānshí Guó Jìn Chūnqiū 三十國·晉春秋
are listed one year earlier.
This is due to Cuī Hóng's 崔鴻 error."
Nányáng Gōng Yáo Yīn 南陽公姚愔, Lǚ Lóng 呂隆, Dàjiāngjūn Yǐn Yuán 大將軍尹元, and others were captured
and all executed.
Then, the mourning was announced,
and Yáo Hóng 姚泓 ascended the throne as emperor.
Yáo Hóng 姚泓,
courtesy name Yuánzǐ 元子,
was Yáo Xīng's 姚興 eldest son.
He changed the reign title to Yǒnghé 永和.
Yáo Hóng 姚泓 ordered Qí Gōng Yáo Huī 齊公恢 to kill the prefect of Āndìng 安定, Lǚ Chāo 呂超.
Lǚ Lóng 呂隆 and Lǚ Chāo 呂超
were brothers
and both sided with Bì 弼.
Qí Gōng Yáo Huī 齊公恢 was stationed in Āndìng 安定 at the time.
So he killed him.
Yáo Hóng 姚泓 suspected Yáo Huī 姚恢 of disloyalty,
and Yáo Huī 姚恢, consequently afraid,
secretly gathered troops and plotted rebellion.
This sets the stage for Yáo Huī's 姚恢 later rebellion.
Yáo Xīng 姚興 was posthumously given the title Wénhuán Huángdì 文桓皇帝,
and his temple name was Gāozǔ 高祖.
Previously,
Yáo Xīng 姚興 had resettled three thousand households of the Lǐrùn Qiāng 李閏羌 to Āndìng 安定.
When Yáo Xīng 姚興 died,
the Qiāng 羌 chieftain Dǎng Róng 党容 rebelled.
Sūn Mǐn 孫愐 said: "Dǎng 党 was originally a falling tone,
now an upper tone.
Originally from the Western Qiāng 羌."
Yáo Qín 姚秦 had a general named Dǎng Nàihǔ 党耐虎,
who claimed to be a descendant of Xiàhòushì 夏后氏 and was a Qiāng 羌 chieftain.
Chieftain (qiú 酋) is pronounced cí-yóu (慈由翻);
the same below.
Dǎng 党 is pronounced dǐ-lǎng (底朗翻).
Their chieftains were resettled in Cháng'ān 長安,
and the rest were sent back to Lǐrùn 李閏.
Běidì Tàishǒu Máo Yōng 北地太守毛雍 rebelled by occupying Zhào Shì Wù 趙氏塢.
Zhào Shì Wù 趙氏塢 was the place where Qín Zhǔ Jiān 秦主堅 was garrisoned when he attacked Hòu Qín 后秦 in the ninth year of Xiàowǔ Tàiyuán 孝武太元.
At that time, Yáo Xuān 姚宣 was stationed in Lǐrùn 李閏.
Cānjūn Wéi Zōng 參軍韋宗, hearing of Máo Yōng's 毛雍 rebellion,
advised Yáo Xuān 姚宣, saying:
"The sovereign has just ascended the throne,
and his prestige and virtue are not yet established.
The difficulties facing the state
cannot be measured,
Your Highness must consider this deeply.
Xíngwàng 邢望 is a strategic point;
it would be advisable to move and occupy it.
This is the capital for a hegemon."
Yáo Xuān 姚宣 followed his advice,
leading thirty-eight thousand households,
abandoned Lǐrùn 李閏,
and moved south to secure Xíngwàng 邢望.
The various Qiāng 羌 occupied Lǐrùn 李閏 and rebelled.
Dōngpíng Gōng Yáo Shào 東平公紹 advanced to suppress them
and defeated them.
Yáo Xuān 姚宣 went to Yáo Shào 姚紹 to confess his crime,
and Yáo Shào 姚紹 killed him.
6 In the second month, Tàiwèi Liú Yù 太尉裕 was appointed Grand Commander of Internal and External Affairs.
Liú Yù 裕 prepared for an expedition against Qín 秦.
An imperial edict appointed Liú Yù 裕 as Intendant of Sī 司 and Yù 豫 Provinces,
and his eldest son, Liú Yìfú 劉義符, as Intendant of Xú 徐 and Yǎn 兗 Provinces.
Lángxié Wáng Déwén 琅邪王德文 requested to initiate the military campaign.
The Shī 詩 says:
"Ten chariots of the grand army
lead the way."
Xíng 行 is pronounced hù-gāng (戶剛翻).
The imperial edict granted his request.
7 In summer,
on the day Rénzǐ 壬子 of the fourth month,
Wèi 魏 declared a general amnesty
and changed its reign title to Tàicháng 泰常.
8 The Xi Qín Xiāngwǔ Hóu Tán Dá 西秦襄武侯曇達 and others attacked Qín Qín Zhōu Cìshǐ Yáo Ài 秦秦州刺史姚艾 in Shàngguī 上邽,
defeated him,
and relocated over five thousand households of his people to Fāohǎn 枹罕.
9 In the fifth month, on the day Guǐsì 癸巳, Tàiwèi Liú Yù 太尉裕 was additionally appointed Intendant of Běiyōng Zhōu 北雍州.
Jìn 晉 first established Yōng Zhōu 雍州 in Cháng'ān 長安.
During the chaos of Yǒngjiā 永嘉,
it fell to Liú 劉 and Shí 石.
During the chaos of Fú Qín 苻秦,
refugees from Yōng Zhōu 雍州 moved south to Fán 樊 and Miǎn 沔.
Xiàowǔ 孝武 first established a temporary Yōng Zhōu 雍州 in Xiāngyáng 襄陽.
Now, Liú Yù 裕 wanted to capture Cháng'ān 長安,
hence he was appointed Intendant of Běiyōng Zhōu 北雍州,
to distinguish it from the Yōng Zhōu 雍州 in Xiāngyáng 襄陽.
Yōng 雍 is pronounced yú-yòng (於用翻);
the same below.
10 In the sixth month, on the day Dīngsì 丁巳, Wèi Zhǔ Sī 魏主嗣 made a northern tour.
11 Tens of thousands of households of Hú from Bìngzhōu rebelled against Qín,
entered Píngyáng,
and enthroned the Xiōngnú Cáohóng as Grand Chányú.
Hóng was a descendant of Yǐn, son of Cáogǔ, the Xiōngnú Right Worthy King,
who was known as the 'Eastern Cáo'.
单 (chán)
is pronounced 'chán'.
This was where the various Xiōngnú tribes had gathered to protect themselves,
and it was named after that.
Hóng was captured
and sent to Cháng'ān.
Fifteen thousand households of their powerful and wealthy members were relocated to Yōngzhōu.
The seat of Qín's Yōngzhōu commandery was Āndìng.
12 The Dī king Yáng Shèng attacked Qín's Qíshān,
captured it,
and advanced to threaten Qínzhōu.
Qín's Rear General Yáo Píng went to relieve it;
Shèng withdrew his troops,
and Píng, with Yáo Sōng, the defender of Shàngguī, pursued him.
Xià King Bóbó led 40,000 cavalry to attack Shàngguī.
Before he arrived,
Sōng fought Shèng at Zhúlǐng
and was defeated and killed.
The Commentary on the Water Classic says: The Jíshǔi flows past Dāngtíng Chuān,
then flows southeast,
joining the Zhúlǐngshuǐ.
The water flows out from Zhúlǐng in the southern mountains,
and enters the Jíshǔi from the northeast.
The Jíshǔi enters Shàngguī County from the northeast.
After twenty days,
he captured it,
killed Qínzhōu Inspector Yáo Jūndū and over five thousand officers and soldiers,
and then destroyed the city.
He then attacked Yīnmì.
Yīnmì
was the ancient state of the Mì people,
referred to in the Shī
as "the Mì people were disrespectful,
daring to resist the great state."
From the Hàn dynasty onwards, it was a county,
belonging to Āndìng Commandery.
The Kuòdì Zhì says: The old city of Yīnmì
is west of Qúnchóng County in Jīngzhōu,
its eastern part connected to the county seat,
which was the ancient Mì state.
He made his son Chāng the Inspector of Yōngzhōu,
stationed at Yīnmì.
Commander of the Northern Expedition Yáo Huī abandoned Āndìng
and fled back to Cháng'ān.
The people of Āndìng, led by Hú Yǎn and others, with fifty thousand households, occupied the city and surrendered to Xià.
Bóbó sent Zhengdōng General Yáng Gǒugēr with five thousand Xiānbēi to garrison Āndìng,
and advanced to attack Qín's Zhènxī General Yáo Chén at Yōngchéng.
Chén abandoned the garrison and fled to Cháng'ān.
Bóbó occupied Yōng
and advanced to plunder Méichéng.
Qín's Prince Dōngpíng Shào and General Zhēnglǔ Yǐn Zhāo and others led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack him.
Bóbó retreated towards Āndìng.
Hú Yǎn closed the gates and resisted him,
killed Yáng Gǒugēr and the Xiānbēi he led,
and again surrendered Āndìng to Qín.
Shào advanced and attacked Bóbó at Mǎ'ān Bǎn,
defeated him,
pursued him to Cháonà,
but could not catch him and returned.
Bóbó returned to Xìngchéng.
Yáng Shèng again sent his nephew Juàn to attack Qín,
reaching Chéncāng.
Qín's Liǎnmànwěi repelled him.
Xià King Bóbó again sent his nephew Tí to invade Xièyáng in the south.
Jìnshū Zàijì records it as
"Chíyáng,"
which should be followed.
Chíyáng County belonged to Fúfēng Commandery;
in the Táng dynasty, it was Jīngzhào Yúnyáng County.
复 (fù)
is pronounced 'fú yòu fān'.
13 Liáng's Sīmǎ Suǒ Chéngmíng submitted a memorial urging Duke Gǎo of Liáng to attack King Méngxùn of Hexī.

Guān,

Héběi County,

Xià,

27 In this year,
Wèi Wèi Jiāngjūn, Ānchéng Xiàoyuán Wáng Shú Sūn Jùn passed away.

saying to his wife, Lady Huán:
"If we shared glory in life,

When Sì ascended the throne,

Báijiànshān should be west of Huòzé County, Hédōng, in Hàn territory.

Huòzé

The Analects say: Zǐzhāng said:

“I will manage it myself for the general.

refers to Yù.

In summer,
the fourth month,

Wǔ,
pronounced like Ruan Gu.
He crossed to the north bank,

with both ends embracing river chariots,

At that time, Chāoshí separately carried over a thousand large hammers and lances.
He then cut the lances to three or four feet long,

each lance would pierce through three or four people.
The Wèi soldiers could not withstand this

Ābógān was beheaded on the battlefield.

Chāoshí, leading Níngshuò Jiāngjūn Hú Fān and Níngyuǎn Jiāngjūn Liú Róngzǔ, pursued and attacked them,

Wèi Zhǔ Sì heard of this

using the river as a defense,

He led his troops to attack Línzi,

Tàiwèi Yù arrived at Luòyáng,

8 On the day Dīngsì,
Wèi Zhǔ Sì went to Gāoliǔ;
on the day Rénxū,
he returned to Píngchéng.
9 Héxī Wáng Méngxùn granted a general amnesty.
He sent Zhāngyè Tàishǒu Jǔqú Guǎngzōng to feign surrender to lure Liáng Gōng Xīn.

The Xīn Tángshū Dìlǐzhì states:
Northwest of Gānzhōu Zhāngyè Jùn, one hundred ninety lǐ away, is Qílián Shān.
North of the mountain is Jiànkāng Jūn,
and one hundred twenty lǐ west of the military garrison is Liǎoquán Shǒuzhuō Chéng.
He withdrew his troops.
Méngxùn pursued them.
Xīn fought him at Jiězhī Jiàn.
“Jiězhī Jiàn”
is written as
“Xiānzhī Jiàn”

Seven thousand heads were cut off.
Méngxùn fortified Jiànkāng,

on the day Yǐwèi,

Sì asked him:

Sì said:

Chuí relied on the resources of his father and brothers

The people of the state flocked to him,

With a little reliance

Liú Yù rose from humble origins,
without a foot of land,
defeated Huán Xuán,
and restored the Jìn dynasty.
This account is found in Volume 113, Yuánxīng 3rd year.
This account is found in Volume 115, 5th and 6th years.

Xiāo,
qiáo yáo fān.

Sì said:

He replied:
"To the west there is Qū Gài,

humble and lowly.

Whenever an army moves,

Sì smiled and said:

Hào said:

Sì said:

Hào said:

He did not think of repaying their kindness and righteousness,

usurping a region.
This account is found in Volume 114, 3rd year.
Jiǎo,

7th month,

15 Grand Commandant Yù reached Ménxiāng.
Shěn Tiánzǐ and others were about to attack Yáoliǔ.
The Qín ruler Hóng wished to personally lead troops to resist Yù's army,
but feared Tiánzǐ and others would raid his rear.
He wanted to first attack and eliminate Tiánzǐ and others,
and then sally forth eastward with the entire state's forces.
So he led tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry

Tiánzǐ's original purpose was to be a feint;
he commanded barely over a thousand men.
Hearing of Hóng's arrival,

Fù Hóngzhī stopped him, citing the numerical disadvantage.
Tiánzǐ said:
"Warfare values surprise,
not necessarily numbers.
Furthermore, the numerical disparity is so great now,
that it's a do-or-die situation.
If they establish a solid encirclement,
then we will have no escape.
It is better to strike them while they have just arrived

By attacking first,

The Qín army formed several layers of encirclement.
Tiánzǐ comforted his officers and soldiers, saying:

The officers and soldiers all leapt up, shouted,
and fought with short weapons.
The Qín army was utterly defeated.
Shěn Tiánzǐ defeated Yáo Hóng's tens of thousands of troops with over a thousand men

They captured his imperial carriage and personal belongings.
The Qín ruler Hóng fled back to Bàshàng.
Initially,
Yù, considering Tiánzǐ and others had few men,

Qínlǐng is south of Cháng'ān.
Bān Gù's "Xīdū Fù" mentions

From here, one exits Lántiánguān.

Many counties in Guānzhōng secretly sent their allegiance to Tiánzǐ.
On the day of Xīnchǒu,
Grand Commandant Yù arrived at Tóngguān.

with Jīshí to its east

The river flows north past the west of Zhèngchéng.
There is a bridge over the water.
It is ten *lǐ* east of Zhèngchéng,
hence people named the river after the bridge.
The Sānfǔ Huángtú says: Luòmén
was the first gate on the eastern side of the northern wall of Cháng'ān city.
The Jīng River originates from Jiāntóushān in Jīngyáng County, Āndìng,

This section of the Jīng River was within the jurisdiction of Yánglíng, Jīngzhào in the Hàn dynasty.
They defeated him,
Qiáng died,
and Nán fled to Cháng'ān.
Prince of Dōngpíng, Zàn, retreated to garrison Zhèngchéng.
Grand Commandant Yù advanced his army to press him.
Hóng ordered Yáo Pī to guard Wèiqiáo,
Hú Yìdù to garrison Shíjī,
Prince of Dōngpíng, Zàn, to garrison Bàdōng,
and Hóng himself to garrison Xiāoyáoyuán.
